title: Lean toolchains now bundle independent kernel checkers; `lake check --paranoid` accepts only if all accept
summary: Since September 2026, Lean release toolchains bundle nanoda (PR #15099, merged 2026-09-10), lean4lean (#15048, 2026-09-10), leanchecker-paranoid, con-leche and con-ron. lake check/lake comparator --paranoid (#15145, 2026-09-14) runs leanchecker-paranoid, lean4lean, nanoda and con-leche over the export plus Lean's own kernel, and accepts only if every one accepts. Since #15762 (2026-10-19), unpermitted axioms are reported before the checkers run. In the Lean Kernel Arena (73 bad, 127 good tests, generated 2026-10-24), official, nanoda and lean4lean accept 0 bad proofs, while con-ron and con-leche each accept 3. The conjunction is therefore sound if any one checker is sound.
specifics: Measured: nanoda_bin 0.4.19 re-checked 59,400 declarations (all Init + toy) in 49.7 s / 362 MB. Running bundled lean4lean directly on .olean files printed 'incompatible header' for every module. Either I invoked it wrong (the intended path is lake check) or it is a packaging bug; unresolved. Whole-export nanoda config with unpermitted_axiom_hard_error=true rejects because Init declares sorryAx, so audit axioms per theorem (lake check does this).
overclaim_risk: Independent kernels share the export format and elaborated terms; the spec-to-code gap is untouched.
underclaim_risk: Kernel diversity costs under 1 min for a core-only project. It closes the 'tiny trusted kernel' single point of failure that the 2026 kernel bugs exposed.
tcb: any one of {Lean C++ kernel, nanoda (Rust), lean4lean (Lean), leanchecker-paranoid}

verify.note: #15145 merged 2026-09-14 verified; con-ron not seen on the PR page; lean4lean header error unresolved; conjunction not independent against shared-spec bugs (nanoda accepted #14807 exploit).

title: Lean kernel soundness bugs fixed in 2026 (is_prop stuck term, nested-inductive params), one also accepted by nanoda
summary: #14807 (merged 2026-08-18): the kernel's is_prop returned false on a stuck non-sort type, which broke the proof-irrelevance guard on projections. Daniel Selsam (OpenAI) reported it, found with internal models. nanoda also accepted the bogus proof; lean4lean did not. #14577 (2026-07-28): parametric args of nested inductives escaped type checking. #14498 (2026-07-22): opaque values not checked for fvars. AI-driven kernel fuzzing is finding real bugs, so a single kernel is not enough for a required gate.
overclaim_risk: Exploiting these needs deliberately crafted terms; honest proofs almost never hit them.
underclaim_risk: LLM-written proofs optimise to pass the checker. That is the adversary that finds these bugs, so the golden's gate must be multi-kernel.

verify.note: #14807 verified exactly (found with OpenAI internal models; nanoda also accepted); #14577/#14498 not rechecked.

title: native_decide and bv_decide add per-proof axioms that trust the Lean compiler; confirmed with #print axioms
summary: Lean/Meta/Native.lean (v4.35.0): proofs by native evaluation 'assert the result of that computation as an axiom'. ImplementedByAttr.lean: an incorrect @[implemented_by] 'makes it possible to prove False with native_decide'. Measured: a bv_decide proof depends on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, len_mask._native.bv_decide.ax_1_5]; the omega proof depends on no axioms. Golden rule: axiom allowlist {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}; no native_decide or bv_decide in assurance proofs; omega, decide or grind instead.
overclaim_risk: bv_decide's SAT certificate is LRAT-checked. The trust gap is the compiled checker plus the compiler, not CaDiCaL.
underclaim_risk: One stray native_decide silently widens the TCB to the whole compiler; nanoda and lake check catch it only if the allowlist is enforced.

verify.note: Long-standing documented mechanism; allowlist propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound standard.

title: Obligation class -> minimal tool map, with where Lean is required vs where another tool fits better
summary: The smallest toolchain that discharges each obligation, using no prover LLMs. Lean core (no Mathlib) carries every spec/model obligation: attenuation, policy semantics, canonical grammar, the budget model and the effect mediator, all tied to Rust by differential testing. Kani covers unsafe glue and arithmetic in Rust, TLA+/TLC covers liveness and cross-request interleavings, and EverParse or Vest covers binary framings.
specifics:
1 PARSER CANONICALITY. Binary framings (H2 frame header, QUIC varint/frames, PROXY v2, CBOR tokens): EverParse 3D/CDDL, proof-free generated (CI-only, 973 MB), or Vest/Verus (3.2 GB). HTTP/1.1 text grammar: LEAN REQUIRED as spec. Write a canonical-grammar model in Lean core and prove (a) unambiguity (at most one parse), (b) parse(serialize(m)) = m and serialize(parse(b)) = canon(b), (c) rejection of the desync classes (CL+TE, obs-fold, bare LF). Rust impl tied by DRT plus fuzz; Lean Std.Http (13.5 K lines, unproven framing) is a second oracle. Verus impl proof is optional.
2 BUDGET INVARIANTS (per-request bytes/streams/time/host-calls): Lean core model with omega (measured 0.24 s). Kani harnesses for Rust counter arithmetic and saturating ops (small, bounded, under 1 GB). TLA+/TLC for global/cross-request budgets under concurrency.
3 ATTENUATION MONOTONICITY / NO AMBIENT AUTHORITY: LEAN REQUIRED (best fit). rights(attenuate(c, r)) is a subset of rights(c); chain closure; delegation never amplifies. Cedar precedent: Batteries only, 3.4:1 proof:model.
4 POLICY SEMANTICS: LEAN, with a tri-state evaluator Allow | Deny | Error and the theorem Error => Deny (fail-closed). Motivated by Envoy CVE-2026-73552, where an RBAC regex error collapsed into no-match and failed open. DRT against the Rust evaluator. cvc5/z3 only through SymCC-style analysis if policy diffing is needed.
5 UNSAFE GLUE (FFI to aws-lc-rs, io_uring/epoll shims, arena allocator): KANI (bounded UB/panic freedom), pinned >= #4910, serial or instruction-budgeted. Miri in tests. #![forbid(unsafe_code)] elsewhere. Lean is NOT applicable.
6 LIVENESS (graceful drain completes, WAL eventually commits or aborts, no starvation under fair scheduling): TLA+/TLC with fairness at design time (4.5 MB). Apalache for larger parameters. Verus/Anvil-style impl liveness only if the controller is complex. Lean is a poor fit (no model checker).
7 FAILED REQUEST => NO MUTATION: Lean model of the host effect mediator (staged effects, commit iff ok; measured toy). TLA+ for crash interleavings. DST for the implementation.
8 AUDIT COMPLETENESS: Lean model that every committed effect has a preceding audit record (same mediator). Implementation by construction (single choke point), plus a test that diffs the audit log against effects.
Gate rules: Lean axiom allowlist {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}; lake check --paranoid; Kani nonzero CBMC exit => FAIL; 6 GB cap per proof job.
overclaim_risk: Lean model proofs prove models, not Rust. The tie is DRT, which Cedar showed misses some bugs (validator non-termination).
underclaim_risk: Every obligation class except unsafe glue and liveness can be carried by core Lean, so Lean-in-the-story costs about 1 GB, not 10 GB.

verify.note: Design judgement; Lean-required for attenuation overclaimed (Verus/Kani bounded could discharge); Std.Http as oracle unverified.

title: Out-of-process extension boundaries still break the host: Envoy ext_proc/ext_authz CVEs 2024-2026
summary: CVE-2026-47207 (GHSA-68cv-hq5f-g6xv, 2026-06-23): an ext_proc server packing two unexpected ProcessingResponses into one gRPC message causes a UAF in Envoy, affecting all supported versions. CVE-2024-23324: ext_authz bypassed via PROXY-protocol invalid UTF-8 when failure_mode_allow=true. CVE-2026-47205 ext_authz UAF on teardown; CVE-2026-50572 ext_authz segfault; CVE-2025-30157 ext_proc local-reply crash; CVE-2026-73552 RBAC fail-open on obs-text. Lesson: the HOST's parser and state machine for module responses is part of the TCB. Out-of-process placement keeps module memory away from the host but does not protect host invariants against hostile responses.
overclaim_risk: These are C++ memory bugs; a Rust host removes the UAF class but not the protocol-state or fail-open classes.
underclaim_risk: Protocol-state bugs from malformed module responses carry over to any extension protocol.

verify.note: CVE-2026-47207 verified (malicious ext_proc server -> UAF/DoS, Envoy 1.34-<1.39, patched 1.35.13/1.36.9/1.37.5/1.38.3); other CVE ids (incl. 73552) not verified.

title: Proxy-Wasm ABI v0.2.1 is not capability-safe by spec: limits are SHOULD, plugins can switch effective context, and plugins share global KV and queues
summary: The spec says hosts 'should' enforce memory/CPU limits and 'should' keep per-plugin external-resource lists. proxy_set_effective_context lets a plugin act on other connections or requests, and hosts only 'might limit' this. proxy_set_shared_data, proxy_get_shared_data and the shared queues are cross-plugin global state. After a crash the host recreates the VM, rate-limited. An extension contract copied from Proxy-Wasm would let a malicious module break tenant isolation and no-ambient-authority unless the host removes these functions.
overclaim_risk: Real hosts (Envoy) may restrict some of this in configuration.
underclaim_risk: This is the de facto plugin ABI for Envoy, Istio, APISIX and others, and copying it would import the weaknesses.

verify.note: SHOULD limits and effective-context switching verified; global KV/queues is inference; hosts may restrict.

title: wasmtime-wasi 50.0.0 WasiCtxBuilder::new() grants no env, args, preopens or DNS, but does grant clocks and RNG; Component Model goal is capability-safe, shared-nothing
summary: docs.rs wasmtime-wasi 50.0.0 says the defaults are: stdin closed, stdout/err discarded, no env, no args, no preopens, sockets with all addresses denied, ip-name-lookup denied, host wall and monotonic clocks, and RNG. The page also contradicts itself on whether allow_tcp/allow_udp are on by default. Component Model Goals.md: 'capability-safe ... interfaces', fine-grained sandboxing, shared-nothing linking. Ambient authority is therefore decided by the embedder's linker. The golden must ship a linker allowlist and a static import check.
underclaim_risk: The default clock grant is a timing-channel input for Spectre-class attacks. Coarsen it or virtualize it for untrusted modules.

verify.note: v50.0.0 confirmed; docs inconsistent on default TCP/UDP policy; clocks give timing side channel.

title: Golden extension contract: which core invariants SURVIVE an arbitrary malicious sandboxed/out-of-process module vs ASSUME golden modules
summary: Each invariant is classified with its architectural reason. The rule underneath: an invariant survives only if it is enforced at a host choke point that the module cannot bypass and the host code at that point is in the verified TCB. Everything that depends on module semantics or on non-transactional external side effects assumes golden modules.
specifics:
I1 NO AMBIENT AUTHORITY: SURVIVES. Module gets only host-minted, unforgeable handles (component resources, or capability tokens over IPC). Linker allowlist plus static import check (no shared-KV, no effective-context switch, no raw sockets/fs). Out-of-process: seccomp+Landlock, no netns egress. Residual TCB: runtime escapes (wasmtime 57 GHSAs in 2026, Cranelift criticals Oct 2026), kernel.
I2 BOUNDED RESOURCES PER REQUEST: SURVIVES if enforced by the host, never by module cooperation. Epoch/deadline interruption (not fuel; fuel had bypass CVEs), ResourceLimiter memory caps, per-request host-call and I/O-byte quotas (USENIX'25 WASI I/O amplification shows CPU metering is not enough), cgroup v2 for out-of-process. Proof: Lean budget model plus Kani on host counters.
I3 FAILED REQUEST => NO MUTATION: SURVIVES only for effects routed through the host transactional effect API, where the module stages writes and the host commits iff the request succeeds. ASSUMES GOLDEN for any module or adapter with direct external side effects (third-party DB adapters, outbound HTTP, email/payments), because these cannot be rolled back. At best they are idempotency-keyed (outbox pattern), which the golden's adapters implement and forks may not.
I4 TENANT ISOLATION: data-plane SURVIVES with instance-per-tenant(-request), host-keyed storage namespaces and no cross-instance shared state. Side channels: in-process Wasm does NOT survive (Swivel/Spectre), so a hostile multi-tenant deployment needs process-per-tenant plus coarsened clocks. Classified SURVIVES (logical) / ASSUMES (microarchitectural, unless process-isolated).
I5 PARSER CANONICALITY / NO DESYNC: SURVIVES if the host core parses and canonicalizes before any module sees the request, modules receive structured values, and the host re-serializes everything a module emits. Modules never write raw bytes to the client or upstream. The host's decoder of module responses is in the verified TCB (CVE-2026-47207 pattern). ASSUMES GOLDEN if a module is given raw stream access (Proxy-Wasm TCP callbacks).
I6 AUDIT COMPLETENESS: SURVIVES for host-mediated effects: every capability invocation is logged by the host before it executes, in a tamper-evident chain. Does NOT survive for module-internal intent, covert channels, or module-authored log contents (ASSUMES GOLDEN).
I7 FAIL-CLOSED AUTHZ (extra): SURVIVES if a module decision is one input to a host tri-state combiner where Error, timeout or crash => Deny. A failure_mode_allow-style config is forbidden in the golden (CVE-2024-23324).
I8 AVAILABILITY UNDER MODULE CRASH: PARTIAL. A crash is contained per instance, and crash-loop rate-limiting returns errors (Proxy-Wasm spec pattern). The module's own function is lost.
overclaim_risk: SURVIVES assumes the host TCB (runtime, kernel, mediator) is correct; runtime CVEs make this probabilistic.
underclaim_risk: Four of six core invariants survive arbitrary modules by construction. That is the responsibility boundary the operator asked for.

title: Conformance suite third parties can run: static import check, behavioral contract, adversarial-module corpus against the host, and DRT against Lean reference models
summary: Modeled on the wasi-testsuite adapter layout (Apache-2.0, active 2026-10-23), CNCF k8s-conformance self-certification by PR, Cedar DRT, and duvet requirement traceability.
specifics:
Package: aegis-conformance (Apache-2.0), versioned with the WIT world golden:module@1.
C0 STATIC (module): component imports subset of the allowlist (wasm-tools component wit); no core-wasm imports outside the canonical ABI; size and declared-limits manifest present.
C1 BEHAVIORAL (module): handler totality under budget; deterministic output for declared-pure handlers on replay; error mapping to the contract's error enum; idempotency-key honoured for effectful adapters (re-run => no second effect).
C2 ADVERSARIAL (host; for forks of the host): a corpus of hostile modules must leave invariants I1-I7 intact. Includes infinite loop, memory bomb, I/O amplification (fsync/urandom), forged/stale handle ids, use-after-drop handles, attempted effective-context switch, double or late responses (ext_proc CVE-2026-47207 pattern), oversized or non-canonical header output, invalid UTF-8/obs-text in decisions (CVE-2026-73552), crash loops, and partial commits followed by trap. Oracle: host invariant monitors plus audit-vs-effect diff.
C3 DIFFERENTIAL (adapters/parsers/policy): DRT against the Lean reference models (policy evaluator, canonical HTTP grammar, budget model) compiled from Lean; N=1e6 cases per release; plus h2spec/h3spec/BoGo where relevant.
C4 TRACEABILITY: duvet annotations from contract MUST-clauses to tests; coverage report.
Output: signed JSON report (suite version, module digest, pass/fail per clause). Self-certification by PR to a public registry, k8s-conformance style. Acceptance: C0-C2 100% pass to claim 'golden-contract conformant'; C3 for adapters claiming fail-closed or canonical guarantees.
overclaim_risk: A conformance suite shows behavior on a corpus, not a proof. Forks may pass and still be unsound.
underclaim_risk: C2 runs against the host, so it detects forks that broke the surviving invariants. That is the property the responsibility boundary needs.

title: Admission control under agent swarms is an economics + queueing problem, not an identity problem
summary: 2025-26 practitioner evidence (SourceHut, KDE, GNOME, Codeberg, small VPS posts) shows floods arrive as tens of thousands of IPs doing ~1 request each against expensive deep endpoints. Per-IP limits and UA blocks fail; what held was (a) making expensive endpoints cheap or cached, (b) a global load-keyed shed/challenge ladder, (c) identity-bound budgets for identified agents. Defence must be judged by attacker-cost-per-admitted-request vs defender-cost-per-request and by human collateral, neither of which most vendors publish.
overclaim_risk: Incident posts are self-reported, few have request-level data; generalising 'per-IP limits fail' from git-forge workloads (expensive blame/log pages) to all middle-tier apps.
underclaim_risk: Treating the lack of rigorous measurements as 'no signal': multiple independent operators report the same pattern (many IPs, ~1 req each, random UAs).

verify.note: Sources verified but self-reported forge anecdotes; ladder is synthesis; Forgejo swap shows making endpoints cheap works.

title: Dated AI-crawler flood incident ledger 2025-03..2026-07
summary: SourceHut (DeVault, ~2025-03-17): tens of thousands of IPs, random UAs, ~1 req/IP, hits git blame/log/every commit; weeks of delayed work, outages. KDE GitLab 2025-03-19: Alibaba-range IPs claiming MS Edge. GNOME GitLab: problem since ~2024-11; Anubis deployed ~2025-03-13; Piotrowski measured 81,000 requests in ~2.5h of which only 3% passed PoW (~97% bots). Diaspora (Schubert): ~70% of requests from AI companies (OpenAI agent ~25%, Amazon ~15%, Anthropic ~4.3%). Read the Docs: blocking AI crawlers cut traffic 800->200 GB/day (-75%, ~$1,500/mo). Fedora pagure: subnet blocks then whole-country (Brazil) ban. Codeberg 2025-08-15: bots solving Anubis; July 2026 status notes unauthenticated spikes. Household-scale 2026-07 (rdnlsmith): cgit->Forgejo dropped CPU 100%->10% but bandwidth rose to 13 Mbps; Anubis denied 1.10M requests in first 24h (778k AI-training rule, 256k AI catch-all); author cannot tell if Anubis or crawler pause ended the spike; raising somaxconn/netdev_max_backlog did nothing.

underclaim_risk: Single-site anecdotes are not generalisable but the shape (distributed, low per-IP rate) recurs in 5+ independent reports.

title: Anubis (TecharoHQ) PoW/weighing reverse-proxy gate
summary: Go, MIT, first release 2025-01-19; v1.28.2 on 2026-10-23, v1.28.1 2026-10-09; repo active. Adopters per Wikipedia: GNOME GitLab, LKML archives, sourceware, FFmpeg, Wine, Wikimedia, UNESCO, OpenWRT, FreeCAD. Current default botPolicies.yaml is a WEIGH ladder: weight<=0 allow; 0-10 metarefresh d1; 10-20 fast d2; 20-30 fast d4; >=30 fast d6; +10 for BR/CN and +10 for generic 'Mozilla|Opera' UA; CHALLENGE/DENY return HTTP 200; state store=memory by default; DNSBL off after backlash (#184). v1.28.2 adds rejection of empty User-Agent. Challenge is bound to a cookie, so cost is per session, not per request.
overclaim_risk: Adopter list is from Wikipedia (one entry marked citation-needed); no public per-deployment block rate beyond a few posts.
underclaim_risk: Dismissing it as bypassed ignores that it is now a weighted multi-signal policy engine, not just PoW; the PoW is the weakest layer.

verify.note: v1.28.2 (2026-10-23) and ladder thresholds verified; BR/CN +10 needs commented-out GeoIP config; HTTP 200/memory-store claims not re-verified.

title: Negative results: PoW gates are bypassed by real browsers and native solvers
summary: Issue #978 (2025-08-15, closed 2025-08-20): Huawei Cloud scrapers 'installed headless chrome and simply computed the proof of work'; maintainer: 'not a bug', fix = block Huawei Cloud in default config (PR #1004). Issue #765 (2025-07-06, still open): Marginalia saw sustained high-volume traffic punching through; maintainer collecting JA4 TLS fingerprints, 'cat and mouse'. Ormandy (~Aug 2025): default d=4 hex zeros = 2^16 SHA-256 ops; his C miner solved in 0.017s on a GCE e2-micro (~2.3M hash/s); all 11,508 GitHub-star sites ~ 6 min compute; monthly cost <1 cent until several million sites deploy. Zakaria released a CLI solver 2026-07-09. Codeberg praised months of protection before bots adapted. Net: PoW filters only non-JS low-effort bots; against headless Chrome or native solvers it is cost ~0 for the attacker and non-zero for humans.
overclaim_risk: Ormandy's page is undated and benchmarks a single micro-VM; the 'Codeberg bots learned to solve' claim has never been disclosed in detail (could be headless Chrome rather than a solver); #765 has no confirmed method.
underclaim_risk: Saying 'PoW still helps' without numbers: the GNOME 97% and rdnlsmith 1.1M denied are real but are mostly non-JS bots, which cheap rules (UA/ASN/JA4) also catch.

verify.note: #978 (maintainer: headless Chrome computed PoW) and Ormandy numbers confirmed; 11,508 is GitHub stars as proxy; Ormandy also found a double-spend bug.

title: Derived PoW economics: attacker cost per session vs human cost
summary: Derived (not measured by us): d=4 hex => 2^16=65,536 expected hashes; at ~2.3M hash/s native single core that is ~28 ms of CPU, ~1e-7 USD at cloud vCPU prices; d=6 => 2^24 ~ 16.7M hashes ~ 7 s native. Challenge cookie reuse (valid up to ~a week per Ormandy) amortises the cost over thousands of requests => per-request attacker cost ~0. Human side: GNOME saw ~1 min (desktop) and ~2 min (phone) waits during a link-spike. Conclusion: PoW difficulty that a phone tolerates (<~2 s) is irrelevant to a native-solver attacker; PoW is only a load-keyed speed bump and must be paired with per-session cost budgets and cheap-reject paths.
overclaim_risk: Hash rate taken from Ormandy's e2-micro; JS-in-browser rate unmeasured here; attacker actually pays for residential proxy egress (not CPU) which dominates.
underclaim_risk: Ignoring that PoW also forces attackers to run JS/WASM, raising per-request engineering cost and memory; unquantified.

verify.note: Derived; d6 ~8 s; human tail from single report.

title: Per-IP token buckets are structurally ineffective against low-rate distributed swarms

Keyed limiter state grows O(N) so a 100k-IP swarm also pressures memory. Effective controls are aggregate: global concurrency/queue-delay limit, cost-weighted class budgets, and path-cost reduction (cache, static rendering, 'cheap reject'). Derived from first principles plus the incident reports; no controlled experiment found.
overclaim_risk: Generalises from forge workloads; per-IP limits still stop single-origin floods and are needed.
underclaim_risk: Skipping per-prefix limits entirely would let one host exhaust shared capacity.

title: Adaptive concurrency limits: Netflix concurrency-limits and Envoy gradient controller
summary: Netflix/concurrency-limits (Apache-2.0, 3,623 stars, last push 2026-10-21, not archived): Vegas (queue estimate L*(1-minRTT/sampleRTT), +1 if < alpha (2-3), -1 if > beta (4-6)), Gradient2 (long vs short EWMA divergence, aggressive decrease), AIMDLimit (loss-based, recommended for client side). Partitioning: Simple gauge vs Percentage guarantee (gRPC example live 0.9 / batch 0.1; servlet partition by principal). README has NO measured results or benchmarks. Envoy adaptive_concurrency (experimental): gradient=(minRTT+B)/sampleRTT, new_limit=gradient*old_limit+headroom with headroom=sqrt(limit) fixed; minRTT recalculated by pinning concurrency to 3 by default; doc example: p90 sampling, 100 ms update, min limit 25, minRTT window 60 s, jitter 10%, 50 requests. No independent measured comparison of Gradient2 vs Vegas vs AIMD under adversarial load found.
overclaim_risk: Delay-based controllers assume latency rises with load; a swarm of cheap cached hits and a few expensive ones can confuse minRTT, and the minRTT probe window is itself an attack surface (attacker times load during probe).
underclaim_risk: No measured results is a documentation gap, not evidence the algorithms fail; they are widely used.

verify.note: Envoy formula verified; no experimental marker seen; minRTT probing raises 503s and is adversarially manipulable.

title: CoDel (RFC 8289) and adaptive LIFO as request-queue shedding
summary: RFC 8289 (Jan 2018, Experimental): TARGET 5 ms, INTERVAL 100 ms; next drop time t + INTERVAL/sqrt(count). Facebook's 'Fail at Scale' (ACM Queue 2015) applies controlled delay to request queues with adaptive LIFO (serve newest when queue is standing) -- primary page not retrievable here (HTTP 403) so parameters beyond RFC are not verified. LIFO under overload sacrifices fairness to serve requests whose clients are still waiting; pair with per-class queues so humans are not LIFO-starved by agents.
overclaim_risk: RFC targets packet queues; sojourn-time thresholds for HTTP requests (5 ms) are far tighter than app-level service times: needs scaling to handler p50.
underclaim_risk: Skipping queue-delay signal and using only CPU% is the common mistake; sojourn time is the cheapest overload signal.

verify.note: RFC 8289 primary; transfer to request queues untested; FB adaptive LIFO source unreachable.

title: Cost-weighted budgets: GitHub GraphQL points as the worked public example
summary: GitHub GraphQL: primary 5,000 points/hour per user; cost = (sum of requested connection node counts)/100, minimum 1; secondary limits: 100 concurrent requests, 2,000 points/min (GraphQL) / 900 (REST), 90 s CPU per 60 s real time (<=60 s GraphQL). Pattern: static pre-computed cost up front, plus a separate runtime CPU-seconds budget; two independent dimensions. For our server the analogue is a route-declared cost class, a runtime debit of measured CPU/DB time or Wasm fuel, and refunds on cache hit.
overclaim_risk: GitHub's limits may change; mapping to Wasm fuel units is an untested design.
underclaim_risk: Cost-based limiting is the only measured-in-production approach found that bounds expensive-endpoint abuse regardless of IP count.

title: Identified agents (Web Bot Auth) as a separate admission class with accountable budgets
summary: Verified-bot signatures (RFC 9421 + WBA draft) give a stable key id, enabling per-identity budgets and honest 429/Retry-After feedback, and the Cloudflare 'trust band' ties standing to robots.txt and HTTP 429 compliance. This converts abuse control from 'guess intent' to 'meter an identity', but only for cooperating agents; anonymous residential swarms stay in the anonymous class. Design implication: signature verification must happen after cheap pre-auth limits (verify cost is attacker-triggerable) and identified agents must get guaranteed capacity share so they are not collateral in a shed.

title: L5: admission-control pipeline order and default parameters for a 1 vCPU / 1-2 GB box
summary: Order is by ascending cost-to-reject; every stage must reject in O(1) memory-bounded work before the next, costlier stage. S0 listener: max 2,048 open conns; per-/32 (v4) or per-/64 (v6) conn cap 32; header-read deadline 10 s and min body rate 1 KiB/s; TLS handshakes behind a semaphore of 8. S1 pre-auth anonymous GCRA (governor 0.10.4 keyed by /32 or /64, bounded key store 65,536 entries with LRU eviction; on overflow degrade to a global anonymous bucket): 5 req/s sustained, burst 20, cost-weighted; plus a /24-/48 aggregate bucket 50 req/s burst 200. S2 identity classes: (a) Web Bot Auth-verified key id (verify only after S1 passes), (b) session-cookie humans who passed a challenge, (c) Privacy Pass redeemed (type 2 blind RSA) if an issuer is configured, (d) anonymous. S3 cost class from route table: static/cached=1, dynamic read=5, DB write/search=20, pathological (blame/log/export) =100 units; per-identity GCRA over units: anonymous 60 units/min burst 120; session 600/min burst 1,200; verified agent 1,200/min default (operator-raised by contract). S4 load-keyed challenge ladder (only active when S5 queue sojourn > 5 ms for 100 ms or concurrency at limit): weight-based like Anubis thresholds (metarefresh -> PoW d4 -> d6) applied to class (d) only, with an accessible alternative path (see invariant). S5 concurrency admission: Gradient2/Vegas-style adaptive limit start 16, min 4, max 64 (1 vCPU async; start low because CPU-bound), Percentage partition: verified 0.30, session 0.50, anonymous 0.20 floor with work-conserving borrow; queue per class max 32 entries; CoDel target 5 ms / interval 100 ms scaled to 2x handler p50, adaptive LIFO only inside the anonymous queue. S6 handler under hard CPU deadline (Wasm fuel / 250 ms wall) and DB statement_timeout 2 s; actual cost debited post hoc to the S3 bucket (negative balance allowed, GCRA TAT advances). Shed responses: per-identity -> 429 + Retry-After computed from TAT; global shed -> 503 + Retry-After 1-5 s jittered; never HTTP 200 for rejects (Anubis returns 200 for CHALLENGE/DENY, which breaks monitoring and caches). Parameter values are engineering proposals (grade E) to be calibrated by the swarm test, not measurements.
overclaim_risk: Defaults are not benchmarked; 1 vCPU numbers (2,048 conns, concurrency 16) are reasoning, not measurement.
underclaim_risk: Not specifying numbers would leave implementers to copy Anubis/nginx defaults tuned for other cost profiles.

title: L5: per-tenant / per-identity budget invariants (spec-ready, TLA+/Verus-able)
summary: Let identity i have rate r_i (units/s), burst b_i, GCRA state TAT_i. I1 (conformance): for every identity i and every interval [t,t+W], sum of admitted cost units c <= b_i + r_i*W. I2 (isolation): admission of identity j never changes TAT_i for i != j (no shared mutable bucket across identities except the declared aggregate bucket). I3 (capacity partition): for class k with guaranteed share s_k of concurrency limit L, if class k offers load <= s_k*L, then in steady state its admission probability is 1 regardless of offered load in other classes (work-conserving borrow is revocable within one controller interval 100 ms). I4 (bounded state): memory of the limiter store <= M bytes constant; on eviction the evicted key is treated as a fresh key with burst b_anon (never granted more than anonymous burst), so eviction cannot be used to mint verified budget. I5 (non-negative debit semantic): post-hoc debit may drive balance negative but TAT is monotonically non-decreasing and bounded by now + D_max (D_max = 10 min) to avoid unbounded penalty. I6 (human-liveness): for any anonymous client that is not rate-exceeding at S1/S3 and completes either the PoW OR the non-JS/accessible alternative (rate-limited manual token, Privacy Pass redemption, or operator-issued session link), the system admits at least 1 request/10 s even at global overload (reserved human lane of 5% of L). I7 (no-fail-open): any error in a limiter/verifier stage results in reject (429/503), never admit-unmetered. Proof obligations: I1/I2/I5 are GCRA algebra (small, Verus/Kani-tractable); I3/I4 need a model of the controller (TLA+ with bounded clients); I6 is a liveness property needing fairness assumptions.
overclaim_risk: I3 and I6 depend on the adaptive controller converging; cannot be proven for the real feedback loop, only for a model.
underclaim_risk: I1/I2/I4/I5/I7 are directly checkable by property tests with no controller in the loop.

title: L5: synthetic agent-swarm simulation test spec with success criteria
summary: Deterministic harness (turmoil/madsim-style virtual time; one seed -> one trace; CI gate on fixed seed set + nightly random seeds) driving the real admission pipeline against a modelled 1 vCPU backend (service time per cost class: 0.2/1/4/30 ms for units 1/5/20/100, queue model, memory cap). Actor mixes: H humans (200, 0.2 req/s, session cookies, 10% behind CG-NAT sharing 20 IPs, 5% screen-reader/no-JS using accessible path); V verified agents (10, WBA key ids, 5 req/s each, honour Retry-After); R residential swarm (50,000 distinct IPs, each 1 req per 30 s = 1,667 req/s aggregate, random deep paths cost 100, random UAs) -- reproduces SourceHut pattern; B headless-browser swarm that solves PoW (1,000 IPs, 3 req/s each, valid cookies); N native-solver swarm (fresh session per 20 requests, 28 ms solve at d4); G greedy identified agent that ignores 429 (10x its budget); K key-churn attacker (new anonymous keys to evict limiter state, 1M distinct /64s). Success criteria (proposals, E-grade, tune on first run): (1) human request success >= 99% and p99 latency <= 2x unloaded for non-NAT humans, >= 95% for CG-NAT humans, and 100% of accessible-path humans complete within 60 s; (2) verified agents within budget get >= 99% admission and their p99 unaffected by R/B/N (I3); (3) aggregate backend CPU utilisation <= 85% and queue sojourn p99 <= 100 ms under swarm of >= 20x capacity; (4) attacker admitted cost units/s <= anonymous class share (20% of capacity) summed over all swarms; (5) G is capped at <= 1.05x its budget over any 60 s window (I1) and receives 429 with correct Retry-After; (6) K cannot raise limiter memory above M or mint more than b_anon burst (I4); (7) report attacker-cost-per-admitted-unit (CPU-s plus proxy cost model) and defender-cost-per-rejected-request (CPU us); defender reject path <= 20 us p99 for S0/S1 rejects, <= 1 ms for challenge issuance; (8) no-fail-open: fault-inject panics/timeouts in each stage, assert zero unmetered admits (I7); (9) report PoW-solved fraction separately: if B or N reach >50% of anonymous admits the PoW layer is declared ineffective and the budget layer must carry the load alone. Also run a replay of the rdnlsmith shape (dozens of req/s, many IPs, deep paths) and the GNOME shape (81,000 requests/2.5 h with 3% PoW-pass).
overclaim_risk: The simulator models service times; real CPU/cache behaviour differs, so sim passes are necessary not sufficient; follow with a real-hardware load test (BENCH_PLAN).
underclaim_risk: Without the swarm shapes taken from real incidents (many IPs x ~1 req) typical load tests (few IPs high rate) would pass a useless limiter.

title: Evidence that bounded model checking of stateful buffers runs out of memory
summary: s2n-quic buffer/deque/tests.rs:160: 'even with the minimal amount of parameter bounds, this proof's memory consumption explodes', so it is gated behind cfg(kani_slow) and not run in CI. title: No formally verified HPACK/QPACK or HTTP/2 frame decoder exists in Rust or C (Oct 2026), and the verified parser generators cannot express the dynamic table
summary: Searches across Coq, Isabelle, F*, SPARK, Lean, Verus and Dafny found no verified HPACK/QPACK implementation. Vest (USENIX Sec'25; crates vest 0.1.4 / vest_lib) covers stateless formats: TLS 1.3 handshake, Bitcoin, Wasm. Its paper says 'Vest does not have a concept of a stack counter', so Wasm needed a preprocessor. EverParse/3D (Hyper-V vSwitch) proves only non-malleability plus double-fetch freedom, again for stateless formats. everquic (S&P'21) verified the QUIC record layer (draft-30, F*/Low*, about 2 GB/s), not frames or QPACK.
specifics: The HPACK/QPACK dynamic table is cross-frame state, so it falls outside the stateless parser-generator model. A verified frame-header layer (9-byte H2 frame header, QUIC varints and frame types) is feasible with Vest. The table and the budget accounting need hand-written Verus or Kani proofs.
overclaim_risk: Absence of evidence from web search; an unpublished or academic artifact could exist.
underclaim_risk: A Vest-based HTTP/2 frame-header parser is roughly a weeks-scale artifact and would remove one parser class from the TCB.

verify.note: Absence claim corroborated by verifier search; Narcissus/Leapfrog adjacent.

title: h2 0.4.20 / hyper 1.12.0 budget mechanics as written (exact constants and gaps)
summary: h2 proto/mod.rs:33-47: REMOTE_RESET_STREAM_MAX 20, LOCAL_RESET_COUNT_MAX 1024 (connection lifetime), RESET_STREAM_MAX 50 kept for 1 s, DATA_FRAME_BUDGET 25,600 (256 B overhead x 100), MAX_RECV_EMPTY_DATA_FRAMES 100, MAX_SEND_BUFFER 400 KiB. framed_read.rs:22: crate default MHLS 16 MiB. The CONTINUATION cap is max(5, 1.25*MHLS/max_frame) (framed_read.rs:106-113). An oversize block keeps decoding until 4x MHLS (headers.rs:17, 873-889) and then sends GOAWAY COMPRESSION_ERROR. hpack decoded size = 32+name+value (header.rs:38-40). h2 server Builder sets max_concurrent_streams to unlimited by default. hyper 1.12.0 (proto/h2/server.rs:36-80) defaults: max_concurrent_streams 200, MHLS 16 KiB, windows 1 MiB, max_frame 16 KiB, keep_alive_timeout 20 s, interval None.
specifics: GAPS (grep-verified): (1) no header field-COUNT cap in h2 or hyper's H2 path (hyper h1 has max_headers 100); (2) no stall/idle/send-progress timeout anywhere in h2/src or hyper/src/proto/h2 (grep stall|idle_timeout|send_timeout = 0 hits); (3) counts.rs has a pure Budget{spent,max} with checked_add (lines 1-40) and Counts::inc_* guarded by assert!, so a logic slip is a panic, which is a DoS; (4) hyper spawns each accepted stream with exec.execute_h2stream (server.rs:316), and the handler is dropped only when poll_reset fires while the service is Pending (server.rs:452-458). Fix history: #909 (2026-06-09, try_append; >24,576 unique headers panicked HeaderMap, v0.4.15), #915 (2026-06-13, 4x MHLS close), #935 (2026-08-17 small-DATA budget, GHSA-q83h), #858 (2025-08-06 expiring reset limits, MadeYouReset).
overclaim_risk: Line numbers are from the shallow clones (h2 e64c166, hyper b073378) and may drift.
underclaim_risk: h2 already enforces implicit field-count via RFC-unit MHLS (each field >= 33 B), which is a provable bound once MHLS is small.

verify.note: Pinned to 0.4.20; post-0.4.20 releases unchecked; h3 PR #377 shows class still active.

title: Per-field memory is 3-7x the RFC 32-byte accounting: the root of HTTP/2 Bomb and Header Accordions
summary: RFC 7541 4.1 counts each field as 32+|name|+|value|. Measured server allocations per field: nginx 59 B (ngx_table_elt_t 56+2+1), and Calif reports about 70 to 4,000 B per entry across servers. In the Rust stack (http 1.4.0 map.rs:305), Bucket{hash u16, HeaderName 32 B, HeaderValue 40 B, Option<Links> 24 B} is about 104 B, plus a 4 B Pos index, plus Vec doubling slack (up to 2x). Repeated names go to ExtraValue at about 72 B. HeaderMap MAX_SIZE is 1<<15 = 32,768. Analytic estimate: 104-224 B per 1-byte field against an accounted 33-34 B.
specifics: Bound derivation for hyper defaults: fields per block <= floor(16384/33) = 496. Memory per block <= 496 x 224 + 16384 = about 127 KB. Times 200 streams = about 25 MB per connection pinned under a zero window. With raw h2 defaults (MHLS 16 MiB, unlimited streams) per-connection memory has no bound. The measurement spike was refused by heavy.sh (9 GB free < 10 GB), so this is an implementation-phase spike: a counting global allocator over HeaderMap with N in {496, 1k, 4k, 16k}, same-name and distinct-name cases.
overclaim_risk: The Rust numbers are analytic layout estimates, not measured. Allocator size classes could add 10-30%.
underclaim_risk: Even the pessimistic Rust figure is far below Envoy and httpd amplification, so hyper with a small MHLS is structurally safer than the incumbents.

verify.note: Analytic only.

title: Regression corpus identifiers: Rapid Reset, CONTINUATION, MadeYouReset, HTTP/2 Bomb, Header Accordions
summary: Rapid Reset CVE-2023-44487 (2023-10-10). CONTINUATION flood CERT VU#421644 (2024-04-03): CVE-2023-45288 Go (CPU), CVE-2024-27316 httpd, CVE-2024-28182 nghttp2, CVE-2024-30255 Envoy (about 1 core per 300 Mbit/s), CVE-2024-27919 Envoy oghttp, CVE-2024-2653 amphp, CVE-2024-27983 Node, CVE-2024-31309 ATS, CVE-2024-2758 Tempesta.
