verify.note: Calif post ratios: nginx ~70:1, IIS ~68:1, Envoy ~5,700:1, Apache ~4,000:1; Pingora 62-70x and 34 B/s keepalive not in post; Envoy CVE-2026-47774 unsupported (only GHSA-22m2); CVE-2026-49975 Apache-only confirmed.

title: Designs that survived MadeYouReset bound live handlers, not protocol-open streams
summary: Go x/net http2 scheduleHandler: run while curHandlers < advMaxStreams, otherwise queue; if len(unstartedHandlers) > 4*advMaxStreams, send GOAWAY ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM ('too_many_early_resets'); queued entries for already-reset streams are dropped. Other Go limits: maxQueuedControlFrames 10,000; >100 SETTINGS is an error; defaultMaxStreams 250. HAProxy counts allocated streams and uses a glitch counter (fe glitches-threshold 1000 kills a short-CONTINUATION flood instantly; be default 0 = off) and max-total-streams then GOAWAY. lighttpd closes the per-request backend socket on reset. nghttp2 1.57.0 uses an RST token bucket (burst 1000, 33/s) then GOAWAY.
specifics: hyper+h2 as written: h2 Counts decrements on reset, but the hyper task spawned by execute_h2stream lives until it is next polled and observes poll_reset. Live handlers are executor state, invisible to h2.
overclaim_risk: Vendor 'not affected' statements in the CERT note are self-reported.
underclaim_risk: Go's 4x-queue rule is a simple, checkable inductive invariant that AEGIS can adopt directly.

verify.note: Source snapshots not re-fetched.

title: QUIC/H3 default windows: s2n-quic caps the connection at 3.75 MB; quinn has no connection cap; h3 has no field-section cap
summary: s2n-quic d20f8fa: InitialMaxData = compute_data_window(150 Mbps, 100 ms, 2) = 3,750,000 B (transport/parameters/mod.rs:619-634), stream windows the same, 100 bidi / 100 uni, idle 30 s. quinn-proto (0.11.19, 2026-09-30) transport.rs:375-406: receive_window VarInt::MAX (no connection cap), stream_receive_window 1.25 MB, 100 bidi / 100 uni, so the flow-control ceiling is about 250 MB per connection. quiche 0.30.0: MAX_CONNECTION_WINDOW 24 MiB, MAX_STREAM_WINDOW 16 MiB, H3 max field section 32,768, QPACK dynamic table 0. hyperium h3 0.0.8: max_field_section_size VarInt::MAX (config.rs:140), static-only QPACK; open PR #366 notes FrameDecoder buffers the whole declared payload outside flow control. RFC 9204 s5 defaults: QPACK table capacity 0 and blocked streams 0; s7.3 calls the blocked-stream limit 'only a proxy' for memory.
overclaim_risk: quinn main may differ from the 0.11.19 release.
underclaim_risk: Setting quinn's receive_window to 4 MiB closes its largest gap with a single line.

verify.note: Version-specific defaults drift.

title: Zero-window stalls are a liveness property: nothing in h2/hyper bounds them, and TLA+ shows the deadlock
summary: RFC 9113 4.3: receivers 'MUST perform decompression even if the frames are to be discarded', and SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE is advisory (6.5.2). Calif's fix: 'stalled streams should have a bounded lifetime regardless of WINDOW_UPDATE activity'. A TLA+/TLC model of HTTP/2 flow control (Kurotych 2026, repo kurotych/conf_communication_deadlock, curl #16955) checks no-deadlock, byte conservation and liveness, and shows the deadlock is inevitable when data exceeds the window. Ivy NSCT (arXiv 2503.04810) and JADE (IFIP Networking 2026) test time-dependent QUIC behavior and found a picoquic idle-timeout bug.
specifics: Pinned bytes x time is unbounded at the library level today. It needs an AEGIS-level progress deadline, verified in DST with a simulated clock.
overclaim_risk: The TLA+ paper is a single regional-conference source.
underclaim_risk: Liveness cannot be checked by Kani at all, so without this clause every safety proof misses the HTTP/2 Bomb.

verify.note: Kurotych TLA+ is minor venue; gap not contradicted.

title: SPEC_INVARIANTS: Transport Budget Invariant (TBI-1..TBI-9) for H2/H3 ingress
summary: Per connection c, at every reachable state (inductive) and across time windows:
specifics: TBI-1 field block: decoded_rfc(c,s) = sum(32+|n|+|v|) <= MHLS=16384 AND fields(c,s) <= F=128, counting cookie crumbs. Every field is counted at decode time, before any merge. TBI-2 decode work: decoded_rfc bytes processed per field block before abort <= 4*MHLS, and work(frame) <= K1*|wire| + K2*decoded, so CPU is linear in input plus a bounded expansion. TBI-3 tables: HPACK dynamic table <= SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE=4096. QPACK capacity = 0 and blocked_streams = 0 in the golden. TBI-4 live handlers: H_live(c) <= S=100 AND queued(c) <= 4*S, else GOAWAY ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM. A permit is acquired before spawn and released on task drop, independent of protocol stream state. Global: sum over c of H_live(c) <= H_global. TBI-5 resets: peer RST_STREAM consumes a token bucket (burst 100, refill 33/s). Server-initiated error resets <= 256 per connection lifetime. Total streams per connection <= 10,000. Exhaustion sends GOAWAY. TBI-6 buffered bytes: unacknowledged received body bytes(c) <= conn_window (H2 1 MiB; QUIC 4 MiB) AND small-frame overhead budget <= 25,600 B. TBI-7 memory: live_alloc(c) <= M_conn = S*(F*C_FIELD + MHLS) + conn_window + send_buf, with C_FIELD measured, budgeted at 256 B. With the golden pins that is about 100*(128*256+16384) + 1 MiB + 400 KiB, about 6.3 MiB. TBI-8 liveness: a stream with no response-byte progress for T_stall=10 s is reset, regardless of WINDOW_UPDATE or PING. A connection with no stream progress for T_conn=30 s is closed. So pinned bytes x time <= M_conn x T_conn. TBI-9 no panic: no network input reaches panic!/assert!/HeaderMap overflow. Follows from TBI-1 (F < 32,768) and checked arithmetic.
overclaim_risk: The constants (F=128, T_stall=10 s, bucket 100/33) are engineering choices that need load-test validation. Legitimate gRPC/long-poll clients may stall for more than 10 s, so TBI-8 needs per-route overrides.
underclaim_risk: Every 2023-2026 H2/H3 DoS in the corpus violates at least one clause, so the invariant set is complete for the known lineage.

verify.note: Own design; constants are choices.

title: Tool per TBI clause (Kani vs Verus vs proptest/fuzz/DST), plus the clauses that cannot be proven over h2 as written
summary: Kani for pure arithmetic structs that exist in h2 or are ours: TBI-5 token bucket (Firecracker pattern), TBI-6 h2 FlowControl/Window (flow_control.rs, 269 LOC, pure i32 window arithmetic) and Budget (counts.rs), TBI-9 overflow-freedom. Verus for AEGIS's own admission/ledger module, which is new code we write: TBI-4 handler permits via a ghost multiset (permits_out + available == S, queued <= 4S) and TBI-1/TBI-7 ledger arithmetic as an inductive invariant over a sequence of decode events. Verus is chosen over Kani here because the property is unbounded-inductive (any number of streams) and Kani would need unwinding. Lean 4 (no Mathlib) for the small composition theorem: per-connection clause bounds sum to M_conn, and N connections sum to the global budget. Proptest + fuzz oracle for TBI-2 (Kani and Verus have no cost semantics) and for TBI-1 as realized inside h2's decoder. DST (tokio::time::pause / turmoil) for TBI-8, a liveness property Kani cannot express.
specifics: NOT provable over h2 as written: (a) TBI-4. Live handlers are tokio tasks spawned by hyper (server.rs:316), and h2's Counts tracks protocol-open streams, which drop on reset; this is exactly the MadeYouReset gap. It must be enforced and proven in an AEGIS wrapper (a Service layer holding a semaphore permit, or a custom Http2ServerConnExec). (b) TBI-8. Neither h2 nor hyper has any stall or progress timer, so the wrapper must own the deadline. (c) TBI-7's C_FIELD depends on http::HeaderMap layout and the allocator, so it can only be measured, not proven. (d) TBI-1's field count: h2 has no count cap, only MHLS in RFC units. F <= MHLS/33 = 496 is implied and provable, but F=128 needs a wrapper check, or a pre-decode pass over our own frame layer. Kani is infeasible on h2's Streams/Store (slab + Arc<Mutex> + async) per the Kani concurrency/await limits and the memory-blowup evidence.
overclaim_risk: Proving a wrapper's ledger does not prove h2 actually reports decode events truthfully. The trusted boundary is the h2 public API.
underclaim_risk: The split keeps every proof within the 6 GB / CI budget and needs no prover LLM.

verify.note: Kani feasibility on flow_control.rs untested.

title: Kani harness spec: aegis-transport-budget crate (+ optional upstream #[cfg(kani)] PRs to h2)
summary: Crate crates/aegis-transport-budget (no_std-ish, no async): TokenBucket, HandlerLedger, BlockLedger, ConnLedger. Harnesses live in #[cfg(kani)] mod verification and run on every PR in CI.
specifics: H1 bucket_preserves_invariant: any bucket with is_valid(), any op in {consume(n), refill(dt)} with Instant stubbed and dt symbolic; assert is_valid() and tokens <= burst. H2 block_ledger_bound: symbolic sequence of <= 8 add_field(n_len, v_len) with lens <= u16::MAX; assert that Ok implies decoded <= MHLS and fields <= F, that Err is returned exactly when a bound would be crossed, and that there is no overflow. Unwind 9. H3 handler_ledger_permits: <= 6 symbolic ops in {acquire, release, queue, dequeue_reset}; assert live <= S, queued <= 4S, live + available == S. Unwind 7. H4 h2_flow_control_window (upstream PR to h2 src/proto/streams/flow_control.rs): symbolic FlowControl with window in [i32::MIN, MAX_WINDOW_SIZE] and ops inc_window/send_data/dec_recv_window; assert no panic and window <= MAX_WINDOW_SIZE, and that inc_window errors with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR exactly on overflow. H5 h2_counts_budget: Budget::consume/replenish/set_max sequences; assert spent <= max or Err with spent unchanged. Solver cadical. Memory ceiling: every harness must pass under the heavy.sh 6 GB cap, with CI failure if any harness exceeds 300 s. Acceptance: cargo kani reports 0 failures on H1-H5. The Verus twin of H2/H3 (unbounded) lives in verus/ and is checked in CI with a pinned Verus + Z3 4.16.0.
overclaim_risk: The bounded harnesses (8 ops) prove small traces only. The unbounded claim rests on the Verus twin.
underclaim_risk: The pure-struct design mirrors s2n-quic and Firecracker CI patterns that already run in production.

verify.note: Spec only; Firecracker precedent confirmed.

title: Fuzz oracle and corpus: resource-ratio oracle over an in-memory h2 server with the AEGIS wrapper
summary: Target fuzz/fuzz_targets/h2_budget.rs: a tokio current-thread runtime with paused time, tokio::io::duplex, and hyper 1.12.0 server + AEGIS wrapper with golden config. The service never responds (worst case). A counting #[global_allocator] tracks live bytes. Input is a structured frame script (arbitrary-derived enum: HEADERS/CONTINUATION/DATA/RST/WINDOW_UPDATE/SETTINGS/PING/PRIORITY/advance_time(ms)).
specifics: Oracles (abort = finding): O1 peak_live_alloc <= M_conn (6.3 MiB) + baseline. O2 for each field block, decoded_rfc_bytes_processed / wire_bytes <= 4*MHLS / max(wire, 1), and process CPU (instruction counter or poll-iteration count) <= K * total_input_bytes with K fixed from a baseline run. O3 live_handlers <= 100 and queued <= 400 at every step. O4 after 101 RST without refill time, a GOAWAY is observed within 1 frame. O5 under INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=0 plus 1-byte WINDOW_UPDATEs, every stream is reset by virtual t = 10 s + epsilon and the connection is closed by 30 s. O6 no panic. Corpus seeds: Rapid Reset (CVE-2023-44487, HEADERS+RST x10k); MadeYouReset (CVE-2025-8671: HEADERS, then WINDOW_UPDATE increment 0 on the stream / overflow to 2^31, forcing a server RST, x10k); CONTINUATION flood (VU#421644: HEADERS without END_HEADERS + 100k 1-byte CONTINUATION, Huffman and raw variants); HTTP/2 Bomb (insert 1 entry, 16k 1-byte indexed refs + cookie crumbs, INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=0, WINDOW_UPDATE(1) every 5 s; califio PoC); h2 #909 (25k unique literal headers); GHSA-q83h small/empty DATA floods; SETTINGS flood (>100 entries) and PING/empty-frame floods (CVE-2019-9512/9518 lineage); Header Accordions for the h3 path (QPACK refs, FoxIO 2026-10-20). CI: cargo-fuzz 60 s smoke per PR, 1 h nightly, corpus committed under fuzz/corpus/h2_budget.
overclaim_risk: CPU-ratio oracles are noisy, which is why instruction/poll counters are used instead of wall time. Fuzzing cannot show the bound holds for all inputs.
underclaim_risk: No existing Rust transport fuzzer has any resource oracle, so this harness would be first of its kind and catches the whole DoS lineage.

verify.note: Untested design filling verified gap.

title: Config-pin table for the golden ingress (H2 via hyper/h2; H3 gated)
specifics: hyper http2 Builder: max_concurrent_streams(100) [default 200]; max_header_list_size(16384) [16 KiB]; header_table_size(4096); max_pending_accept_reset_streams(Some(20)); max_local_error_reset_streams(Some(256)) [default 1024]; initial_stream_window_size(256 KiB); initial_connection_window_size(1 MiB); max_frame_size(16384); max_send_buf_size(400 KiB); keep_alive_interval(Some(20 s)); keep_alive_timeout(20 s). AEGIS wrapper (not in hyper/h2): field_count<=128 incl cookie crumbs; handler semaphore 100/conn + 4x queue; global handler cap; RST bucket 100/33 s^-1; max_total_streams 10,000; T_stall 10 s; T_conn 30 s; control-frame queue <= 10,000. Never use raw h2 defaults (MHLS 16 MiB, unlimited streams). quinn-proto 0.11.19 (if H3 is enabled): receive_window(4 MiB) [default VarInt::MAX]; stream_receive_window(256 KiB) [1.25 MB]; max_concurrent_bidi_streams(100); max_concurrent_uni_streams(8) (H3 needs >= 3); max_idle_timeout(30 s). hyperium h3 0.0.8: max_field_section_size(16384) [default VarInt::MAX]. The golden keeps H3 OFF until h3 #366/#377/#378 land, or uses quiche 0.30.0 (32 KiB field section, QPACK dynamic table 0, 24 MiB conn window, which must be lowered). s2n-quic 1.91.0 defaults (3.75 MB conn window, 100/100 streams, 30 s idle) are acceptable as-is.
overclaim_risk: A 256 KiB stream window may throttle bulk uploads on high-BDP links. Tune it per route.
underclaim_risk: Each pin closes a documented gap (#909-class panics, the h3 unbounded section, the quinn connection window).

verify.note: h3 #377 (opened 2026-10-22) may merge soon and change the H3-off pin.

title: CI gate and acceptance criteria for the TBI
summary: The gate passes only if all of these hold: (1) cargo kani H1-H5 report 0 failures, each under 300 s and 6 GB. (2) The Verus twin of the ledger and handler invariants verifies with a pinned Verus + Z3. (3) The Lean composition lemma checks with Lean 4 core, no Mathlib. (4) The h2_budget fuzz smoke runs 60 s with 0 oracle violations, and every corpus seed replays clean. (5) A DST test replays HTTP/2 Bomb with paused time and asserts O5. (6) A config-pin test: a unit test instantiates the golden Builder and asserts each pinned value. (7) An implementation-phase spike measures C_FIELD (counting allocator over http 1.4.0 HeaderMap) and fails if C_FIELD > 256 B.
overclaim_risk: Gate (2) depends on Verus soundness (131 known soundness issues per the existing map).
underclaim_risk: All seven gates are machine-checkable and laptop-safe.

verify.note: verifier sampled other nodes; explorer grade kept

title: Wasmtime advisories classified by feature precondition: share hitting a minimal config
summary: Snapshot gh api 2026-10-25: 81 published GHSAs (81 unique), 65 in 2024-2026, 57 in 2026. Own classification by required feature preconditions. M0 (x86_64, Cranelift, core wasm only, no component/WASI/async/GC/memory64/threads): 6/65 (9%) guest-triggerable, of which exactly 1 exploitable sandbox escape (GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm, SSA bit-packing, default config any arch, fixed 36.0.19 / v43). M1 (+sync P2 components + non-fs WASI + wasi-http): 25/65 (38%); adds 2 string-transcoding OOB (GHSA-394w, GHSA-hx6p) that abort/DoS under default 4GiB reservation. M2 (+wasi-fs): 31/65 (48%), adds 2026 cap-std/fs escapes. Disabling cm-async/WASIp3 removes 14/65, gc+exceptions 6, winch 4, aarch64-only 2, memory64 1, wasi-fs 7, embedder-only 5.
specifics: Files: 07-data/adv.json, classify.py, classified.json. Hand-tagged from advisory text, tags are 'required preconditions'; embedder-only advisories excluded from guest-triggerable counts. Counter-evidence: cm-async and gc are Tier 1 and wasm_gc defaults true in Config, so M0 requires explicit disabling. 'Minimal config' shrinks but never zeroes: the one default-config critical hit M0.
overclaim_risk: Classification is mine from prose; tags may be wrong for 3-5 advisories (+-8pp). n=65 small; share of advisories is not share of exploitable risk, and unknown future bugs correlate with code volume in Cranelift, which M0 cannot shed.
underclaim_risk: Shares are of published advisories only; unreported/silently fixed bugs and the April 2026 LLM audit sprint mean the true M0 bug rate is probably higher than 6/65 suggests.

verify.note: Hand classification not reproducible externally; n=65; same-day batches not independent.

title: Minimal Wasmtime Config pin: flags and residual advisory share
summary: Pin wasmtime >= 43.0.x (or 36.0.19+ on the 36 LTS line), default-features=false, features cranelift, pooling-allocator, runtime, std, plus component-model only if P2 components needed; NO component-model-async, gc, threads, winch, profiling, wasi-fs preopens. Config: strategy(Cranelift); wasm_memory64(false); wasm_gc(false); wasm_threads(false); wasm_exceptions off; wasm_component_model_async(false); signals_based_traps left TRUE (disabling also disables Spectre mitigations and re-opens GHSA-jhxm); keep default memory_reservation (4GiB) and memory_guard_size (32MiB 64-bit default; do NOT set guard 0); epoch_interruption(true) with ResourceLimiter on memory/tables since bulk memory ops check epoch only once; fresh Store per request, drop on any trap; pooling with sizes computed per component (a P2 component consumed >1 core instance each: pool of 64 failed at 60 components, so size total_core_instances ~ 8x concurrent). Residual share on the 65-advisory base: M0 9% (1 sandbox escape, fixed), M1 38% (adds transcoding OOB/DoS and wasi-http), vs 100% unfiltered. Acceptance gate: cargo deny + CI test that asserts Config fields and fails on any added feature; patch SLO <72h because the one M0 escape was in default Cranelift.
specifics: Defaults observed in docs.rs 48.0.7: memory_reservation 4GiB, guard 32MiB, memory_may_move true, wasm_gc true, wasm_memory64 false, wasm_threads follows crate feature (default on), pooling defaults 1000 slots each, max_memory_size 4GiB, decommit_batch_size 1, MPK off, ~4GiB VA/slot (cap ~32k slots). My bench used =48.0.7 with features cranelift,pooling-allocator,component-model,runtime,std,parallel-compilation,memory-protection-keys.
overclaim_risk: Does not prove safety: GHSA-897f shows default Cranelift on any arch can be escaped by a crafted large function; pin is necessary not sufficient, and still needs an OS sandbox around it. Version numbers drift (v43/48 current at snapshot).
underclaim_risk: Share numbers are conservative-to-wrong in both directions; M1 38% is an upper bound because many of those need rarely used wasi-http paths.

verify.note: Defaults verified; pin must be exactly 36.0.19+ on 36 line or >=43.

title: Skeptic: 'hardened pooling with small max_memory_size / reduced reservation' re-opens advisories
summary: The common hardening advice to shrink per-slot virtual reservation and guards for density can re-enable GHSA-6wgr (pooling leak needs guard_size=0 and reservation == max_memory_size < 4GiB) and widens impact of GHSA-394w string-transcoding OOB (reduced reservation + no guards => host memory corruption rather than abort). Also CVE-2026-34971 (GHSA-jhxm-h53p-jm7w, aarch64 Cranelift, critical, fixed 36.0.7/42.0.2/43.0.1) needs memory64 AND (spectre mitigations off OR signals_based_traps off). Hardened != dense: keep default guard/reservation, pay the ~4GiB VA/slot (cap ~32k slots) and use MPK only for density.
specifics: Source: advisory texts in adv.json; wasmtime pooling docs say steady-state no-VM-tricks config disables guard and memory_init_cow as a perf option without discussing security.
overclaim_risk: Each preconditioned bug is only reachable with unusual config; the point is the interaction, not that default is broken.
underclaim_risk: Might also interact with other bugs not yet classified.

verify.note: GHSA-6wgr = CVE-2026-34988 (four opt-in conditions; defaults not vulnerable); GHSA-394w = CVE-2026-35195 / RUSTSEC-2026-0091 Medium 6.1; cited URL wrong.

title: LOCAL: component canonical-ABI cost per call and per KB, serde_json handler, wasmtime 48.0.7 vs native Rust
summary: i9-14900HX, pinned core, rustc 1.98, Cranelift, epoch on, parse+double qty+reserialize. Native: 105B 0.38us; 756B 3.3us; 12.2KB 41.7us; 198KB 860us. Core wasm incl host alloc/copy: 1.06 / 6.1 / 84 / 1310 us. Component handle-bytes: 1.24 / 6.78 / 90.8 / 1397 us; handle-str within 1%. Call floor: core noop 11 ns, component noop 97 ns => ~85 ns canonical-ABI fixed cost; marginal component vs core = +0.2us fixed, ~ +0.03-0.4 ns/B (copy+utf8 validation), i.e. 2-7% of core cost. Dominant overhead is wasm vs native serde (about 2.0x at all sizes, ~6.6 vs 4.3 ns/B), not ABI. Fresh Store+instantiate per request (pooling, WASI p2 linked): setup p50 4.2us/p99 8.6us, first call 11.7us, total with drop p50 20.3us/p99 30us, RSS 52KB per live instance after one request.
specifics: Code 07-bench/{host,logic,guest-comp,guest-core}; outputs run5.txt. Pitfalls found: pooling total_core_instances must exceed component count x core-instances-per-component (64 failed at 60); ulimit -v breaks pooling (needs ~258GB VA for 64 slots); missing epoch deadline on new Stores traps immediately.
overclaim_risk: Single machine, single workload (JSON-heavy, large per-byte compute) so ABI share is small; with trivial handlers ABI + instantiate (about 20us) dominates. Linking cost of async-enabled components (roadmap says ~3.5x on sync cross-component calls) not measured since async is off.
underclaim_risk: Per-KB ABI cost may be even lower than measured; resolution is limited by compute noise.

verify.note: Own measurement with noop floor; one machine, serde handler only.

title: Zygote sandbox recipe with measured latency: fork from pre-warmed zygote + Landlock + seccomp-bpf
summary: Recipe: zygote process loads engine + precompiled component, sets no_new_privs, opens listening/log fds, applies Landlock ruleset (1 rule) and seccomp allowlist BEFORE any request, then per request fork(); child handles one request and _exit. If per-request policy differs, apply Landlock (12us) in child; avoid compiling seccomp BPF in child (~120-130us). Measured (kernel 6.17.0-14, Landlock on): fork latency by zygote RSS 8MB p50 124us (p99 400), 64MB 677us, 256MB 1466us (~70us fixed + ~5.5-10us/MB); fork+exit+wait 400us / 1.7ms / 3.7ms; vfork baseline 17us. seccomp install of 60-syscall allowlist p50 123-131us; Landlock create+rule+restrict p50 11-13us (p99 17-27). CoW: child dirtying 4MB inherited heap adds ~2.0ms (~2us/page), 256KB adds ~0.18ms. Idle sibling PSS = zygote_heap/(n+1)+~60KB (187KB/child at 8MB, 1.3MB at 64MB, 5.2MB at 256MB for 50 children); Private_Dirty 16.4MB after touching 16MB. Comparison: in-process pooled instance 20us / 52KB, i.e. fork is 6x (8MB zygote) to 80x (256MB) more latency and 3.6x-100x more memory than a Wasmtime Store; hence use process sandbox per worker/tenant-tier (long-lived), not per request, unless request is untrusted-native code.
specifics: Code 07-bench/sb/sb.c; outputs sb8.txt sb64.txt sb256.txt. Landlock must be applied before seccomp (seccomp allowlist otherwise kills landlock syscalls). Landlock ABI up to 11 per docs: TSYNC (ABI 8) for threaded servers; scoped signal/abstract-socket (ABI 6); 16 stacked layers max; stat/chdir/chmod not restrictable.
overclaim_risk: Zygote here is a bare C process with dirtied anonymous heap; a real zygote with mapped wasmtime code (file-backed, shared) forks cheaper per MB than anon heap; THP/hugepages and 4K-page assumptions affect numbers. Not tested under memory pressure or with many threads (fork in multithreaded process is unsafe).
underclaim_risk: fork cost scales with mapped anon RSS only, so a lean zygote (<10MB private) is ~100us, close to the best a process can get; vfork+exec (17us) path not evaluated with exec cost.

verify.note: Own measurement; synthetic C zygote vs Rust pooled Store not like-for-like; Sandlock paper supports only its own row.

title: LOCAL: seccomp-bpf per-syscall overhead: cacheable allowlist ~+20-30 ns, arg-checks ~1 ns/insn
summary: getppid loop, kernel 6.17: unfiltered 84-116 ns (varies by run; compare within a run). Cacheable allowlist (syscall-number-only) of 16/60/200 rules: +18 to +30 ns (~+20-25%) independent of list length, confirming 5.11 constant-action bitmap cache. Non-cacheable (filter loads args) worst-case position: 60 rules +41 ns, 200 rules +108 ns, 500 rules +290 to +450 ns, about 0.5-0.8 ns per BPF instruction. Filter stacking adds evaluation time (kernel doc). Rule: keep hot syscalls (read/write/futex/clock_gettime/epoll) arg-free to stay on the bitmap; put arg checks only on cold syscalls (openat, mmap flags, clone3).
specifics: Code 07-bench/sb/sb.c. Single syscall type, CPU frequency noise between runs (baseline 84 vs 116 ns), n=3 rule config anomaly (135 vs 102 at n=16) unexplained; treat +/-10 ns.
overclaim_risk: Mitigations (Spectre SSBD) interacting with seccomp not controlled; per-syscall ns is tiny vs the ~1us+ of real I/O syscalls.
underclaim_risk: Overhead on I/O-heavy server is likely unmeasurable (Sandlock paper reports Redis within noise).

verify.note: Baseline drift same size as effect; consistent with 5.11 bitmap cache theory.

title: Updated isolation decision-input table (numbers only, own measurements + cited)
summary: Per-request cost / memory / residual advisory exposure: (a) native in-process Rust handler: 0.38us for 105B JSON, 0 extra RSS, no wasm bug class. (b) Wasmtime core module, warm instance: call 11ns, handler 1.06us (2.8x native at 105B, 1.5x at 198KB incl copies). (c) Wasmtime P2 component warm: 97ns noop, 1.24us handler; (d) fresh pooled Store+component instance with WASI linked: 20us p50/30us p99, 52KB RSS/instance (earlier module-only: 6.9us, 7.1KB). (e) fork from lean 8MB zygote with policy pre-installed: ~124us + exit/wait 400us, PSS ~190KB/child; 64MB zygote: 0.7ms; 256MB: 1.5ms. (f) fork + in-child seccomp compile + Landlock: +135us. (g) Hyperlight microVM per call ~0.9ms claimed (KubeCon demo), VM creation 1-2ms; independent Dandelion paper measured Hyperlight-Wasm unloaded 27.5ms avg on matmul. (h) Sandlock (arXiv 2605.26298) ~5ms startup, Redis within noise. Advisory exposure: M0 6/65 (1 escape), M1 25/65, M2 31/65 of 2024-26 Wasmtime advisories. seccomp tax +20-30ns/syscall cacheable.
specifics: No prior picks recorded here per brief; decision rule left to synthesis. All A rows are from this machine (i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17, 2 pinned cores). Hyperlight/Sandlock rows are secondary-reported (B/C).
overclaim_risk: Mixing own-hardware and vendor numbers; microVM numbers different hardware/workload.
underclaim_risk: Per-request wasm overhead is small vs typical handler I/O; ratios shown are worst-case for tiny handlers.

verify.note: Hyperlight 0.9 ms is warm recycled-guest vendor demo; Dandelion 27.5 ms dominated by runtime load; cross-hardware.

title: GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm (CVE id as published CVE-2026-115889): Cranelift SSA bit-packing overflow, critical, default config any arch
summary: Published 2026-10-19; Wasmtime <36.0.19 and 37.0.0-<43.0.0; a large or SSA-heavy function body forces silent index overflow and arbitrary miscompilation => type confusion and sandbox escape. Fixed by full u32 index with limit checks in v43, backport 36.0.19; no workaround listed; reporter credited with AI-assisted submission. Only advisory in the 65 that is an exploitable escape on the minimal M0 config. Companion: CVE-2026-34971 / GHSA-jhxm (aarch64, memory64 + spectre/signals off) and CVE-2026-34987 Winch.
specifics: Advisory page states no mitigation via function-size limits; do not assume max function size mitigates.
overclaim_risk: One incident; does not generalize to a rate.
underclaim_risk: Cranelift compiler bugs remain the central residual risk for wasm-as-sole-boundary, supporting an OS layer.

verify.note: GHSA-897f facts match (CVSS 9.9, CVE-2026-115889, 2026-10-19); JLSEC-2026-1360 and RUSTSEC-2026-0096 are the aarch64 jhxm advisory, mis-attributed; 37-42 have no backport.

title: Own crash-state replay harness (ALICE-style) with positive/negative controls, 7 stores, 36 config x seed cells, ~132k crash images
summary: LD_PRELOAD op-trace shim + python replay: at ~400 random cut points per run, builds crash images under 4 data policies (dropall, all=SIGKILL, subset=per-4KiB-page random survival with reorder, prefix=issue-order prefix with last write torn at 512B) x 3 namespace regimes (journal=ext4-ordered-like, fsfile, strict=POSIX-literal: ns op durable only after parent-dir fsync); oracle = counter in two tables+full-state equality+integrity_check; acked = marker after commit returns. Positive control (no-fsync log) loses acked data in ~99% of dropall cuts and tears records under subset; negative control (len|crc|fdatasync|dir-fsync log) 0/8020 violations. Oracle can fail and can pass.
specifics: N=300 txns/run (2 keys-tables, counter+payload), 400 cuts, seeds 1-3 (fjall, canopydb, wal controls 2-3 seeds; redb 2; heed/sqlite 1). Versions: redb 4.4.0 (vcs 7061f7e6), fjall 3.1.12 (d43b66b9; lsm-tree 3.1.10 9812163a), heed 0.23.0 (407de3c3; lmdb-master-sys 0.2.6 57025ff0), rusqlite 0.41.0 (a60e76b5; libsqlite3-sys 0.39.0 bundled SQLite 3.54.0), canopydb 0.2.5 (cb52555f); rustc 1.98.0 (+ rustix_use_libc). Kernel 6.17.0-14, ext4 nvme. Artifacts: raw/round-002/08-...harness/ (crashsim.py, main.rs, shim.c), ...results.jsonl, ...final_table.json.
overclaim_risk: Replay is a logical model not a real power cut: no sub-512B tearing, no misdirected/lost-flush device behaviour, mmap stores not modelled (redb/heed/sqlite use pwrite here, MMAPW logged but flagged), fsync-error semantics untouched, and 'strict'/'fsfile' ns regimes are adversarial POSIX readings not ext4 behaviour. Zero violations means 'none found in ~1e4 states', not proof.
underclaim_risk: Controls prove sensitivity; cut sampling (400/run) can still miss rare windows; N=300 txns is small relative to checkpoint/compaction thresholds (SQLite 1000-page checkpoint, redb growth) so checkpoint-boundary bugs are under-sampled.

verify.note: Logical replay model, small N; controls demonstrate sensitivity.

title: NEGATIVE: LD_PRELOAD write tracing is blind to rustix/tempfile raw syscalls - first fjall run was 100% false positives
summary: fjall persists keyspaces/N/current via tempfile 3.27.0 -> rustix 1.1.5 whose default linux_raw backend issues raw syscalls (strace: renameat; shim saw 0 rename ops), so replayed images kept .tmp files and an empty 'current' and 391/401 all/full (SIGKILL) states 'lost' acked writes. Also materializing images dropped empty directories. Fixed by building with RUSTFLAGS='--cfg rustix_use_libc' and recreating dirs; after fix fjall SyncAll shows 0 acked loss. Any interposer-based Rust crash harness must be coverage-audited against strace per store; FUSE (LazyFS), dm-log-writes/dm-flakey or ptrace/seccomp-unotify are interposer-independent. io_uring would bypass too.
specifics: Audit command: strace -f -e trace=%file,write,pwrite64,fsync,fdatasync,renameat... per store vs shim hook list. Only tempfile (fjall) used rustix in this dependency set; redb/heed/sqlite/canopydb syscalls (pwrite64, writev, fdatasync, fsync, fallocate, ftruncate, rename, mkdir) were all hooked.
overclaim_risk: Only audited 6 store configs with N=3 txns; a path taken only at larger N (e.g. compaction, WAL rotation) could still bypass the shim.
underclaim_risk: The libc-backend rebuild is not what production runs (production uses linux_raw); behavior difference should be nil but is unmeasured.

verify.note: General methodological result; audit limited to 6 configs.

title: redb 4.4.0: 0 violations when the file's creation is durable; 1PC+C vs 2PC indistinguishable in 16k states; loses ALL acked data in POSIX-strict regime because parent dir never fsynced; Durability::None loses everything on SIGKILL
summary: imm (1PC+C default, 1 fsync): journal/fsfile/SIGKILL regimes 0/801 violations per policy; strict: 383/801 dropall, 393/801 subset, 401/801 prefix lost_ack with c=0 (the db file itself vanishes: redb creates+fsyncs the file but never fsyncs the parent directory). imm2pc (set_two_phase_commit(true), 2 fsync): identical (380/802 strict), no corruption either way, check_integrity true on all survivors. Durability::None: 6000/6160 lost_ack incl. SIGKILL (acks are not durable even against process death) + 43 init_open_fail. Upstream CHANGELOG shows 1PC+C recovery-path durability bugs fixed in the last 3 months: 4.2.0 (2026-08-17) 'A crash during recovery from an earlier crash could roll back or corrupt durable transactions (not those using two-phase commit)'; 4.3.0 (2026-09-14) 'crash shortly after a commit could silently roll it back during recovery'; 5.0.0 (unreleased) makes SingleWriter commits always two-phase and refuses Durability::None. design.md: 1PC+C relies on XXH3 (non-crypto) checksum + txn id; assumes single-byte atomic write and powersafe-overwrite, states no ordering guarantee.
specifics: PIN: redb =4.4.0 (or newer 4.x), set_two_phase_commit(true) on every write txn, Durability::Immediate only, never None for acked state; at bootstrap create the file via Database::create then fsync the file and its parent directory before serving (our harness shows the missing dir fsync is the only acked-loss path). Unmeasured: 2PC latency cost on target VPS (2 fsyncs/commit).
overclaim_risk: 'No corruption' is for the model above, not a proof; the 4.2.0/4.3.0 recovery bugs show the crash-during-recovery path (double fault) is where redb 1PC+C has actually failed, and my single-crash harness does NOT exercise it (no crash-in-recovery stage).
underclaim_risk: The strict-regime loss is a one-time creation window: on ext4/xfs in practice a later fsync of anything usually commits the journal, so real-world exposure is the first seconds after db creation. Harness 'journal' regime shows 0.

verify.note: CHANGELOG matches (4.2.0, 4.3.0, 4.4.0 fixes; 5.0.0 unreleased forces 2PC); strict-regime loss is worst case.

title: heed 0.23.0 / LMDB (lmdb-master-sys 0.2.6): default flags safe except the same create-time dir fsync gap; NO_META_SYNC loses 1 commit (documented) but up to all in strict; NO_SYNC corrupts (395 open failures + 110 SIGSEGV/SIGBUS in 4010 states)
summary: default (full sync): 0 violations under journal/fsfile/SIGKILL; strict dropall 194/401 lost_ack (file vanishes, LMDB never fsyncs parent dir). nometasync: 2225/4010 lost_ack of which lag=1 commit in 1613 (matches lmdb.h: 'system crash may undo the last committed transaction ... preserves ACI but not D') but 585 states lost >=9 acked commits (strict ns, file vanish); no corruption. nosync: acked loss in 3057/4010, MDB_INVALID 'not an LMDB file' open failures 395, MDB_CORRUPTED read failures 23, atomicity break 2 (A/B tables diverge), 110 process crashes (SIGSEGV 55, SIGBUS 55) when opening/reading torn maps - i.e. a poisoned DB can crash the reader process, not just error. Matches lmdb.h text: NOSYNC may corrupt unless fs preserves write order; Howard Chu 2019: 'all bets are off' otherwise. ATC20 (Rebello) lists LMDB among apps studied for fsync-failure handling.
specifics: PIN: heed 0.23.0 with EnvOpenOptions default flags only (no NO_SYNC/NO_META_SYNC/WRITE_MAP/MAP_ASYNC), fsync parent dir after first create. Single seed only for heed (4010 states per config).
overclaim_risk: One seed; mmap-based WRITE_MAP mode not tested (stores via pwrite in default); LMDB's reliance on single-sector meta-page atomic write is untestable below 512B in this model.
underclaim_risk: NO_META_SYNC may still be acceptable for a cache-class store with a documented one-commit window; sampled loss there is the documented one.

verify.note: One seed; nometasync lag of exactly 1 commit matches lmdb.h.

title: fjall 3.1.12: SyncAll/SyncData batches show 0 acked loss in 12030 states each; default (Buffer) loses acked writes even on SIGKILL and can refuse to open (JournalRecovery(ChecksumMismatch)); creation-time kill bricks the directory
summary: syncall: 0 lost_ack, 0 corruption in 12030 states (3 seeds); only 78 init_open_fail = process/OS killed during first-time creation (before any ack) leaves keyspace dir that open() rejects (InvalidVersion(None) / AlreadyExists 'File exists') and cannot recreate -> needs manual rm; reproduces under SIGKILL regime too (8/1203). syncdata: 0 lost, 71 init_open_fail. default (PersistMode::Buffer): lost_ack 6658/12030 states, 1 in 3 SIGKILL (all/full) cuts lose acked writes (acks mean only 'in userspace buffer'), commits lost in runs of >=9; plus 5 open_fail JournalRecovery(ChecksumMismatch) when a torn/partial middle journal write survives (subset policy) - DB unavailable until repaired. Upstream issue #329 (fjall/lsm-tree 3.1.10, opened 2026-10-01, fixed in main 8b2bae0): memtable flush did not sync journal first; Buffer commits lost on power loss; cross-keyspace batch recovered partially; get() and range() returned different values (5 vs 126) silently; maintainer 'blind-fix' since no fault injection existed. Not reproduced by my harness because only 300 txns with 64KiB memtable and SyncAll tested (bug needs Buffer mode + flush).
specifics: PIN: fjall =3.1.12 (and lsm-tree verify >= fix of #329), every batch .durability(Some(PersistMode::SyncAll)); never rely on Buffer for acked state; application bootstrap must rm -r a keyspace dir that has no 'version' marker. fjall does fsync directories (file.rs fsync_directory), explaining 0 strict-regime loss unlike redb/LMDB.
overclaim_risk: SyncAll 0/12030 is bounded by N=300 and small memtables: flush/compaction/journal rotation (64MB) windows where #329 lived are not reached; do not read it as 'fjall is crash-safe'.
underclaim_risk: Open-fail on creation crash is a sharp edge but loses no acked data.

verify.note: #329 confirmed (fixed 8b2bae0, 3.1.10); issue says process crashes unaffected, in tension with SIGKILL Buffer loss - recheck BufWriter replay semantics.

title: SQLite 3.54.0 (rusqlite 0.41.0): WAL+FULL and WAL+EXTRA and TRUNCATE+FULL: 0 violations in 4010 states each; WAL+NORMAL loses acked commits in 85% of cuts (unbounded to last checkpoint); DELETE journal FULL loses last commit ~12% (journal unlink not dir-synced)
summary: wal-full/wal-extra/trunc-full: 4010/4010 ok under all regimes incl. strict. wal-normal: lost_ack 3391/4010; lag histogram: 107 states lost 1 commit, 2770 states lost >=9 commits => NORMAL durability gap is not 'last transaction' but everything since last WAL sync (checkpoint) - consistent with wal.html ('checkpoint is the only operation to issue a sync ... transactions are no longer durable'); no corruption in NORMAL (WAL stays consistent). del-full (rollback journal, synchronous=FULL): journal/strict regimes lost_ack ~87/401 (~22%) because the journal unlink is not directory-synced so the hot journal is replayed and rolls back a committed txn (SQLite doc: EXTRA adds the dir sync); under the adversarial fsfile regime (out-of-order ns persistence) del-full ALSO shows corruption (integrity_fail 21, atomicity 32, open_fail 24, state_mismatch 39 of 4010) but 0 in the ext4-like journal regime, and I attribute that to the model allowing an older unlink to be applied after a newer journal create (unverified hypothesis) - treat as a POSIX-literal risk, not an observed ext4 bug. SQLite's own forum: commit survives process crash but not OS crash under NORMAL.
specifics: PIN: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=FULL (EXTRA if the unlink/rename window matters), wal_autocheckpoint default; never NORMAL for acked state. Needs a multi-writer story? SQLite is single-writer; WAL needs shared-memory, same host.
overclaim_risk: wal-full passes 4010 states with 1 seed and N=300 (< 1000-page auto-checkpoint, so checkpoint crash windows - the place SQLite docs say syncs matter - were barely exercised).
underclaim_risk: SQLite is the most battle-tested here (billions of deployments); my harness tests only one workload shape.

verify.note: WAL+NORMAL documented; DELETE+FULL loss 12.7% (509/4010) vs ~22% of dropall wording inconsistent.

title: canopydb 0.2.5: plain commit() is NOT durable (default_commit_sync=false) - 10600/12030 states lose acked commits; commit_with(true) passes 12030/12030; doc says background WAL sync default 1s but source default is None
summary: EnvOptions.wal_background_sync_interval doc: 'Default: 1 second' but Default impl sets None; DbOptions.default_commit_sync default false, so WriteTransaction::commit() acks before fsync. sync config (commit_with(true)): 0 violations in all regimes incl. strict (it fsyncs dirs; includes mkdir/rename/fallocate paths). async = default in outcome. Early-stage: lib.rs listed single 0.1.0 (Oct 2024) but 0.2.5 resolved locally.
specifics: This was the 'one more candidate found independently' (alternatives enumerated before reading prior treatments: sled alpha, libmdbx, Turso/limbo, Fjall, redb, canopydb, SQLite, LMDB). sled =1.0.0-alpha.124 compiled in the workload but not swept (alpha).
overclaim_risk: Only a 'default is unsafe' finding; the engine is young, so absence of other findings is weak evidence.

verify.note: Source confirms default_commit_sync=false and wal_background_sync_interval=None; nothing syncs WAL by default.

title: Which store loses acknowledged writes (measured table): ranking by configuration
summary: Violations of acked-durability (acked count > recovered) over all images, per store/config (states): wal-naive control 6679/8000; redb Durability::None 6000/6160; canopydb commit() 10600/12030; fjall Buffer 6658/12030; heed NO_SYNC 3057/4010 (+corruption 395 open fail, 110 crashes); sqlite WAL+NORMAL 3391/4010; heed NO_META_SYNC 2225/4010; sqlite DELETE+FULL 509/4010 (+corruption only under adversarial ns model); redb 1PC+C 1177/8010 and 2PC 1176/8020 (all in strict-ns create window); heed default 587/4010 (same window); PASS (0 acked loss, 0 corruption): sqlite WAL+FULL/EXTRA, sqlite TRUNCATE+FULL, canopydb sync, fjall SyncAll/SyncData (only create-time open failures), walcrc control. Interpretation: the dominant failure across stores is not torn writes but (a) acks issued before fsync by default/opt-in flags and (b) parent-directory fsync missing at creation (redb, LMDB).
specifics: Source: 08-...final_table.json. SIGKILL (process death, page cache intact) loses acked writes only for redb None, fjall Buffer, canopydb/async? (canopy all/full OK). Torn-write corruption found only in LMDB NO_SYNC and (adversarial model) SQLite DELETE mode.

verify.note: Mixed denominators/regimes; qualitative ranking robust.

title: RWF_ATOMIC / untorn writes: Linux 6.13 (not 6.11) merged DIO-only single-block atomic writes on ext4/XFS; 6.16 added XFS multi-block; buffered atomic not merged as of May 2026; this host does not advertise it
summary: LWN 1009298 + docs.kernel.org: RWF_ATOMIC direct I/O only, ext4 single fs-block (bigalloc for multi-block), no software fallback, requires device support, statx STATX_WRITE_ATOMIC reports unit min/max. kernelnewbies: 6.13 'atomic writes in XFS, Ext4's Direct I/O, md RAID'; 6.16 'large atomic writes for xfs (multi-block, all or none)'. LWN Mar/May 2026: atomic buffered I/O still absent; RWF_WRITETHROUGH proposal 2026-04; PostgreSQL full_page_writes off = 1.7x TPS and 14x less TPS variance (session claim, setup not given). Own probe on this machine (kernel 6.17.0-14, ext4 on nvme0n1p9): statx mask lacks STATX_WRITE_ATOMIC (0x10000) -> RWF_ATOMIC is unusable here. None of redb/fjall/LMDB/SQLite use RWF_ATOMIC. => For a household VPS the practical answer is checksums (WAL CRC, redb XXH3, fjall) not atomic writes.
specifics: VPS virtio-blk disks do not forward atomic-write limits unless the hypervisor does; unmeasured on a VPS.
overclaim_risk: kernelnewbies pages truncated at 100k chars; 6.16 multi-block XFS requires forcealign/ big blocks details not verified from patch text.
underclaim_risk: Hardware-level (NVMe AWUPF) atomicity may be present on many drives without being exposed.

verify.note: RWF_ATOMIC interface landed in 6.11 (kernelnewbies); ext4 single-block 6.13; buffered atomic unmerged (LWN 2026-05-14).

title: fsync/O_SYNC guarantees are weaker than man pages in practice: ext4 6.19.2 O_SYNC size bug, fsync-failure studies, virtio flush contract, CrashMonkey
summary: LKML 2026-02-18 (Kovalevsky): Linux 6.19.2 ext4 default (XFS reportedly too): file created+synced with 5000 B, reopened O_SYNC, 10 B write, QEMU system_reset -> file size 4096 not 5000 (O_SYNC not equivalent to fsync after each write); no fix noted in the thread page I fetched. My shim treated O_SYNC/O_DSYNC writes as durable, so the harness would miss this class -> specify fsync()/fdatasync() explicitly, avoid O_SYNC for append. ATC20 'Can Applications Recover from fsync Failures?': PostgreSQL, LMDB, LevelDB, SQLite, Redis; failures cause data loss/corruption; ext4/XFS/btrfs mark pages clean. CrashMonkey/ACE (OSDI18): 26 historical bugs studied, 10 new bugs in ext4/btrfs/F2FS (rename atomicity, files lost after fsync), most need <=3 ops and crash after fsync. virtio: device MUST commit completed writes on flush when flush negotiated; writeback hypervisors that ack flushes without honoring them defeat every store above (provider-specific, unmeasured). dm-flakey drop_writes/dm-log-writes (xfstests generic/482,500) are the in-kernel crash replay alternatives (discard caveat on XFS).
overclaim_risk: LKML page showed no maintainer reply; do not assert it is unfixed.
underclaim_risk: Many kernel crash bugs never reach LKML summaries.

verify.note: LKML O_SYNC report is single reporter, unconfirmed, also suspects XFS.

title: LazyFS (dsrhaslab): FUSE3 fault-injection FS (torn-seq, torn-op, clear-cache); VLDB'24 found 8 new bugs in PG/etcd/ZK/Redis/LevelDB/PebblesDB/LN but tested none of redb/fjall/LMDB/SQLite; not runnable here (needs libfuse3-dev)
summary: Repo: 234 stars, 299 commits, BSD-3 (badge says MIT), C++17+CMake, tested ext4 default on Debian 11/Ubuntu 20.04, 'simple' cache most tested, post-crash mount may need fusermount -uz. 'When Amnesia Strikes' (VLDB 2024, p3017-ramos): 20 scenarios. Gap = our experiment. Reorder fault not documented on the README page.
specifics: CI use needs libfuse3 and user_allow_other.
underclaim_risk: Maintenance recency unverified (last commit date not shown).

verify.note: VLDB24 eight bugs confirmed.

title: L5: storage crash-harness spec for CI (fault model, oracle, pass criteria, interposer-independence)
summary: FAULT MODEL (all must be run): (1) SIGKILL at random syscall boundaries, page cache intact; (2) power-cut drop-all-unsynced; (3) per-4KiB-page random survival with reorder of unsynced writes; (4) issue-order prefix with last write torn at 512B; (5) namespace regimes ext4-ordered and POSIX-strict (ns op durable only after parent-dir fsync); (6) crash-during-recovery (second crash while reopening) - NOT yet implemented, required because redb 4.2.0/4.3.0 bugs were double-fault; (7) injected fsync EIO (fsyncgate: no retry may be treated as success). ORACLE: workload of N txns each updating >=2 tables with a monotone counter + payload; after every commit return write an ack marker out-of-band; after recovery require (a) open succeeds, (b) counter A==B (atomicity), (c) counter >= last ack (durability) and <= issued, (d) full-state equality with the model at that counter, (e) engine integrity check. Mutation gate: ship a no-fsync control that MUST fail and a len|crc|fdatasync|dir-fsync control that MUST pass in every CI run, else the harness is broken (as.oracle-mutation). INTERPOSER: coverage-audit by strace diff per store each run (rustix raw syscalls bypass LD_PRELOAD; build with --cfg rustix_use_libc or use FUSE/dm-log-writes/ptrace). PASS: zero violations over >=10k images per (store,config) on 3 seeds incl. one run with N above checkpoint/rotation thresholds (>=2000 txns, >64MB journal for fjall, >1000 WAL pages for SQLite). Reference impl: raw/round-002/08-...harness/{crashsim.py,main.rs,shim.c}; ~4-12 min per config on a loaded 32-core host (images verified in 8 threads).
specifics: Extends sdg-l5-crash-harness (ALICE-style) with measured instrument, controls, two regimes and the rustix lesson.
underclaim_risk: Spec is stronger than needed for a cache-only tier.

verify.note: Crash-during-recovery and EIO not yet implemented; redb 4.2.0 shows the gap is material.

title: L5: store-of-record acceptance gate (what a store must show before holding acknowledged state)
summary: A store/config is admitted only if: G1 harness (cc.l5-crash-harness-spec) zero acked-loss and zero corruption on ext4-ordered regime for 3 seeds; G2 strict-regime result is either zero or the only failures are class 'file vanishes at creation' AND bootstrap does file+parent-dir fsync (verified by a bootstrap test that re-runs the strict regime after bootstrap = 0); G3 default-config footgun scan: grep options for durability defaults (canopydb default_commit_sync=false, fjall Buffer, redb None, SQLite synchronous NORMAL, LMDB NO_*) and require explicit pin in code + test that asserts the pinned value; G4 upstream CHANGELOG/issue scan for 'crash|recovery|corrupt|fsync|data loss' in last 12 months with each item mapped to a regression test (redb has 4 such in 2026); G5 acked-loss under SIGKILL must be 0 (process death must never lose acked data); G6 unavailability budget: after any single crash the store must open without manual action (fjall creation-time brick fails G6 unless bootstrap wrapper cleans); G7 pinned versions + vcs sha recorded. Result with current evidence: PASS = SQLite WAL+FULL, canopydb sync (young), fjall SyncAll (with bootstrap wrapper, N-limited), redb 2PC (with dir-fsync bootstrap); FAIL = LMDB NO_SYNC, heed NO_META_SYNC for acked state, redb None, fjall Buffer, canopydb commit(), SQLite WAL+NORMAL.
specifics: Criteria G1-G7 are our proposal; thresholds (3 seeds, >=10k images) are judgment, not from literature.
underclaim_risk: Gate may exclude stores that are fine on a single-node household box with UPS; tune G5/G6 to risk.

verify.note: Own policy; PASS rests on N=300.

title: L5: per-store config pin with measured result (copy into Cargo.toml / bootstrap code)
summary: sqlite: rusqlite =0.41.0 (bundled SQLite 3.54.0) PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; synchronous=FULL (EXTRA optional) -> 0/4010 violations. redb: =4.4.0, Database::create then fsync file + parent dir; every WriteTransaction set_durability(Immediate) + set_two_phase_commit(true) -> 0 violations outside create window (0/16k), 1PC+C default also 0 but had 2 recovery-path durability bugs fixed in 4.2/4.3. fjall: =3.1.12 with batch.durability(Some(PersistMode::SyncAll)) -> 0/12030 acked loss; wrap open with cleanup of dir lacking 'version'. heed: =0.23.0 default flags only -> 0 outside create window; ban NO_SYNC/NO_META_SYNC/MAP_ASYNC via clippy-style grep in CI. canopydb: =0.2.5 only with commit_with(true) -> 0/12030; set wal_background_sync_interval explicitly. Not recommended for acked state: redb Durability::None, fjall Buffer, canopydb commit(), SQLite NORMAL, LMDB NO_SYNC. Bootstrap rule (all stores): create dir, create db file, fsync file, fsync parent directory, then serve; redb and LMDB lose the whole database in 15-50% of POSIX-strict creation-window images without it.
specifics: Measured on ext4/nvme, kernel 6.17, rustc 1.98.0.
overclaim_risk: Pins hold for the modelled faults and N=300 only.
underclaim_risk: Latency cost of FULL/2PC unmeasured here (needs separate benchmark on VPS fsync latency).

verify.note: Pins match upstream docs/changelog; latency unmeasured.

title: NEGATIVE: POSIX-literal namespace model (fsfile) reports SQLite DELETE-journal corruption that the ext4-like model does not - regime choice changes verdicts
summary: Same traces, three ns regimes: SQLite del-full corruption classes (atomicity 32, integrity_fail 21, open_fail 24, read_fail 37) appear only in 'fsfile' (create durable at fsync(file), unlink/rename durable only after dir fsync, ops persisted independently and out of order); 0 corruption in 'journal' and 'strict'. redb/LMDB loss appears only in 'strict'. So a harness verdict must name its regime; reporting one number conflates real bugs with model pessimism. Cannot verify against real ext4 here (no root/loop device, no LazyFS build); a dm-log-writes or LazyFS replay on a real fs would arbitrate.
overclaim_risk: Hypothesis for cause (older unlink applied after newer create) unverified.
underclaim_risk: Real filesystems may be this adversarial on btrfs/F2FS (CrashMonkey found rename/fsync bugs there).

verify.note: Artifact explanation unverified.

title: Invariant list ranked by advisories prevented (of 58)
summary: 1. Outbound fetches checked on resolved connected address; redirects strip credentials cross-origin (18); 2. Listener gate: Host allowlist + Origin allowlist (absent Origin treated per credential) + Content-Type application/json, applied at the listener for every route and protocol revision (15); 3. One strict parser shared by policy and backend: reject duplicate/case-variant/NUL/BOM keys; policy evaluates only fully parsed names, unparseable denies (8); 4. Token aud == this resource server, enforced non-optionally; OAuth credentials only to pinned issuer; PRM resource must match (8); 5. Pre-auth and per-request memory bounded: body cap, batch cap, session TTL, no unbounded caches (8); 6. Listener cannot be constructed without authenticator; defaults secure (signature verify, audience) with typed opt-out (8); 7. Principal scoping: every stateful handle (session, task, requestState, response route) is bound to authenticated principal and scope; lookup outside scope returns 404 (7)

title: Origin / audience / session rule set for AEGIS listener
summary: 1) Host in allowlist else 403 (HTTP/1.1 Host and H2 :authority both). 2) Origin present and not allowlisted -> 403; Origin absent allowed only if request carries bearer or mTLS credential. 3) POST Content-Type must be application/json else 415. 4) No ACAO wildcard; preflight only for allowlisted origins. 5) Token aud == canonical resource URI, mandatory, no opt-out in release builds. 6) Any state handle (Mcp-Session-Id if accepted for legacy, task id, requestState, SSE stream) carries (principal, route, backend, policy-version, ttl) and is sealed (AEAD); mismatch -> 404. 7) Under 2026-07-28 no session minting; requestState sealed by default (not opt-in). 8) Rules live in listener type so every protocol revision route inherits them (ToolHive 7h6f). 9) Strict JSON parse shared with policy engine; unparseable -> deny. 10) Egress: resolved-address check at connect, redirects stripped cross-origin, args never from untrusted metadata.
overclaim_risk: Rule 2 absent-Origin conditioning is my design, not tested against real clients
underclaim_risk: Rule 7 default-sealing may be unnecessary if no handler uses requestState

verify.note: Absent-Origin rule interop untested.

title: TLS 1.3 tickets: authenticated (STEK-sealed) yet unscoped state enables client-auth bypass across vhosts (CVE-2025-23419, CVE-2025-23048)
summary: RFC 8446 §4.2.11 says the server need not associate SNI with a ticket; §4.6.1 SNI match is only a client-side SHOULD. Hebrok et al. (USENIX Security 2025, 'STEK Sharing is Not Caring') bypassed client-certificate auth by resuming a ticket issued by a non-mTLS vhost on an mTLS vhost sharing the STEK: nginx CVE-2025-23419 (pub 2025-02-05, 1.11.4+), Apache CVE-2025-23048 (pub 2025-07-10, 2.4.35-2.4.63), (Open)LiteSpeed, Caddy (single global STEK), Cloudflare mTLS (fixed by disabling resumption with mTLS), Fastly (resumed regardless of SNI; fixed 2023-09 by binding ticket to issuing cert). Scan Dec 2024-Jan 2025: 59.75M host pairs, 176 manually confirmed vulnerable. Binding to SNI alone is not enough; bind to server cert chain + client-auth trust config. VERDICT: the invariant as worded is FALSE. The state is authenticated, but authenticated means 'issued by us', not 'issued for this scope'.
overclaim_risk: Most of the 176 confirmed cases need a co-hosted mTLS vhost on the same IP:port. A single-tenant AEGIS listener without client auth is not exposed.
underclaim_risk: Writing this off as 'a TLS-library bug'. Rustls documents that sharing a ticketer/session_storage across ServerConfigs is unenforced policy ('rustls does not enforce any policy here'), so AEGIS inherits the exact hazard.

verify.note: CVEs verified; scan numbers not re-verified; paper also shows server-auth bypass across six provider clusters (Fastly, DDoS-Guard, Variti).

title: STEK lifecycle failures: all-zero key (GnuTLS CVE-2020-13777) and faulty rotation (AWS ALB) turn ticket state into passive-decryption/auth-bypass
summary: Hebrok et al. USENIX Security 2023: AWS ALB's faulty STEK rotation allowed passive decryption for at least 1.9% of the Tranco top-100k. Keystream reuse was also found. GnuTLS 3.6.4-3.6.13 used an all-zero STEK until the first rotation (CVE-2020-13777), which allowed TLS 1.3 auth bypass and passive decryption. Resumption costs about 4% of full-handshake CPU, so the perf gain is real but small. The STEK breaks forward secrecy for the ticket lifetime (max 604800 s per RFC 8446). VERDICT: covered only if 'authenticated' requires a fresh, secret, rotated key. Refine: key provenance and lifetime are part of the invariant.
overclaim_risk: The 1.9% figure is ALB-specific (2023).
underclaim_risk: Treating PQC KEM handshakes as making tickets safe: a ticket resumption skips the ML-KEM exchange entirely and relies on the symmetric STEK (and an optional psk_dhe_ke share), so the PQ property of resumed sessions equals the STEK's handling.

verify.note: CVE-2020-13777 and 1.9% verified ("AWS ecosystem"); resumption skips ML-KEM only for psk_ke, not psk_dhe_ke.

title: 0-RTT early data: authenticated but replayable; RFC 8446 §8 allows 'billions of replays' within the freshness window
summary: RFC 8446 §8: a server MUST accept the same 0-RTT handshake at most once per instance, but cross-instance replay remains, and application-level replay 'MUST be dealt with by any application'. The §8.3 freshness window is about 10 s. RFC 9001 §9.2: 'Disabling 0-RTT entirely is the most effective defense'; tickets/tokens MUST NOT carry application semantics. RFC 8470: intermediaries MUST add Early-Data: 1; origins return 425 Too Early; clients MUST retry. No dedicated CVE for QUIC-server 0-RTT anti-replay was found (negative result). Holz et al. (arXiv 1907.12762): 6.8% of TLS 1.3 connections carry early_data, but whether servers accept it cannot be observed passively. VERDICT: REFINE. The invariant needs a freshness/at-most-once clause, because the input is authenticated and still unsafe.
overclaim_risk: Replay needs a non-idempotent route reachable in early data. With GET-only early data plus 425, the risk is small.
underclaim_risk: The absence of CVEs reflects that acceptance is unobservable, not that the risk is absent.

verify.note: Negative CVE result supported; missed curl CURL-CVE-2026-9545 (HTTP/3 early data to impostor); RFC 9308 notes accepted 0-RTT cannot be selectively discarded.

title: Contrarian: QUIC NEW_TOKEN/Retry tokens are spec-sanctioned UNAUTHENTICATED cross-connection state
summary: RFC 9000 §8.1.3/8.1.4: NEW_TOKEN tokens 'are not integrated into the cryptographic handshake, and so they are not authenticated'. Their use is limited to address validation; they must be unique per client and SHOULD expire. Rate-limit counters, DNS caches, hash tables and public caches are likewise necessary state that unauthenticated input influences. VERDICT: the invariant is TOO STRONG as a prohibition. Replace it with an authority ceiling. State that unauthenticated input influences may only affect resource budgets and address validation, never authorization or another principal's response bytes.
underclaim_risk: Dropping the invariant because of these exceptions. They all share one property: a capped, non-authorizing influence.

verify.note: RFC text confirmed.

title: HTTP/2/3 connection coalescing: connection-level authority decisions reused for requests to other origins
summary: RFC 9113 §9.1.1 lets one connection serve several authorities when the cert covers them. RFC 9110 §7.4: the origin MUST reject a request not received on a connection secured with a cert valid for the target origin (421 Misdirected Request). draft-rajappa-httpbis-connection-contamination: routing decided once at connection setup misroutes coalesced requests across tenants. Delignat-Lavaud & Bhargavan (WWW 2015) broke OAuth on Akamai-hosted sites through virtual-host confusion. Contour issue #5240 (2023-04-03): a wildcard cert plus coalescing gives 421, and Safari gets stuck because the retry is only a MAY. VERDICT: REFINE. Anything derived from the connection (SNI vhost, client-cert verification, routing) must be re-checked per request against :authority.
overclaim_risk: The rajappa draft could not be fetched (404); the claim rests on the search summary only.
underclaim_risk: A 421 is a liveness cost; send an ORIGIN frame (RFC 8336) to avoid clients stalling.

verify.note: 421 confirmed; Contour/WWW2015 not re-verified; curl CVE-2026-87861/8458 support per-request recheck.

title: Web cache poisoning/deception: unkeyed inputs and parser/normalization differentials (PortSwigger 2024; Next.js CVE-2026-44572, CVE-2025-49005)
summary: Doyhenard, 'Gotta cache em all' (PortSwigger, BH USA 2024-08-08): delimiter discrepancies (Spring ';', Rails '.', OpenLiteSpeed %00, nginx %0a) and normalization discrepancies. CloudFront/Azure/Imperva normalize before applying cache rules; Cloudflare/GCP/Fastly do not. Next.js CVE-2026-44572 (pub 2026-05-13; 12.2.0-<15.5.16, 16.0-<16.2.5): a client-sent internal header x-nextjs-data rewrote the redirect, and one request poisoned the CDN's cached redirect. CVE-2025-49005 (pub 2025-07-03; 15.3.0-<15.3.3): a missing Vary served the RSC payload as HTML. Varnish CVE-2021-36740: H2 smuggling led to poisoning. HCache (Tsinghua, reportedly CCS 2024; secondary source): about 17% of Tranco top-1000 domains vulnerable. RFC 9111 §7.1 names parsing differentials as the root cause; §3.5 forbids shared reuse of Authorization responses unless explicitly public; §7.3 notes Set-Cookie does not inhibit caching. VERDICT: COVERED in spirit. Unauthenticated input influences shared state, but it needs a key-completeness and single-parser rule to be checkable.
overclaim_risk: The HCache prevalence number is grade C (not fetched).
underclaim_risk: AEGIS-as-origin is exposed even without its own cache, because downstream CDNs key differently. Ingress stripping of internal headers is mandatory.

verify.note: Next.js CVEs both CVSS 3.7 LOW; CVE-2025-49005 CWE-444; Varnish CVE-2021-36740 is smuggling not cache key; HCache 17% unchecked.

title: HPACK/QPACK dynamic tables: cross-request compression state shared between mutually distrustful but possibly AUTHENTICATED principals
summary: RFC 7541 §7.1.1-7.1.3: the dynamic table is cross-request state. Anyone who can inject headers and observe lengths can probe it, and the risk applies whenever 'two mutually distrustful entities' share a connection, e.g. an intermediary multiplexing several clients upstream. The ideal is to segregate tables per entity; sensitive headers go never-indexed. HEIST (BH USA 2016) showed cross-origin length oracles. VERDICT: FALSE-as-stated. Both principals may be authenticated. The right axis is principal partitioning, not authentication.
overclaim_risk: Server-side tables are per-connection, so the risk arises only in AEGIS's upstream proxy fan-out.
underclaim_risk: QPACK has the same structure (see rec60-header-accordions-qpack for its DoS face).

verify.note: RFC 7541 §7.1 only; no field CVE; proxies keep per-connection contexts (but see r2e11.h3-proxy-qpack-sidechannel).

title: Connection-pool reuse with hand-enumerated keys: the curl 2026 CVE cluster, curl CVE-2024-0853 failed-validation caching, response-queue poisoning
summary: curl vuln.json (fetched 2026-10-24) has 16 connection/session-reuse CVEs in 2026 alone, against 1-3 per year in 2014-2024. Examples: CVE-2026-8932 (private-key options missing from the mTLS reuse match), CVE-2026-80231 (native CA store not in the key), CVE-2026-107929 (bind interface not in the key), CVE-2026-87861 (cross-origin Negotiate reuse), CVE-2026-4873 (reuse ignores the TLS requirement). Root cause: a hand-maintained field list that omits newly added config. CVE-2024-0853 (curl 8.5.0) kept a session ID after OCSP verification FAILED, so the later transfer skipped the check. CVE-2016-5419: resumption after a client cert change. Kettle (BH USA 2021): response-queue poisoning through upstream connection reuse (Netty CVE-2021-21295; Jira global session mix-up). hyper-util 0.1.21 (2026-09-24) legacy Client uses `type PoolKey = (Scheme, Authority)` (client.rs l.95). It omits SNI override, client identity, CA store and tenant. VERDICT: REFINE. Add (a) key completeness by construction, (b) failure non-population, (c) drain on framing error.
overclaim_risk: The 2026 curl spike may partly be an AI-assisted audit wave (more found, not more created).
underclaim_risk: Assuming hyper-util's key is sufficient. It is safe only while every connection to a (scheme, authority) is identical in TLS identity.

verify.note: curl 2026 cluster broader than 16 (69 CVE-2026 entries, ~18-20 reuse/state); CVE-2026-8932/80231/2024-0853 and hyper-util PoolKey line 95 verified.

title: Idempotency store keyed by client-chosen value: cross-client retrieval (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-08 §5)
summary: Draft -08 (updated 2026-10-22) §5: with low-entropy keys, attackers can guess other clients' keys and retrieve cached responses. The draft RECOMMENDS a composite key of the client key plus client-specific attributes. §2.4: MAY fingerprint the payload; reuse with a different payload SHOULD return 422. VERDICT: REFINE. The key must include the authenticated principal; the client key alone is not authenticated state.
underclaim_risk: The draft only RECOMMENDS this. AEGIS should make it a MUST in the store's type signature.

verify.note: Draft -08 current.

title: JWKS caches mutated by an unverified kid: PyJWT CVE-2026-48524 (cache cleared on fetch error), CVE-2026-101917 (no negative cache)
summary: PyJWT <2.13.0 (pub 2026-05-28): an unknown kid read from the UNVERIFIED header forces a JWKS refetch, and a finally-block clears the cache on network error, causing cascading auth failure. <2.14.0 (pub 2026-09-28): no negative cache or minimum refresh interval. libjwt added a cooldown. VERDICT: CONFIRMS the invariant. An unauthenticated field drives mutation of shared state. It also adds the rule that a failed operation must not destroy last-good state.
overclaim_risk: CVE-2026-101917 was seen via the advisory listing and not refetched from MITRE this session.

verify.note: PyJWT CVEs are amplification DoS (no negative cache); cache-cleared-on-error/evict-last-good sub-claim unsupported.

title: Rate-limiter state keyed on spoofable X-Forwarded-For (Litestar CVE-2025-59152, Lemmy CVE-2026-54738, 9Router CVE-2026-55501)

Refine 'authenticated' to include transport-authenticated attributes (socket peer, or the rightmost untrusted hop of a validated trusted-proxy chain).

verify.note: Three CVEs confirmed across Python/Rust/JS; Lemmy root cause in actix-web ConnectionInfo.

title: DNS resolution cached between validation and connect: SSRF rebinding TOCTOU cluster 2026 (MCP Atlassian CVE-2026-73497, ContextForge CVE-2026-53708, datamodel-code-generator CVE-2026-55391)
summary: Validation resolves the name and checks the IP, then the client re-resolves at connect time and an attacker-controlled DNS answer changes. The fix is for validation to return the pinned IP that the connect uses, on every client path including redirects. VERDICT: REFINE. Add a time-of-use binding clause: the state checked must be the state used.

verify.note: Three CVEs confirmed in niche projects; one is a fix bypass.

title: Session fixation and auth-change survival: pre-auth state carried across a privilege boundary
summary: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet: regenerate the session ID after any privilege change, and never accept IDs the server did not generate. The same pattern shows up in curl CVE-2016-5419 (resumption after a client cert change) and the Hebrok 2025 mTLS bypass (state from a lower-assurance context reused in a higher one). VERDICT: REFINE. Add an epoch clause: state is bound to an auth-context epoch, and any auth change invalidates it.

verify.note: CVE-2016-5419 is resumption-after-cert-change; curl 2026 86411/86415 add fresher evidence.

title: Contrarian: hash tables are cross-request state influenced by unauthenticated keys; the defense is secret keying, not authentication
summary: HashDoS (CVE-2011-4885 class). Rust std HashMap uses keyed SipHash-1-3 (RandomState); foldhash is 'minimally DoS-resistant' and FxHash not at all. VERDICT: outside the prohibition, inside the authority ceiling (clause C7). Any map keyed by attacker input uses a secret-keyed hasher.

verify.note: Docs-only; textbook.

title: rustls ServerConfig: ticketer/session_storage sharing across configs is unenforced ('rustls does not enforce any policy here')
summary: The rustls 0.23.46 docs warn that sharing a ticketer or session_storage between ServerConfigs with different verifiers or cert resolvers is the caller's responsibility. AEGIS must therefore build one ticketer per (cert chain, client-auth verifier, config epoch) and make resumption impossible across those boundaries. For mTLS listeners the simplest safe choice is resumption off (Cloudflare's fix), at about 4% CPU cost per reconnect according to Hebrok 2023.
underclaim_risk: Not verifying that rustls binds tickets to SNI or the cert internally. Assume it does not; add the scope to the ticket AAD ourselves through a wrapping ProducesTickets.

verify.note: API claim supported only by generic docs; design untested.

title: Verdict matrix: 'no unauthenticated cross-request state' across 14 counterexample classes is false as stated, too strong as a prohibition, and right in spirit
summary: COVERED (unauthenticated input mutated shared state): cache poisoning/deception, JWKS kid refetch, XFF limiter. FALSE (authenticated state, wrong scope): TLS tickets across vhosts, HPACK across principals. REFINE (missing freshness, time-of-use or epoch): 0-RTT replay, coalescing, pool reuse, idempotency, DNS rebinding, session fixation, STEK lifecycle. TOO STRONG: QUIC tokens, rate counters, hash tables. Tally: 3 covered, 2 false-as-stated, 7 refine, 3 too strong (QUIC token counted once; hashdos in too-strong). The common root cause across all 14: a state lookup key or scope tuple that is a strict subset of the inputs that determine the authorization or response. 'Authenticated' must mean scope-bound, fresh and current-epoch; 'unauthenticated' input may influence only resource budgets.
overclaim_risk: The classes are drawn from the attacker literature; frequency weighting per class is not established.
underclaim_risk: Calling this just another checklist. The single root cause (key is a subset of the determining inputs) is mechanically testable.

verify.note: verifier sampled other nodes; explorer grade kept

title: Refined invariant CRS (Cross-Request State) with clauses C1-C8 and definitions
summary: DEFINITIONS. Cross-request state = any state that outlives the request that created it and can affect a later request's processing or response. It exists at four levels: connection (TLS session, H2/H3 stream tables, HPACK/QPACK), process (caches, pools, counters, maps), fleet (STEK, shared cache, idempotency/session store), and client-held server-issued (tickets, NEW_TOKEN, cookies, idempotency keys). Authenticated = this server verified a cryptographic binding at the time of use, under a current, non-default key and the current policy epoch, to a scope tuple sigma = (issuer cert-chain hash, origin/authority, principal/tenant or PUBLIC, auth context {client-cert trust store id, auth method, privilege level}, config epoch). Transport-authenticated attributes (socket peer, verified client cert) authenticate only what they prove. CLAUSES. C1 Provenance: server-issued state is AEAD-sealed under a CSPRNG key that is rotated (STEK at most 24 h with a 2-key window; ticket lifetime at most 24 h, below the 7 d spec max). Startup refuses an all-zero or default key. C2 Scope: state S may influence request R only if sigma(S) == sigma(R), with sigma(R) computed per request (not per connection) and equality on every component. PUBLIC is allowed only for responses the origin marked public, with no Authorization or Set-Cookie. C3 Key completeness: every input that can change the response bytes or the authorization outcome is in the lookup key, or is stripped or normalized at ingress by the SAME parser the router and origin use. C4 Freshness: state that authorizes a side effect is single-use, or the effect is idempotent. Early data is accepted only on routes marked replay_safe, with at-most-once per ticket per instance, Early-Data: 1 forwarded, and 425 otherwise. C5 Epoch revocation: any auth or config change (login, logout, privilege change, cert/CA rotation, reload) bumps the epoch. Old-epoch state is rejected; session IDs are regenerated and pooled upstream connections drained. C6 Failure atomicity: failed validation never inserts or retains state, and a failed refresh never evicts last-good state. C7 Authority ceiling: state influenced by unauthenticated input may affect only resource budgets and address validation. Its size is capped per transport-authenticated key, refreshes triggered by unverified fields are rate-limited and negatively cached, and maps over attacker keys use secret-keyed hashing. C8 Shared-context partitioning: compression contexts, upstream connections and response queues are never shared between principals. Sensitive headers are never-indexed, and the upstream connection is closed on any framing error.

title: Keying rule for every cache/ticket/pool in AEGIS
summary: TLS tickets/session cache: one ticketer per (cert-chain hash, client-auth verifier id, ALPN set, epoch). The scope hash goes in the ticket AAD and is checked on decrypt. Resumption is disabled on mTLS listeners by default. 0-RTT: off by default; max_early_data_size>0 only if the listener has replay_safe routes; an anti-replay set of (ticket nonce, obfuscated age) per instance for the freshness window. QUIC NEW_TOKEN/Retry: AEAD(client IP, issue time, expiry 24 h), consulted only for address validation. H2/H3 per-request authority: :authority is in the SAN of THIS connection's cert AND maps to the same vhost/trust config as the SNI, else 421; send an ORIGIN frame. HPACK/QPACK upstream: per-principal upstream connection, or dynamic table 0 when multiplexing principals; Authorization/Cookie never-indexed. Response cache: key = (method, scheme, authority, router-canonical path [same parser], canonical query, values of Vary-listed headers, response variant [e.g. RSC vs HTML], principal or PUBLIC, epoch). Ingress strips the internal header namespace by allowlist; no extension-based rules override origin Cache-Control. Upstream pool: key = the entire UpstreamConnConfig struct via derive(Hash, Eq) (scheme, host, port, pinned IP, SNI, ALPN, client identity, CA store id, TLS min, proxy, bind iface, epoch). Excluding a field requires an explicit #[pool_key(skip, reason=...)] attribute; do not use hyper-util's (Scheme, Authority) PoolKey directly when TLS identity varies. Idempotency store: (principal id, route template, client key) to (request fingerprint, response); fingerprint mismatch returns 422. JWKS: (issuer from static config, kid). Unknown kid triggers at most 1 fetch per 5 min per issuer, with a negative cache; last-good keys are kept on error. Rate limiter: socket peer, or the rightmost untrusted hop of a validated trusted-proxy chain; never raw XFF. DNS/egress: the connector resolves, checks the IP against policy and connects to that exact IP; no re-resolve; recheck on every redirect. Sessions: server-generated only, regenerated on privilege change, epoch-bound. Hash maps keyed by attacker input: std RandomState (SipHash).
overclaim_risk: The JWKS interval and token expiry values are choices.

title: Test-oracle spec per CRS clause (DST/property/differential harness)
summary: C1: unit test that a startup with a zero or default STEK fails, plus a rotation property: a ticket under a key older than 2 rotations is rejected. C2: a two-scope differential harness for EVERY state type. Issue the artifact under scope A, present it under scope B (different vhost on the same IP:port, different client CA, different principal); expect a full handshake, cache miss or new upstream connection. Include the nginx CVE-2025-23419 replica as a named regression: two vhosts on one IP:port, one with mTLS; resuming the non-mTLS ticket must still demand a client cert. C3: cache-key completeness fuzzer. For each request field (every header, path variants with ; . %00 %0a %2f %23 .. and case, query order), mutate it and compare origin responses. Response differs but cache key unchanged means FAIL. Also a router-vs-cache canonicalization differential: one parser, assert identical output. C4: replay the same 0-RTT ClientHello N=1000 times at one instance, expect at most 1 acceptance; a non-replay_safe route in early data returns 425; with the proxy, Early-Data: 1 is present upstream. C5: after rotating the client CA, logging out, changing a role or reloading config, the old ticket, session ID and pooled connection must all fail to be reused (epoch counter assertion). C6: fault injection. A forced validation failure leaves the store snapshot byte-identical; a JWKS network error keeps the last-good key verifying. C7: an adversarial load of 10k req/s unknown-kid gives at most 1 upstream JWKS fetch per interval; rotating XFF gives the same limiter bucket; state bytes stay at or under the cap per peer. C8: two downstream principals through the proxy share no upstream connection IDs (or dynamic table size = 0); injecting malformed upstream framing closes the connection before the next request is dequeued. CI gate: all oracles run in the DST suite (as.dst-harness-spec), and oracle mutation (as.oracle-mutation) must show each one can fail. For example, removing the epoch from the pool key must turn C5 red.
underclaim_risk: Skipping the oracle-mutation step. Key-completeness tests are classically vacuous when the mutation set misses the one field that matters.

title: Gap: no internet-scale measurement of 0-RTT replay acceptance; implementation-phase spike
summary: Passive scans cannot observe acceptance (Holz et al. 2019). Spike protocol: an AEGIS listener with rustls/quinn 0-RTT enabled.
