title: RLS plan-cache / role-change CVE family (2016-2026)
summary: Recurring bug class: cached or inlined plans keep applying policies of a prior role after user-id changes. CVE-2016-2193 (pub 2016-04-11), CVE-2023-2455 (2023-06-09, inlining; 14.8/15.3), CVE-2024-10976 (2024-11-14; subquery/WITH/security-invoker view/SQL function; 17.1/16.5/15.9/14.14/13.17/12.21; CVSS ~4.2-5.4 per source), CVE-2026-14666 (published 2026-08-13; cached RLS policies survive role membership/attribute/db-ownership changes; fixed 18.6/17.11/16.15/15.19/14.24; CVSS 4.2 AV:N/AC:H/PR:L; stale policies persist until invalidation or connection end). All need role switching inside one backend session with plan reuse - exactly what SET ROLE + pooled connections do. CVE-2023-39418 (MERGE skips UPDATE/SELECT policies, 15.4). All verified in cveawg.mitre.org.
specifics: L5: never change role on a connection that will run prepared/cached statements for another principal; one backend session = one principal for its lifetime OR use SET LOCAL ROLE only inside a txn on a connection whose plan cache is invalidated (DISCARD PLANS/ DEALLOCATE ALL) - and still treat as defense-in-depth not primary gate. Pin Postgres >= 18.6/17.11/16.15 (and subscribe to security list).
overclaim_risk: Over: CVSS 4.2 understates impact for a multi-tenant gate (confidentiality of other tenants' rows).
underclaim_risk: Under: exploitation needs app-specific plan reuse pattern; no public exploitation found.

title: Transaction-pooling session-state leak class (SET ROLE / GUC / advisory locks)
summary: In transaction pooling the backend is reassigned between clients; session state set by one principal can reach the next. PgBouncer docs: SET/RESET 'Never' safe in transaction mode, server_reset_query (DISCARD ALL) not run in transaction pooling, track_extra_parameters default tracks session_authorization, search_path (PG18+) etc but not role. PgDog open issues: #1850 (2026-10-18) search_path/statement_timeout/TimeZone leak to next client via SET inside txn, multi-statement queries, set_config(), DO blocks; #1341 (2026-08-11, v0.1.52) SET ROLE leaks current_user because RESET ALL skips GUC_NO_RESET_ALL role (fix PR #1444 adds RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION); #1407 session advisory locks leak. Supavisor PR #1113 (merged 2026-07-22) adds opt-in txn_mode_leak_action detecting session SET, set_config(..,false), DISCARD, session advisory locks, LISTEN, WITH HOLD cursors, temp tables, LOAD (default 'ignore'). Safe pattern: all identity via SET LOCAL / set_config(...,true) inside an explicit txn; ban session-level state at the protocol/AST layer; or avoid third-party pooler by owning the pool in the gateway.
specifics: L5 invariant INV-NOSESSIONSTATE: after any statement the backend's session-level GUC/role/lock/prepared state equals the pool baseline; enforced by (1) rejecting non-LOCAL SET, set_config(,,false), DISCARD, LISTEN, advisory session locks, WITH HOLD, temp tables, LOAD at AST level, (2) DISCARD ALL + RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION on check-in, (3) canary test: client A sets everything, client B asserts baseline.

title: DST determinism hazards verified in source: aws-lc raw syscall, getrandom 0.2, rustls SecureRandom scope
summary: Own source verification (registry sources, 2026-10-24): aws-lc-sys 0.46.0 crypto/rand_extra/urandom.c calls syscall(__NR_getrandom,...) directly => not interceptable by libc symbol overrides (mad-turmoil overrides getrandom/getentropy/clock_gettime at libc level). getrandom 0.2.17 on Linux uses raw syscall (util_libc::getrandom_syscall) => bypass; getrandom 0.3.4/0.4.3 call libc::getrandom (dlsym on non-musl, static on musl) => interposable only in some configurations. rustls 0.23.46 docs: SecureRandom is used for all randomness required by rustls "but not necessarily randomness required by the underlying cryptography library"; TimeProvider is injectable (time_provider.rs). Consequence: a rustls handshake inside a madsim/mad-turmoil-style sim is NOT deterministic by default; S2 documented HashMap RandomState as an unresolved dependency hazard.

title: 'Failed request => no state mutation': DB txn vs CoW write buffer vs saga
summary: Evidence ranking: (a) single DB transaction per request is the strongest existence proof - PostgREST runs every request in one transaction (default READ COMMITTED), SET LOCAL ROLE + set_config(...,true), COMMIT unless error, all queries prepared. Limits that break the invariant even there: sequences/nextval and setval are never rolled back (PG docs), side effects outside DB, ambiguous commit when connection drops after COMMIT sent, 40001 serialization failures require whole-txn retry (docs), Jepsen found Postgres 12.3 serializable G2-item anomaly present since 2011 (fixed Aug 2020) and RDS Multi-AZ 17.4 Long Fork on reader endpoint. (b) In-process per-request CoW buffer (stage writes, flush at success) gives atomicity only for the buffered store and only if flush itself is atomic - reduces to (a) at flush; no independent verification evidence found for a CoW-buffer-as-isolation design; Cloudflare output gates are the closest production analogue (response held until storage ack). (c) Sagas: compensations are semantic not physical, need durable execution to guarantee they run (CIDR26); suitable for cross-system effects, not for local state. Conclusion: invariant must be stated as 'no committed DB mutation unless the request reached its commit point; external effects only after commit via outbox or idempotent key', with sequences and ambiguous commit explicitly carved out.
specifics: L5 invariant text: INV-NOMUT: for every request r with outcome != Committed, the set of durable user-visible rows changed by r is empty, modulo {sequence values, advisory-lock side effects, pg_stat counters}; proven by construction (one txn per request, no autonomous commits, no COMMIT from handler code), tested by DST with injected failure at every await point.
overclaim_risk: Over: 'atomic request' claims ignoring ambiguous commit and sequences.
underclaim_risk: Under: single-txn-per-request is cheap and well-evidenced.

title: L5: Lean 4 core model + theorem statements for IR filter lowering soundness (refinement-parameterised)
summary: Core-only Lean 4 (no Mathlib/Batteries) model of the IR filter fragment (tt/ff/eq/in/range/prefix/and/or/not; n-ary And[]=tt, Or[]=ff), a Kleene 3VL mini-SQL WHERE semantics, the structural lowering, and soundness theorems parameterised by a Backend record of the engine's primitive comparisons. Key insight: lowering soundness reduces to per-adapter REFINEMENT facts (backend eq/range/prefix true => reference true); the connective/NULL part is engine-independent and provable once. A counter-theorem shows refinement is necessary (any coarser equality, e.g. NOCASE, affinity 1='1', ICU NFC=NFD, PAD SPACE, yields a leak).
specifics:
File research/state/raw/round-003/01-work/lean/AegisIR/Lowering.lean, 262 lines / 232 non-blank-non-comment; lakefile.lean + lean-toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0.
THEOREMS: (T1) lower_sound_pos {B} (h : B.Refines) r : ∀ p, p.positive = true → sql3 B r (lower p) = some true → eval r p = true. (T2) lowerQ_sound: keeps B r (lowerQ tf t p) = true → refQ tf t r p = true (mandatory tenant conjunct). (T3) refines_necessary: x ≠ t → B.beq x t = true → ∃ r, keeps B r (lowerQ tf t .tt) ∧ ¬refQ. (T4) lower_sound_full (with NOT) under Backend.Exact (two-sided atoms) — stated, `sorry` (~40 LOC). (T5) orN_nil / andN_nil by rfl. Helper lemmas k3and_true, k3or_true, anyEq_sound.
Backend.Refines := {eq_ok : beq x v → x = v; range_ok : brange lo hi x → refRange lo hi x; pfx_ok : bpfx s x → refPrefix s x}.

WHERE cond, Put cond) reuse T2 + ~60. Total ~630 LOC ≈ 2-4 engineer-days at Cedar's ratio (3.4:1 proof:model; proof-cedar-lean).

title: L5: executed differential oracle for IR lowerings (reference evaluator vs native rows) + seed corpus + CI gate
summary: Python harness (stdlib sqlite3 + psycopg2) generating typed rows with adversarial values and random IR predicates, running each adapter's lowered query and the strict reference evaluator over the STORED values, and reporting LEAK (unsound) vs MISS (incomplete). It found unsoundness in every naive lowering and also caught a leak in my own first 'hardened' SQLite lowering (NUMERIC-affinity param coercion), which is the evidence that the oracle is a necessary instrument rather than a formality.
specifics:
Files: 01-work/oracle.py (IR, reference, SQLite/PG/Redis adapters), cex.py (78 single-cause cases), oracle_typed.py, cost.py, q1012_repro.py; results *.json alongside.
SEED CORPUS: tenants ['acme','ACME','Acme','acme ','acmé', NFD('acmé'),'1','01','a%','a_','a\\','évil','ǅ','ß','ss']; values [0,1,2,10,-1,1.0,2.5,'1','10','2','a','A','ab','AB','a%b','a_b','ä',NFD('ä'),'',' ','z',NULL]; Redis tenants ['acme','acme:x','a*','a?','a[b]','[ab]','a\\','a\\*','ab','abc','a','','*','a:b:c','x]','^','a-c','ACME','acmé']; extra probe 'acme\x00evil'. Seeds 1,2,3,20261025; 400 rows; 3000 cases/SQLite schema, 1500/PG schema.
MEASURED (SQLite 3.45.3, PG 17.11 + 19rc1 containers): naive-bound lowering LEAK in 1004-1492/3000 SQLite cases, 282-307 (PG default collation), 481-495 (citext), 518-577 (nondet ICU, PG17; 305-346 LIKE errors fail-closed) and 725 on PG19rc1 (LIKE now allowed on nondeterministic collations). Hardened lowerings: 0 LEAK / 0 MISS on all 4 seeds x 4 SQLite schemas x 3 PG schemas. Redis: naive 10/19 tenants leak, escaped-but-':'-delimited 3/19, length-prefixed 0, hex {hash-tag} 0.

CI GATE (proposed): `xtask oracle --adapter <a> --engine-pin <ver> --cases 100000 --seeds 4` must report leak_cases=0 for the golden adapters; re-run on every engine minor bump (PG minor, SQLite amalgamation, Redis/Valkey tag); any MISS>0 is a warning; the 78-case cex corpus runs as unit tests. title: L5: per-adapter unsound-lowering denylist + mandated hardened forms (SQLite, Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, Redis/Valkey, MongoDB)
summary: Build-time rule set the lowering compiler and the allowlist generator must enforce; each entry is tied to an executed counterexample (A) or a primary doc (B).
specifics:
SQLite (A): DENY LIKE/GLOB for Prefix (ASCII case-fold, '_'/'%' wildcards, no default ESCAPE, NUL terminates: 'acme\0evil' LIKE 'acme' = 1); DENY columns with COLLATE NOCASE/RTRIM for tenant or filter fields unless every comparison carries COLLATE BINARY; DENY comparing a literal whose IR class differs from column affinity (TEXT col vs int literal; NUMERIC col vs text literal: ''>=10 true); REQUIRE typeof(col)=<class> guard + COLLATE BINARY, Prefix via substr(col,1,n)=? ; PREFER STRICT tables with declared type == IR field type (then index-friendly form is sound; schema-agnostic unary-+ form is sound but 5,000x slower).
Postgres (A): DENY nondeterministic collations (ICU deterministic=false: case/accent-insensitive AND canonical-equivalence NFC==NFD) and citext on tenant/filter columns, or force COLLATE "C" on every text comparison; DENY LIKE for Prefix (use left(col,n) = ? COLLATE "C"); DENY Range on text under libc/ICU locale collations unless COLLATE "C" (glibc en_US.utf8: 'A' BETWEEN 'a' AND 'b' = true); IN-list as = ANY($1::text[]) ('IN ()' is a syntax error = fail-closed). Note PG18+ made LIKE legal on nondeterministic collations: an error that failed closed on 17 becomes a leak on 18/19.
MySQL/MariaDB (B, not executed): DENY default *_ci/_ai_ci collations and PAD SPACE collations (incl. utf8mb4_bin: 'a ' = 'a') on tenant/filter fields; REQUIRE utf8mb4_0900_bin (NO PAD) or BINARY/VARBINARY columns, or COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_bin on comparisons; LIKE escaping depends on sql_mode NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES -> always emit explicit ESCAPE.
SQL Server (B): DENY LIKE without explicit ESCAPE (no default escape; '[' ']' '^' are live wildcards); default *_CI_AS collation case-insensitive -> REQUIRE *_BIN2 column or COLLATE Latin1_General_100_BIN2_UTF8 on comparisons; trailing blanks ignored in = (ANSI padding) -> tenant ids must be fixed-format (e.g. hex/uuid) or compared with DATALENGTH guard.
Redis/Valkey (A): DENY raw tenant text inside SCAN MATCH / KEYS / ACL %R~ patterns (same stringmatchlen matcher in db.c and acl.c); DENY ':'-delimited unescaped prefixes (tenant 'acme' matches 'acme:x' keys); REQUIRE tenant encoded over a metachar-free alphabet with a terminator: t:{<hex(tenant)>}:<suffix> (also pins cluster slot) or length-prefixed + glob-escaped.
MongoDB (B): DENY implicit {f: v} form (regex value becomes $regex) -> always {f:{$eq:v}}; DENY reliance on $type:'string' for type exactness (matches arrays containing strings); REQUIRE tenant guard {tenant:{$eq:t}} AND {tenant:{$not:{$type:'array'}}} (implicit array membership makes ['acme','evil'] visible to both); numeric literals carry {$type:<exact>} when the IR distinguishes int/double/decimal (all numerics compare equal); every find/aggregate passes collation {locale:'simple'} (collection default collation is inherited otherwise); never pass a NULL literal (matches missing fields and arrays containing null); $where/$function/$accumulator/$expr never from request data.
ALL: Or([]) MUST render FALSE and And([]) TRUE; any builder that drops empty sub-expressions (go-sqlbuilder Cond.Or, SQLAlchemy or_(), ucast-prisma 0.1.6) is forbidden in the lowering path.
overclaim_risk: MySQL/SQL Server/Mongo entries are doc-derived (B), not executed; denylist completeness is not provable (new collations/planner features appear, cf. PG18 LIKE).
underclaim_risk: Every SQLite/PG/Redis entry has a concrete executed leak; these are the exact failure modes generic query builders and policy-to-SQL compilers ship today.

verify.note: Only SQLite/PG/Redis executed; MySQL/SQL Server/Mongo doc-derived (B). MySQL LIKE treats trailing spaces as significant regardless of PAD, narrowing PAD SPACE hazard to =/IN/range.

title: L5: adapter refinement contract (the TCB line between Lean proof and engine) + startup schema gate
summary: Each adapter ships (a) the Lean-side Backend instance it claims, (b) a schema precondition checker run at build time and at startup against the live catalog, (c) the oracle corpus result at the pinned engine version. The core accepts an adapter only if all three are present; this is what makes 'soundness by proof' honest about what is trusted.
specifics:
trait AdapterContract { const ENGINE_PIN: &str; fn refinement_claims() -> RefinementClaims /* eq_exact, range_codepoint, prefix_exact per field type */; fn check_schema(&Catalog) -> Result<(), SchemaViolation> /* SQLite: PRAGMA table_xinfo + sqlite_schema parse: STRICT, declared type == IR type, no NOCASE/RTRIM; PG: pg_attribute.attcollation in {C, POSIX, or deterministic + COLLATE C emitted}, no citext, collprovider/collisdeterministic; MySQL: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS COLLATION_NAME in allowlist with PAD_ATTRIBUTE='NO PAD'; SQL Server: sys.columns collation_name like '%BIN2%'; Mongo: listCollections options.collation absent or simple, $jsonSchema bsonType for tenant */; fn oracle_report() -> &'static OracleReport /* leak_cases == 0, corpus hash, engine version */ }.
Startup refuses to serve the adapter if check_schema fails or the live engine version != ENGINE_PIN major.minor (PG minor >= 18.6/17.11 for CVE-2026-14666). Lean side: one `instance : Backend.Refines (sqliteStrictBackend)` axiom per adapter, named in the TCB ledger.
overclaim_risk: Design, unimplemented; catalog introspection itself can be wrong (e.g., expression-level COLLATE in views/generated columns).
underclaim_risk: Hasura NDC already normatively requires 'equal' = syntactic equality, so the contract shape has precedent; it just was never machine-checked.

verify.note: Design only; NDC spec supports syntactic-equality idea, not the contract; PG minor floor relevant to CVE only.

title: L5: executed q1-012 reproducer — SET LOCAL ROLE + named prepared statements + plan cache on PG 17.11 / 19rc1 (DISCARD PLANS not needed for role switching)
summary: On patched Postgres, switching SET LOCAL ROLE per transaction on one pooled connection while reusing a named prepared statement never leaked across 8 alternations in all three plan_cache_modes; revoking role membership or BYPASSRLS while a plan is cached was also honoured (CVE-2026-14666 fix). A positive control (session-level set_config not reset between requests) leaked in every mode, proving the harness detects leaks.
specifics:
q1012_repro.py scenarios x plan_cache_mode {auto (after 6 warm-up executions), force_generic_plan, force_custom_plan}: S1 SET LOCAL ROLE tenant_a/tenant_b alternating x8 with `PREPARE q` reused: PASS; S1b after COMMIT executing as NOINHERIT authenticator: permission error (fail-closed); S2 member of grp_all (policy TO grp_all USING true) -> REVOKE while cached: PASS (0 rows after); S3 BYPASSRLS -> NOBYPASSRLS while cached: PASS; S4 policy on current_setting('app.tenant', true) with set_config(...,true): PASS; S4b set_config(...,false) leaks to the next request: LEAK (control). Same on PostgreSQL 17.11 (Debian 17.11-1.pgdg13+2) and 19rc1.
DECISION: (1) SET LOCAL ROLE per txn + prepared statements is safe on >= 17.11/18.6 because plancache revalidates when rewriteRoleId != current user for dependsOnRLS plans; DISCARD PLANS buys nothing for role switches. (2) On < 17.11 / 18.6 a membership/attribute/db-owner change does not invalidate cached RLS plans until another inval or disconnect -> gate: refuse to start on older minors, or recycle pooled connections after any role DDL. (3) GUC-keyed tenancy must use is_local=true (SET LOCAL) only; session-level SET is the measured leak. CI: run q1012_repro.py against each pinned PG minor and PG beta.
SPIKE SPK-PG-14666-UNPATCHED: same script against postgres:17.10 (not pulled per brief) — expected S2/S3 LEAK in force_generic_plan/auto; confirms the version gate.
overclaim_risk: Psycopg2 uses SQL-level PREPARE (same CachedPlanSource path as protocol-level Parse, but not byte-identical to a Rust driver's unnamed/named statements); unpatched behaviour not reproduced locally.
underclaim_risk: Directly retires the open question whether SET LOCAL ROLE + statement caching is usable as defense-in-depth on current minors: it is.

verify.note: Finite negative result; unpatched 17.10 control not run so the patch-causes-fix claim is inferred. Has positive control (session set_config leaks).

title: CVE-2026-14666 fix anatomy: commit 1974acf23 adds PlanCacheRoleCallback on pg_auth_members/pg_authid/pg_database; no regression test
summary: Fix (Nathan Bossart, authored by reporters Ilya Staroverov and Shinya Kato; reviewed by Tom Lane; 2026-08-10, backpatched to 14, released 2026-08-13 in 18.6/17.11/16.15/15.19/14.24) registers syscache callbacks on AUTHMEMROLEMEM, AUTHOID and DATABASEOID that invalidate saved plans with dependsOnRLS (querytree + generic plan) or a generic plan with dependsOnRole; pg_database changes for other DBs ignored. Scope: role MEMBERSHIP, role ATTRIBUTE and DB OWNERSHIP changes — not SET ROLE switching, which was already covered.
specifics: Diff: acl.c (cached_db_hash made extern), plancache.c +60, acl.h +3; 3 files +63/-2. No src/test/regress change in the commit (checked the patch). CVSS 3.0 4.2 AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N. Same 17.11 release fixed CVE-2026-16239 (EXECUTE/FETCH portal row-type divergence -> memory disclosure/ACE; reported with Claude/Anthropic Research) and CVE-2026-14671 (contrib/refint plan cache).
overclaim_risk: No public exploit; needs app-specific privilege-removal pattern.
underclaim_risk: Absent regression test means a future plancache refactor could silently regress; our q1012_repro.py S2/S3 is the missing test.

verify.note: Verified 3 files +63/-2, backpatch to 14, reviewer Tom Lane, no tests; 18.6/17.11/16.15/15.19/14.24 on 2026-08-13 CVSS 3.0 4.2. Author roles slightly blurred.

title: SQLite lowering counterexamples (executed, 3.45.3): affinity coercion of bound params, NOCASE, LIKE wildcards/case/NUL, int=real
summary: Ten single-cause leaks under a bound-parameter naive lowering, each with a one-row reproducer; plus one leak in a deliberately hardened lowering (text bound param gets NUMERIC affinity on a NUMERIC column, so '' >= 10 is true because TEXT sorts above numbers). Not leaks: NULL (3VL only shrinks results for this fragment), NFC vs NFD under BINARY, non-ASCII under NOCASE, trailing space, empty IN.
specifics: Leak list: NOCASE tenant ('ACME' for 'acme'); NOCASE field eq; Eq(x,1) vs TEXT col storing '1'; Eq(x,'10') vs NUMERIC col storing 10; Range(x,'10','z') on NUMERIC col matches ''; Eq(x,1) matches 1.0 (untyped col); LIKE 'admin%' matches 'ADMIN-x'; LIKE 'a_%' matches 'aXb'; LIKE 'a%%' matches 'aZZ'; Or([])->TRUE; LIKE 'acme' matches 'acme\0evil'. Docs: datatype3 §4.2 affinity rules; §3.2 unary + strips affinity; §7.1 '+X' still counts as a column for collation (verified: +tenant = ? still NOCASE). Fix: typeof guard + COLLATE BINARY + (schema-typed) or unary + (schema-agnostic).
overclaim_risk: SQLite 3.45.3 (Python bundle) is older than current 3.5x; behaviour here is documented semantics, unlikely to differ.
underclaim_risk: Affinity coercion bit a lowering written to be safe.

verify.note: One old SQLite (3.45.3) but documented datatype3 semantics.

title: Postgres lowering counterexamples (executed, 17.11 + 19rc1): nondeterministic ICU (case + NFC==NFD tenant collision), citext, glibc range, LIKE regression from error to leak in 18+
summary: With deterministic=false ICU collations, tenant 'acmé' (NFC) equals stored NFD 'acmé' and 'ACME' equals 'acme' — distinct tenant ids collide. citext same for case. Under the default en_US.utf8 (libc) collation 'A' BETWEEN 'a' AND 'b' is true. LIKE on a nondeterministic column errors on 17.11 (fail-closed) but succeeds and leaks on 19rc1 (PG18 added LIKE support, committed 2024-11-27). COLLATE "C" on every text comparison removed all leaks.
specifics: PG docs (collation.html): deterministic flag only decides bytewise tie-break; 'und' nondeterministic treats canonically equivalent sequences equal even at identic level. pgsql-bugs #19681 (ILIKE rejected while LIKE works on 18.6) shows the area is still moving. 'IN ()' syntax error; '= ANY(empty array)' false.
overclaim_risk: Needs a schema that uses those collations/types; default deterministic text with '=' is exact.
underclaim_risk: Version-dependent: an upgrade (17->18) turned a fail-closed error into a leak with no schema change.

verify.note: 19rc1 LIKE leak and pgsql-bugs #19681 not independently confirmed; requires nondeterministic collation in schema.

title: Redis/Valkey key-prefix lowering: glob metacharacters and delimiter confusion leak across tenants; ACL key patterns share the matcher
summary: Using a line-for-line Python port of stringmatchlen_impl (redis 8.10.2 src/util.c; identical algorithm in valkey 9.1.2), naive MATCH t:<tenant>:* leaked for 10/19 adversarial tenants (tenant 'a*' saw 72 foreign keys) and glob-escaping alone still leaked 3/19 because ':' inside a tenant id makes 'acme' a prefix of 'acme:x'. Length-prefixed+escaped and hex-encoded {hash-tag} encodings leaked 0. acl.c ACLSelectorCheckKey uses the same stringmatchlen/prefixmatch, so per-tenant ACL users with %R~ patterns built from raw tenant ids inherit the bug.
specifics: Pattern recursion guard 'if (nesting > 1000) return 0' (CVE-2024-31228 fix; CVE-2022-36021 earlier) makes pathological patterns return no-match (fail-closed). db.c SCAN uses patternHashSlot to restrict cluster scans to one slot when the pattern has a fixed hash tag -> t:{hex}: encoding also makes tenant SCAN single-slot. Hardened: tenant handle -> hex (alphabet [0-9a-f]) inside {} + ':' terminator; adapter never accepts raw keys.
overclaim_risk: Executed against a port, not a live server (no redis image present); port fidelity is by inspection.
underclaim_risk: The ':'-in-tenant leak survives correct glob escaping — a reviewer would likely miss it.

verify.note: Matcher port not live server; valkey identity not diffed; tenant-list dependent counts.

title: MongoDB filter lowering hazards from primary docs: implicit array membership, $type on arrays, numeric type equivalence, null≡missing, implicit regex, inherited collation
summary: Doc-derived counterexamples: {tenant:'acme'} matches {tenant:['acme','evil']} (also visible to 'evil'); {$type:'string'} matches arrays containing strings so it does not enforce scalar-ness ({$type:'array'} does match array fields); all numeric BSON types compare equal; {f:null} matches null, missing and arrays containing null; implicit {f: <regex>} becomes $regex (explicit $eq does not; docs: always use explicit $eq with user input); operations inherit a collection's default collation unless {locale:'simple'} is passed, and strength 1/2 ignore case/diacritics; views reject collation override (fail-closed).
specifics: Hardened lowering: {$and:[{tenant:{$eq:t}},{tenant:{$not:{$type:'array'}}}, ...pred with explicit $eq/$in/$gte/$lte, plus {$type:<exact numeric>} when IR distinguishes]} with collation {locale:'simple'}. Executed oracle = spike SPK-MONGO-ORACLE (mongo:8 image > 500 MB limit; FerretDB is not semantics-identical).
overclaim_risk: Not executed; array-membership leak requires a writer able to store an array in the tenant field (validator absent or validationLevel moderate).
underclaim_risk: Array membership is a uniquely document-model hazard that SQL-trained lowerings and reviewers do not anticipate.

verify.note: Doc-only; $type-on-arrays and implicit array membership verified in Mongo docs; hardened form unexecuted.

title: OPA v1.21.4 Compile API (Rego->SQL/UCAST) executed: SQL Server startswith unsound, CI collations ignored, deny/allow encoded as absent vs empty
summary: Existing art for policy-to-native lowering, executed locally (static binary sha256 2ab571f3… matches release). startswith -> LIKE with backslash escaping and no ESCAPE clause for every dialect: correct for Postgres/MySQL default escape, unsound for SQL Server where '\\' is literal and '[b-z]' stays a live wildcard class (LIKE N'a\_[b-z]\%\\%'). No collation awareness: '=' and LIKE inherit MySQL/SQL Server case-insensitive defaults while Rego is case-sensitive. Unconditional include = {'result':{'query':''}}, unconditional deny = {} — documented, but a consumer defaulting a missing query to '' converts deny-all into allow-all.
specifics: Code: internal/ucast/ucast.go (ported from EOPA 2025-09-22, PR #7887) on huandu/go-sqlbuilder v1.43.0. Empty IN -> '0 = 1' (sound). Field node with nil value returns '' and go-sqlbuilder And/Or filter empty strings -> a dropped conjunct widens. Commit 986642777c (2026-07-27) 'ucast: Quote SQL filter field identifiers' fixed identifier injection (dynamic key input.fruits[input.column] -> "WHERE fruit.name = 'allowed' OR 1=1 --"); no GHSA in OPA's advisory list for it (checked 2026-10-25; latest GHSA-g2pf-6v5v-qcc8 2026-10-19 is unrelated). Values are interpolated inline (E'..', N'..'), not bound.
overclaim_risk: SQL Server leak inferred from executed OPA output + MS doc, not run on SQL Server; OPA's docs may scope the fragment per target.
underclaim_risk: The most widely used policy engine's SQL lowering has the same bug classes our denylist targets, a year after release; an identifier-injection fix landed silently in July 2026.

verify.note: Commit 986642777c quotes identifiers only; date/payload not shown; literals still inline; 'no GHSA' unchecked.

title: Empty-disjunction widening, executed in three popular lowerers: SQLAlchemy 2.1.6 or_(), go-sqlbuilder 1.43 Cond.Or(), @open-policy-agent/ucast-prisma 0.1.6
summary: Or([]) denotes FALSE, but SQLAlchemy 2.0.43 and 2.1.6 (latest, 2026-10-21) render or_() as no WHERE and and_(tenant=='acme', or_()) as WHERE tenant='acme' (the FALSE conjunct vanishes; DeprecationWarning only, deprecated since 1.4); go-sqlbuilder v1.43.0 Or()/And() drop empty members and return '' (no condition); ucast-prisma 0.1.6 maps an empty UCAST 'or' to {} (Prisma: all rows) and and[tenant, or[]] to {AND:[{tenant},{}]}. Hasura's ndc-test is the counter-example of good practice: it explicitly tests empty-OR returns no rows and empty-AND is a no-op.
specifics: Same failure as dpf-empty-means-all-pattern at the expression level. Our Lean model makes orN_nil = false a definitional theorem and the oracle exercises And([])/Or([]) nested inside conjunctions. Latent in OPA: its partial evaluator returned {} (deny) rather than an empty 'or' in our probes, so reachability through OPA is not shown.
overclaim_risk: Each needs a caller that builds an empty list dynamically (e.g., 'projects the user belongs to' = []).
underclaim_risk: That caller pattern is the normal way authorization filters are assembled; the result is cross-row exposure with no error.

verify.note: Probes not re-run; version/API dependent; exposure via OPA not reached. ndc-test independently tests empty OR.

title: Cedar TPE: Lean-proved residual soundness, but no residual->SQL/native lowering (issue #592 open since 2024-01-22)
summary: cedar v4.14.0 (2026-10-17) ships type-aware partial evaluation (cedar-policy-core/src/tpe: evaluator.rs 120 KB, residual.rs 33 KB) and cedar-spec main (301bdd22, 2026-10-23) proves reauthorize_is_sound / partial_authorize_decision_is_sound in Lean (re-evaluating a residual with concrete data equals full authorization), DRT-fuzzed (tpe-residual-reauthorize-drt). Nothing lowers residuals to a database query; maintainers suggest attaching SQL WHERE clauses as policy metadata (unverified). The step from residual to native rows is exactly the unproven gap our lowering theorem + refinement contract fills.
specifics: cedar-drt fuzz targets: tpe-is-authorized-drt, tpe-residual-reauthorize-drt, tpe-pbt, tpe-query-action-pbt. If Cedar is used as the policy language, the IR Pred becomes the target of a residual->Pred translation whose soundness is a second Lean theorem (Cedar residual semantics -> Pred eval).
overclaim_risk: Cedar may add data filtering later; absence is as of 2026-10-25.
underclaim_risk: Cedar's TPE proof is reusable: a residual->Pred translation plus our T2 would compose into an end-to-end Lean statement.

verify.note: Theorem names verified in TPE.lean; issue #592 is a general data-filtering request, weaker evidence for 'no lowering'.

title: Hasura NDC spec v0.2.14 normatively defines `equal` as syntactic equality (case-insensitive types must not offer it); ndc-test checks completeness, not soundness
summary: Closest existing art to the refinement contract: rows returned by an equal-predicate must carry exactly the compared value (equal as JSON values); `in` = disjunction of such equalities; ordering operators must be complementary and reflexive. ndc-test generates eq/in predicates from sampled values and only asserts non-empty results, plus explicit empty-AND/empty-OR tests; it never checks that returned rows actually equal the literal.
specifics: Release v0.2.14 2026-09-29. Our oracle's LEAK check is the missing soundness assertion; adopting NDC's wording for the IR spec costs nothing.
overclaim_risk: 'should' prose; connectors may deviate.
underclaim_risk: A production data-connector ecosystem already converged on the same equality discipline.

verify.note: Scalar-types spec text verified; completeness-not-soundness reading of ndc-test not re-checked.

title: DBMS logic bugs in exactly the collation/affinity area make the engine part of the lowering TCB (SQLancer/Rigger evidence)
summary: SQLancer-family oracles (PQS OSDI'20, NoREC FSE'20: 159 bugs/141 fixed/51 optimization; TLP OOPSLA'20; DQP SIGMOD'24; CODDTest SIGMOD'25) found >=131 fixed SQLite bugs, 80 logic bugs, including COLLATE expressions taking an affinity so an integer equalled a text value (#33), CAST inheriting COLLATE so a case-sensitive comparison matched (#41), COLLATE in BETWEEN ignored (#44), IN performing unexpected affinity conversion (#63). A lowering that is sound by the documented semantics can still leak on a buggy engine version.
specifics: Implication: Backend.Refines is a claim about (engine, version, schema); pin engine versions, re-run the differential oracle on every engine bump, and consider running SQLancer TLP/NoREC on the pinned engine in nightly CI (repo pushed 2026-10-21).
overclaim_risk: Historic bugs (2019-2021) are fixed; current rate unknown.
underclaim_risk: Planner regressions keep appearing (cf. sdg-sje-rls-2026).

verify.note: NoREC 159/141/51 verified on arXiv; Rigger list items unchecked; 2020-era.

title: Result-set soundness ≠ non-interference: RLS/DLS post-filter timing and scoring channels amplified by range/prefix predicates (Espiritu & Cash, arXiv 2608.11730, 2026-08-12)
summary: Rich predicates (range, prefix, conjunction) turn existence leakage into record reconstruction via PG RLS timing and OpenSearch DLS scoring/prefix expansion. Our lowering theorem guarantees only that returned rows are permitted; it says nothing about time/cost. The IR's Range and Prefix are exactly the amplifiers.
specifics: NOT-proven list entry. Mitigations to measure (spike SPK-IR-TIMING): tenant-leading composite indexes so the tenant conjunct bounds the scan (cost.py shows index SEARCH on (tenant,x)); per-tenant partitions/schemas; budgeted predicate complexity; constant-time padding only for high-assurance tenants. cwe: CWE-208; agent_amplified: true (agents can issue thousands of probing queries).
overclaim_risk: Attack demonstrated where untrusted queries run over all data (post-filter); a tenant-first index plan narrows but may not remove the channel.
underclaim_risk: LLM agents make high-volume adaptive probing cheap.

verify.note: verifier sampled other nodes; explorer grade kept

title: Mechanized SQL semantics 2020-26 model NULLs, never collation/affinity: Ricciotti-Cheney (Coq, JAR 2022), wrwgs/sqlsem (Lean 4 refinement, 2026), lean-linq
summary: Coq 'A Formalization of SQL with Nulls' (arXiv 2003.11331; JAR 2022) mechanizes nested queries, bags and NULL 3VL with a certified relational-calculus->SQL translation. 2026 Lean 4 experiments: wrwgs/sqlsem proves RelExpr.Refines between two parsed SQL queries (null-aware boolean simplification, projection fusion) — 0 stars; palladin/lean-linq (27 stars, Lean v4.35.0) compiles a typed DSL to parameterized SQL for SQLite/PG/MySQL/SQL Server without engine-semantics proofs. None model collation, type affinity, LIKE escaping or Redis/Mongo — the exact sources of leaks found here — so per-adapter refinement must stay an explicit, tested TCB item.
specifics: arXiv API search (abs:SQL AND Coq/Lean, 'query compiler' verified, collation SQL; 2023-2026) returned no verified query-compilation paper covering collation; DBLP blocked by an Anubis PoW page.
overclaim_risk: Search coverage incomplete (DBLP unavailable).
underclaim_risk: Our refinement-parameterised theorem is novel in shape but small; the mechanized-NULL literature validates the 3VL part.

verify.note: verifier sampled other nodes; explorer grade kept

title: LOCAL: out-of-process hop on ONE pinned core costs 4.8 us (UDS) / 2.1 us (futex shm ring) vs 0.02-0.05 us in-process, p50; p99 5.7 us / 2.5 us
summary: Request/response closed loop, client and helper process pinned to one CPU (2 context switches + 4 syscalls per UDS call). Noop op: in-process dyn call 23 ns (timer control 21 ns); UDS+postcard 4796 ns [4750-5899], p99 5706; UDS+bincode 4756; UDS raw length-prefix 4756; shm ring + futex wake 2054 ns [2035-2797], p99 2544; TCP loopback raw 8145 ns [6988-19027]. Echo payload 64B: inproc 24 ns, UDS-postcard 4866 ns, shm 2061 ns. 4KB: inproc 68 ns, UDS-postcard 9804, UDS-raw 5795, shm 2218. 64KB: inproc 1642 ns (memcpy+Vec), UDS-raw 19578 ns (p99 23377), shm 7420 ns (p99 8408), postcard/bincode 96320 ns before serde_bytes fix. Throughput (sequential closed loop, calls/s): inproc noop 21.8M; UDS 214k; shm 465k; 64KB echo UDS-raw 50k, shm 134k. Wasmtime component call reused from r2 (in-process, not IPC): noop 97 ns, 105B handler 1.24 us.
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets). Fixed hop: UDS-postcard-noop minus inproc-noop = 4.77 us; shm-futex = 2.03 us; ratio UDS/shm = 2.3x. Per-byte (raw frame, 4KB->64KB): (19578-5795)/61440 = 0.22 ns/B round-trip, ~4.5 GB/s each way effective incl. 2 copies/dir. Hop share of one core: rate*4.8us = 1k/s 0.5%, 10k/s 4.8%, 50k/s 24%, 100k/s 48%.
overclaim_risk: Measured on a 5.8 GHz-class laptop core under load and powersave governor, not on a KVM 1-vCPU $5 VPS; context-switch cost in a hypervisor guest is typically higher (unmeasured here, see spike). Closed-loop sequential only; no pipelining/batching so it is the worst-case for throughput.
underclaim_risk: Real adapter hops can be amortized by pipelining/batching (not measured); sibling SMT noise inflates p99 and maxes; so the quiet-machine hop may be lower than 4.8 us.

verify.note: Single loaded laptop, powersave, busy SMT sibling, closed-loop; no external corroboration of absolute 4.8 us; ratio consistent with shmem-ipc 3x.

title: NEGATIVE: spin-then-futex shared ring is catastrophic on 1 core (638 us/call, 133x worse than plain futex) and shm+futex is WORSE on 2 cores (4.8 us) than on 1 core (2.1 us)
summary: Spin-5000 (x86 pause ~140 cycles each) before futex_wait on a single pinned CPU: noop 638054 ns p50 [636296-638767], 1.6k calls/s, because the spinner burns its timeslice while the peer cannot run. Same code on 2 CPUs (13,17): 195 ns noop, 160 ns echo64, 283 ns redis-shaped, 1.66 us presign-shaped, 17.1 us 64KB echo, 5.2M calls/s (a real two-core win, 25x lower than 1-core futex). Conversely futex-only with 2 CPUs: 4784 ns vs 2054 ns on one CPU (cross-core wakeup IPI + idle exit); UDS 2 CPUs 8066 ns vs 4796 ns on one.

title: PITFALL: serde default serializes &[u8]/Vec<u8> element-wise; without serde_bytes postcard/bincode make a 64 KB payload hop 4.9x slower (96 us vs 19.6 us)

After adding #[serde(with="serde_bytes")] the rerun gave postcard 64KB min 19.7 us, 4KB min 5.8 us, matching raw framing (the rerun medians were noisier, 27.4 us and 9.1 us, because host load changed; mins are the clean figures, spread documented in 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl). title: LOCAL: redis-GET-shaped op +4.98 us (UDS) = 100x in-process but ~ one loopback RTT; S3-SigV4-presign-shaped op 1.34 us in-process vs 6.93 us UDS (5.2x) vs 3.46 us shm
summary: redis-GET shape: 17 B key -> 256 B value from a 1024-entry HashMap: inproc 49 ns [44-53]; UDS-postcard 5031 ns (p99 5898); UDS-bincode 4944; UDS-raw 4795; shm-futex 2122; TCP loopback raw 10680 ns median (p50 range 7062-19203). S3 presign shape: 4 HMAC-SHA256 key derivations + SHA-256 of 150 B canonical request + HMAC signature + 363 B URL: inproc 1338 ns [1271-1463]; UDS-postcard 6934 (p99 7806); UDS-raw 6539; shm 3458; TCP 9704. Absolute hop add is constant (4.8-5.6 us) so relative cost depends on the op: pure CPU op of 1.3 us -> 5.2x; a real redis GET over loopback (>= 8.1 us for the bare TCP echo measured here, plus redis work, unmeasured) -> UDS hop adds ~<=50% of just the bare TCP leg and less than the network RTT of any non-loopback store.
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. overclaim_risk: Shaped ops are not real Redis RESP or real driver CPU: a real redis-rs/fred client adds protocol parsing, allocation and socket I/O, so the in-process baseline for a true adapter is larger than 49 ns (thus relative overhead smaller than 100x).

title: LOCAL: for a 10 MB streamed body, zero-copy Bytes through http::Request<Body> copies 0 bytes in userspace and uses 30 us user CPU; an owned-decode+encode per-protocol codec copies 20 MB and costs +0.58 ms wall (+28%); a 3-copy variant +0.72 ms (+34%)
summary: Single-thread tokio current_thread pipeline on one pinned CPU: UnixStream pair ingress (64 KB writes) -> core -> UnixStream egress, 10 MB body, n=10. A (BytesMut read_buf, split().freeze(), http::Request<Body> with 8 headers, policy layer sees Bytes, write_all): wall p50 2079 us (min 2069, max 2121), user 30 us, sys 2057 us, allocator bytes 266 KB (30 allocs), explicit userspace copies 0, kernel copies 20.97 MB (read+write). B1 (owned Vec decode + framed encode): wall 2657 us, user 888 us, sys 1779, allocator bytes 21.24 MB, copies 20.97 MB. B2 (decode + native->neutral conversion + encode): wall 2794 us, user 916 us, allocator bytes 31.7 MB, copies 31.46 MB. Memory-only pipeline (16 KB chunks, no sockets): A 349 us (includes common copy #0 into buffer), B1 690 us, B2 738 us; allocation bytes A 68 KB vs 21.0 MB vs 31.5 MB; memcpy 10 MB cold control 548 us. So each extra userspace copy of a streamed body ~ 0.24-0.29 ms per 10 MB (24-29 us/MB); zero-copy saves 22% wall at 1 core on 10 MB bodies and 97% of user CPU; the kernel copy (read+write sys time 2.06 ms) dominates the zero-copy path.
specifics: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14-generic, taskset -c 13 (one logical CPU; SMT sibling 12 NOT idle-guaranteed), powersave governor, loadavg 10-23 during runs (other research loops), cpuset /user.slice, rustc 1.88.0 release lto, offline crates: tokio 1.x, bytes 1.x, http 1.x, postcard 1.1.3, bincode 1.3.3, serde_bytes 0.11.19, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, libc 0.2. Harness code: state/raw/round-003/02-bench/src, raw data 02-ipc-1core.jsonl (n=10 runs), 02-ipc-2core-control.jsonl (n=5), 02-ipc-1core-tcp.jsonl, 02-ipc-1core-serdebytes.jsonl, 02-rss-1core.jsonl, 02-norm-1core.jsonl. Control: timer floor (Instant pair) 21 ns p50 = no-op control; each run p50/p99 over 10k-20k calls after 300 warm-up; numbers below are medians over 10 runs of per-run p50 (range in brackets). Counting allocator wraps System (alloc/realloc/dealloc), counting enabled only on separate untimed pass; explicit memcpy counter in cp(). bytes 1.12.1 doc: clone/slice O(1) refcount; copy_from_slice copies. http-body 1.1.0 Body::Data: Buf, poll_frame.
overclaim_risk: Variants B1/B2 are constructed strawmen parameterised by copy count; real per-protocol stacks (nginx sendfile/splice, kernel-bypass) can also be zero-copy, so the result bounds the cost of copying, it does not show that any real per-protocol codec copies. Single 10 MB request; small requests (<16 KB) copy in <1 us so the effect vanishes. Not measured: h2/h3 framing (h2 crate copies into frames), TLS (record encryption copies unavoidable).
underclaim_risk: Even a 28-34% wall improvement matters only for large bodies; but the user-CPU 30x gap (30 us vs 888-916 us) is what a CPU-bound 1 vCPU box feels under many concurrent uploads once kernel work is offloaded (splice/sendfile not measured).

verify.note: Kernel copies dominate; owned-codec baseline is a strawman; TLS adds a copy anyway.

title: Prior art: published out-of-process/extension overhead numbers are sparse; best primary figures are MeshInsight (C++ filter +5.7/8.2 us, Wasm no-op +26.3 us, gRPC proxy 5x latency 4x CPU vs TCP) and seL4/Zircon cycle counts
summary: MeshInsight (UW/Duke/Bytedance, arXiv 2207.00592, Jul 2022; pdftotext verified): Envoy HTTP mode, 100 B messages, 30K rps: Fault Injection +5.74 us (3.1%), no-op WebAssembly filter +26.30 us (14.3%); additional overhead of HTTP proxying ~4x latency/3x CPU, gRPC 5x latency/4x CPU vs TCP; sidecar meshes +30-185% latency, +41-92% CPU on benchmark apps. LionsOS (arXiv 2501.06234): seL4 context switch 400-600 cycles; Mi et al. 2019 intra-core fastpath round-trip IPC 986 cycles (seL4) / 2717 (Fiasco) / 8157 (Zircon) - at 3-4 GHz roughly 0.25-0.33 us / 0.7-0.9 us / 2.0-2.7 us, i.e. a verified-microkernel IPC is ~15x cheaper than Linux UDS (4.8 us measured here). Chromium Mojo README: a Mojo call ~1/3 faster with 1/3 fewer context switches than legacy Chrome IPC; ~6 KB heap per bound endpoint; same-process communication should use direct calls. Envoy ext_proc docs (1.37) publish only per-phase latency stat fields (request_header_latency_us etc), no benchmark; OPA-Envoy performance page defines a benchmark method but lists no results; HAProxy SPOE.txt gives no numbers (motivation: blocking client libs); envoy-extproc-sdk README anecdote ~4-5 ms/filter (Python in docker-compose, D). Fuchsia round_trips.cc microbenchmark exists but no published numbers found. Chrome Site Isolation 2018: ~10-13% total memory overhead from more processes (press reports of Google engineer, C).
specifics: Prior-art gap itself is a finding: no primary, reproducible per-call ext_proc/ext_authz/SPOE/Pingora-out-of-process latency exists in the public record I could retrieve (grade: absence-of-evidence, searched 2026-10-25).
overclaim_risk: Different hardware, protocols (gRPC vs UDS) and eras (2019-2022); cycle conversions assume 3-4 GHz and are my arithmetic.
underclaim_risk: Absence of published numbers is not evidence the costs are small; vendor internal numbers may exist.

verify.note: MeshInsight Table 2 numbers confirmed but are sidecar per-filter rows, not clean IPC hops; Mi 2019 cycles quoted secondhand via LionsOS; clock assumption.

title: Shared-memory IPC crates: shmem-ipc 0.3.0 last release 2022-11-22 (vendor 3x vs UDS at 64 KB); iceoryx2 0.10.0 (2026-09-18, Apache-2.0/MIT, Linux x86_64 tier 2) claims ~100 ns polling hops for 8 B offsets - both vendor numbers

Independent M4 (non-Linux) re-bench found tuned UDS within 1-11% of shm (secondary, D). iceoryx2: repo reports charts only (i7-13700H, Linux 6.10.10, rustc 1.81.0); maintainer forum claim ~100 ns polling-mode for 8 B payload; Linux x86_64 tier 2 target tier 1; 225 open issues. Agnocast (arXiv 2506.16882) shows constant latency vs size for zero-copy static types. Decision: a hand-rolled ring is ~12 unsafe sites in my harness; a dependency adds a large unsafe TCB; UDS needs zero unsafe.

title: L5 harness spec: ipcbench (single binary, subcommands run|rss|norm), 1 pinned CPU, n>=10, no-op control, acceptance numbers per transport
summary: Spec: crate ipcbench (tokio 1, bytes 1, http 1, postcard 1.1.3 default-features=false, serde_bytes 0.11, libc 0.2, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12; bincode only as control). Modes: `ipcbench run N` (transports inproc-dyn, uds-postcard, uds-bincode, uds-rawframe, tcp-loopback-rawframe, shm-futex, shm-spin5k; ops noop, echo64/4096/65536, redis_get, s3_presign; 300 warmup, 10-20k calls, per-call Instant latency, JSONL with p50/p90/p99/max/mean/calls_per_s/loadavg/cpus_allowed/cpuset/governor); `ipcbench rss` (exec vs fork-from-zygote 1/8/64 MB heap, n=1/8/32 children, /proc/pid/smaps_rollup Rss/Pss/Private_Dirty, spawn-to-first-reply n=200); `ipcbench norm N` (memcpy control, A/B1/B2 memory-only and socket pipelines, counting allocator pass separate from timed pass, getrusage user/sys). title: L5 decision table: adapter goes out-of-process when it has any C/C++ client, >15 unsafe sites, or is third-party AND its hop budget (rate x 4.8 us) fits; stays in-process when it is hot-path (>50k calls/s/core or op < 10 us) and pure Rust; reversal conditions stated
summary: Table (1 core, UDS+postcard/raw hop ~4.8 us p50, ~5.7 us p99; shm-futex ~2.1 us): (R1) C/C++ client library OR unsafe sites > ~15 at HEAD OR third-party/unreviewed OR driver memory-safety advisory in last 12 months => OUT of process (separate binary, seccomp+Landlock, UDS), provided hop share <= 10% of core: calls/s/core <= 20,000 (<= 2 hops per request => <= 10,000 rps). (R2) Same triggers but expected rate 20k-100k calls/s => stay out-of-process only with batching/pipelining (amortise to <= 1 us/op; spike S2) else the adapter C code must be replaced or the feature dropped from the default build; never move C into the front binary just for speed. (R3) pure Rust, <= 15 unsafe, first-party golden, op < 10 us or rate > 50k/s (token check, route lookup, header policy, SigV4 presign at 1.3 us) => IN process; hop would be 5.2x for presign and 100x for key lookups. (R4) pure Rust, ops 10-100 us (real redis/Scylla driver ops on loopback ~tens of us, unmeasured) => in-process by default; out-of-process allowed when the op is >= 50 us (hop <= 10%) and any trigger from R1 holds. (R5) Heavy compiler-bearing modules (wasmtime/Cranelift) => out of process or per-request wasm in-process only with pooled instances (r2: 20 us fresh instance, 52 KB) - unchanged. Reversal conditions (move OUT -> IN): measured hop p99 on target VPS > 40 us or hop share > 15% of core at observed p95 load; the C dependency is replaced by a pure-Rust fuzzed driver with <= 15 unsafe sites; or crash isolation is demonstrated unnecessary (no panic/abort path in 12 months of fuzzing). Reversal (IN -> OUT): unsafe count > 15, any C binding added, new memory-safety RUSTSEC/GHSA in the driver, or fuzz crash class not catchable by catch_unwind. Memory budget: each extra exec helper ~0.5 MB private + ~0.6 MB PSS minimal (real helper larger, spike S1); budget 8 helpers <= 40 MB on a 1 GB box.
specifics: Thresholds 15 unsafe sites, 10% core budget and 20k calls/s are policy choices derived from the measured 4.8 us hop and a 10% overhead budget, not from a controlled security study. Inputs: w02.ipc-hop-cost-1core, w02.redis-presign-shaped-ops, w02.helper-process-rss-spawn, dpf-l5-adapter-isolation.
overclaim_risk: Single-machine measurements; no real driver costs; 15-site cutoff inherited, not re-derived.
underclaim_risk: If hop is pipelined, rates well above 20k/s are feasible out-of-process.

verify.note: Thresholds are policy from one laptop hop number; 15-unsafe proxy weak; R5 inconsistent with in-process 97 ns.

title: L5 amendment to w02.L5-feature-gate-rule: add rules 5-8 (declared hop budget, wire format, serde_bytes, no spin on <=2 CPUs, CI perf gates)
summary: Append to the rule: (5) every out-of-process module declares op_cost_us and max_calls_per_s in its manifest; build fails if max_calls_per_s * 4.8 us > 10% of one core (CI computes from ipcbench baseline JSON). (6) Control-plane wire format is postcard 1.1.3 (no_std, maintained) or raw length-prefixed frames; bincode is forbidden (RUSTSEC-2025-0141); every byte-slice field uses serde_bytes (CI test: 64 KB echo over the UDS test transport <= 25 us on reference runner, else fail - catches the 4.9x pitfall). (7) Bodies never cross the module boundary inside the serialized message; pass body via fd/shared memfd or stream frames; headers/metadata only in postcard. (8) Shared-memory rings are not in the default build (unsafe TCB; UDS gives 4.8 us with zero unsafe); spin-waiting is forbidden when available_parallelism() <= 2 (638 us/call measured) - futex or eventfd only. (9) Ingress front ends must pass Bytes through without owned copies: CI test streams 10 MB through the normalization core and asserts allocator bytes < 1% of body and 0 explicit copies. Existing rules (1)-(4) unchanged.
specifics: Depends on w02.ipc-hop-cost-1core, w02.serde-bytes-pitfall, w02.bincode-unmaintained-use-postcard, w02.norm-copy-cost-measured.
overclaim_risk: The 25 us and 10% gate values are chosen with margin from laptop data and must be re-baselined on the target VPS (spike S1).

verify.note: Rule 5 hardcodes laptop 4.8 us; rule 8 rests on one 2-core result; rules 6/7/9 sound.

title: Executable HRR acceptance test: rustls 0.23.46 server vs RUSTSEC-2026-0349-shaped ClientHellos (6/6 as expected)
summary: Hand-built TLS1.3 ClientHello probes against rustls =0.23.46 + aws-lc-rs =1.18.2 ServerConnection (2026-10-25). T1 default config, supported_groups [X25519MLKEM768, X25519], key_share only X25519 -> HelloRetryRequest selecting 0x11EC. T5 same with P-256 share -> HRR 0x11EC. T6 MLKEM share -> ServerHello 0x11EC. T2 default config, groups [X25519, X25519MLKEM768], X25519 share -> ServerHello X25519 (classical accepted: server follows CLIENT order). T3 'pq-required' config (CryptoProvider.kx_groups=[X25519MLKEM768]) same input -> HRR 0x11EC. T4 pq-required, client offers only X25519 -> alert 40 (NoKxGroupsInCommon). Full-handshake check: real rustls client with kx order [X25519, X25519MLKEM768] vs pq-required -> negotiated X25519MLKEM768, HandshakeKind FullWithHelloRetryRequest; vs default -> X25519, Full. Verdict for q2-002: YES, the rustls server sends HRR to X25519MLKEM768 when the client lists it FIRST but shares only X25519 (the exact RUSTSEC-2026-0349 shape), so the downgrade does not succeed against a default rustls server; it does NOT when the client lists X25519 first.
specifics: Code: state/raw/round-003/03-work/hrr_acceptance_test.rs (test module, invariants PQ-KX-1/PQ-KX-2) and state/raw/round-003/03-work/pqauth/src/main.rs (probe(), raw_client_hello()). Output: state/raw/round-003/03-work/run1.txt lines HRRTEST. Knobs: 0.23.x = only CryptoProvider.kx_groups (no group-preference knob; ignore_client_order affects cipher suites only, hs.rs:555-660 group = first client-listed group the server supports, tls13.rs:227 HRR if no share). main 28ee6c68 (2026-10-23): ServerConfig.kx_selector: &dyn KeyExchangeSelector, default PreferClientOrder, alternative PreferServerOrder (commit 3fe60d7913 2026-10-12; 483f623e3b 2026-10-13), OfferedKxGroup.has_key_share. title: rustls server group selection = client order in 0.23.46; server-preference only via 0.24-dev KeyExchangeSelector
summary: Source-verified: rustls 0.23.46 ServerConfig picks the first group in the client's supported_groups that its provider supports, HRRs if the client sent no share for it; there is no server-preference knob for groups in 0.23.x. On main (0.24.0-dev.2, commit 28ee6c68 2026-10-23) a new KeyExchangeSelector trait (PreferClientOrder default, PreferServerOrder optional) lets a server prefer X25519MLKEM768 even when a client lists X25519 first, at the cost of one HRR round trip for such clients.
specifics: 0.23.46 src/server/hs.rs:555-660; src/server/tls13.rs:195-245; main rustls/src/server/config.rs:757-818 (PreferClientOrder/PreferServerOrder), :79 kx_selector field, :732 default &PreferClientOrder. PR #3370 (open 2026-10-19): client accepts ServerHello share for a component group it did not offer after HRR (client-side, hybrid component) - track.

title: Pitfall (measured): rustls default-features=false without 'prefer-post-quantum' puts X25519 FIRST -> classical handshakes
summary: With rustls =0.23.46 and default-features=false, features [aws-lc-rs,std,tls12] (a common pattern in hyper-rustls/reqwest/tokio-rustls dependents), DEFAULT_KX_GROUPS becomes [X25519, SECP256R1, SECP384R1, X25519MLKEM768]; the client sends an X25519 share and lists X25519 first, and against a client-order server (rustls default) the handshake is classical. Observed in our first run: group=X25519, ClientHello 319 B instead of 1539 B. Enabling 'prefer-post-quantum' restores X25519MLKEM768 first.
specifics: Source: rustls-0.23.46/src/crypto/aws_lc_rs/mod.rs:254-262 (cfg(feature="prefer-post-quantum")). L5 CI gate: `cargo tree -e features -i rustls | grep prefer-post-quantum` must match for every rustls in the lock (server AND outbound clients: DB drivers, upstream proxies); plus a runtime assert that ClientConfig.crypto_provider().kx_groups[0].name()==X25519MLKEM768 (or MLKEM1024 in gov profile).
overclaim_risk: Only affects configs built from default_provider(); explicit kx_groups lists are unaffected.
underclaim_risk: Silent: no warning, handshake succeeds; HNDL exposure for outbound traffic of the golden if any dependency disables default features.

verify.note: Measured 319 B vs 1539 B ClientHello plus source line; single-version claim.

title: Measured ML-DSA-44/65/87 vs ECDSA/Ed25519 TLS 1.3 handshakes in rustls: bytes, TCP segments vs initcwnd 10, QUIC amplification, server/client CPU
summary: Own measurement 2026-10-25, rustls 0.23.46/aws-lc-rs 1.18.2, in-memory, X25519MLKEM768, server sends leaf+intermediate (rcgen 0.14.10 chains), no SCTs, no cert compression. Server first flight SH..Finished: ECDSA-P256 2,138 B (2 segments @MSS 1448); Ed25519 2,002 (2); ML-DSA-44 11,680 (9 segments: fits initcwnd 10 = 14,480 B with 2.8 KB headroom); ML-DSA-65 15,627 (11: exceeds initcwnd -> +1 RTT on a cold TCP path); ML-DSA-87 20,883 (15: +1 RTT); CNSA 2.0 profile (pure ML-KEM-1024 + ML-DSA-87) 21,331 (15). ClientHello 1,539 B (1,849 B with ML-KEM-1024). QUIC (modeled from exact CRYPTO bytes; 1200-B datagrams, ~50 B/packet overhead): client CH needs 2 Initials -> 3x budget = 6 datagrams; ECDSA needs 2 (OK), ML-DSA-44 11, ML-DSA-65 14, ML-DSA-87 19 -> every ML-DSA chain is anti-amplification-limited (extra RTT unless address already validated). Server CPU/handshake (median of 10x100, two independent runs): ECDSA 103.6/103.8 us; Ed25519 ~90; ML-DSA-44 194.3/197.2 (+88%); ML-DSA-65 255.8/266.0 (+150%); ML-DSA-87 282.9/276.3 (+170%); CNSA2 268.7/282.5. Client verify+kx: ECDSA 243, ML-DSA-44 177 (faster than ECDSA), ML-DSA-65 240, ML-DSA-87 303 us.
specifics: DER sizes leaf/intermediate/root: ECDSA 343/394/381; ML-DSA-44 3940/3989/3978; ML-DSA-65 5469/5518/5507; ML-DSA-87 7427/7476/7465; Ed25519 279/328/317. ML-DSA PKCS#8 = 54 B (seed form). Hardware: Intel i9-14900HX, 32 threads, host load average 36-77 (shared with sibling agents) -> CPU absolute values noisy, ratios stable across runs (within ~5%). Derived (E): a WebPKI-style ML-DSA-44 chain with 2 embedded ML-DSA-44 SCTs adds ~4.8 KB -> ~16.5 KB > initcwnd; leaf-only (intermediate elided via trust anchor IDs) ML-DSA-44 ~7.7 KB = 6 segments but still 7 QUIC datagrams vs 6 budget; MTC landmark-relative with ML-DSA-44 leaf key ~= 2.35 KB cert + 2.42 KB CV -> ~6.1 KB flight (5 segments, ~6 datagrams: at the QUIC budget edge).
overclaim_risk: In-memory: segment and QUIC datagram counts are computed from exact bytes with fixed MSS/overhead constants, not captured on a wire; CPU numbers under heavy host contention; no RFC 8879 compression (ML-DSA keys/signatures are essentially incompressible, but ASN.1 boilerplate is).
underclaim_risk: ML-DSA-44 private-PKI chains fit TCP initcwnd and verify FASTER than ECDSA on the client; for internal mTLS / origin pulls the cost is ~+90 us server CPU and ~+9.5 KB, which is affordable.

numbers_checked.source_value: +9,542 B measured for 2-cert chain without SCTs; +~14.3 KB with 2 SCTs derived

title: Acceptance criterion: QUIC listener with PQ certificates must not exceed 2 RTT; use Retry/NEW_TOKEN-validated paths or keep ECDSA on QUIC
summary: From measured CRYPTO bytes: any ML-DSA chain (>=10.5 KB handshake-space bytes) exceeds the 3x anti-amplification budget of a 2-Initial ClientHello (~7.2 KB), so a cold QUIC handshake needs >=1 extra RTT. Rule for the golden: public QUIC listener serves ECDSA/Ed25519 (or future MTC) only; ML-DSA certs allowed on QUIC only for clients with a validated address (NEW_TOKEN) or on TCP.
specifics: Gate: harness counts server datagrams before first client Handshake ACK; assert <= 3 x client bytes and total handshake RTT <= 2 with ML-DSA-44 leaf+intermediate; record result per release.
overclaim_risk: Packet overhead constant approximated; coalescing changes counts by ~1 datagram.
underclaim_risk: Clients with larger Initials (Firefox 1350 B) raise the budget slightly; still insufficient for ML-DSA chains.

verify.note: Modelled 3x budget; Retry/NEW_TOKEN and compression ease it; conclusion holds under variants.

title: Header-size ceilings for 5-16 KB PQ-signed capability tokens (source lines, 2026-10-23..25)
summary: hyper 1.12.0 (golden pin) HTTP/2 server: DEFAULT_SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE 16 KiB (src/proto/h2/server.rs:40; RFC 7541 accounting name+value+32 per field) -> a 16 KB token header fails, ~15.9 KB is the ceiling minus all other headers; HTTP/1.1: DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE 8192+4096*100 = 417,792 B (proto/h1/io.rs:23), max 100 headers (role.rs:31) -> fits. h2 0.4.20 codec default 16 MiB (codec/framed_read.rs:22) but hyper overrides to 16 KiB. nginx master 9a7439fd (2026-10-23): client_header_buffer_size 1k, large_client_header_buffers 4 8k (src/http/ngx_http_core_module.c:3628-3632) -> any single header line >8 KB rejected (HTTP/1: 400 'Request Header Or Cookie Too Large'; HTTP/2 uses same directive since http2_max_header_size deprecation). Envoy main a0fd7327 (2026-10-25): max_request_headers_kb default 60 KiB, max 8192 (http_connection_manager.proto field 29) -> 431; max_headers_count 100; nghttp2 per-field ~100 KB. Node v26.12.1: --max-http-header-size default 16 KiB (since v13.13.0) and undici defaults its maxHeaderSize to http.maxHeaderSize (lib/dispatcher/client.js:65-69). Cloudflare edge: request headers 128 KB total, URL 16 KB (connection-limits page updated 2026-10-22).
specifics: Verdict per token size (single header, base64url): 5 KB: OK everywhere. 8-11 KB (3-hop ML-DSA-44 = 11.2 KB raw, ~15 KB b64): FAILS nginx default; OK Envoy, CF; borderline hyper h2 & Node (16 KiB total incl. all headers). 16 KB+: FAILS nginx, hyper h2 default, Node/undici default; OK Envoy (60 KiB) and Cloudflare (128 KB). Golden config: hyper http2 max_header_list_size = 65536 only on routes that accept Tier-X tokens; prefer body or by-reference handle; document nginx 'large_client_header_buffers 4 32k' for operators fronting us.
overclaim_risk: Cloudflare per-header limit not documented (only total); Workers/other CF products may differ; nginx HTTP/3 module limits not checked.
underclaim_risk: Header limits are a hard interop wall: a 16 KB token header silently fails behind default nginx or Node, independent of our server.

verify.note: Source-read defaults; not re-verified by verifier; operators override.

title: Multi-KB tokens are never HPACK/QPACK-indexed by default: full retransmission on every request
summary: RFC 9113 SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE initial 4,096 octets; RFC 7541 s4.4 adding an entry larger than the table empties the table; RFC 9204 QPACK max table capacity default 0. h2 0.4.20 encoder refuses to index any header with len*4 > max_size*3 (>3 KB at default) (src/hpack/table.rs:153). So a 5-16 KB PQ-signed capability token in a header costs its full size (Huffman barely compresses base64) on EVERY request on the connection, unlike a 300-B Ed25519 token.
specifics: Implication: per-request overhead ML-DSA-65 single-block token ~5.3 KB raw/~7.1 KB b64 x requests; 100 req/connection = ~0.7 MB vs ~30 KB for Ed25519. Supports the two-tier token (MAC chain locally, PQ signature only at trust-domain crossing) and a by-reference session-bound handle after first presentation.
overclaim_risk: Peers may advertise larger tables; clients may still Huffman-compress.
underclaim_risk: Bandwidth cost is per request, not per connection.

verify.note: RFC 7541 4.4 and QPACK capacity 0 are spec facts; 75% threshold is h2-crate detail.

title: CA/B Forum SC-106 (ML-DSA in TLS server certs) closed without ballot 2026-10-21; moved to proposed NonBrowser WG
summary: cabforum/servercert PR #679 'SC-106: Enable Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQ) Key Pairs in TLS Server Certificates' (opened 2026-08-26) was closed by its proposer on 2026-10-21 without a discussion period: Chrome, Mozilla and Cloudflare agreed to drop the 7.1.3.2.3 restriction (ML-DSA CA signing classical keys, a downgrade-protection use) but disagree on 7.1.3.1.3 (classical CA cross-signing ML-DSA: Chrome forbids for CT/no-benefit reasons, Mozilla wants it). Proposer will re-propose in a ClientAuth/NonBrowser WG once chartered. Earlier PRs #662 (closed 2026-08-11) and #624 'Add MLDSA-87' (closed 2026-06-29). So, as of 2026-10-25, the Baseline Requirements do not permit ML-DSA in publicly-trusted TLS certificates, and the browser path is MTC-only.
overclaim_risk: A NonBrowser WG profile could still appear in 2027 for SDK/IoT relying parties.
underclaim_risk: Anyone planning public ML-DSA X.509 for browsers in 2026-27 is planning against a closed ballot.

verify.note: PR #679 closed 2026-10-21 by author (withdrawal, not CA/B decision); moving to ClientAuth/NonBrowser WG; Chrome/Mozilla agreed to drop ML-DSA-CA-signs-classical restriction.

title: What a server must implement to serve MTCs (draft-07) and where rustls/OpenSSL/Go stand (2026-10-25)
summary: Per draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs-07 s8-9: the server (authenticating party) does NOT fetch landmarks; it holds several credentials (classical X.509 chain, standalone MTC, landmark-relative MTC) and selects per ClientHello using the TLS trust_anchors extension (draft-ietf-tls-trust-anchor-ids-06, 2026-09-30); it SHOULD NOT send a landmark-relative cert without an RP signal (trust_anchor_negotiation), prefers landmark-relative when usable, falls back to standalone or classical. ACME client must send Accept: application/pem-certificate-chain-with-properties, parse CertificatePropertyList (trust_anchor_id/groups/negotiation), and poll the 'acme-optional-alternate' link (HTTP 202 + Retry-After) for the landmark-relative cert without blocking deployment. Sizes: landmark-relative proof 736 B (23 hashes, hourly landmarks, 5.4M certs/h/CA); standalone proof 384 B + cosignatures; 1,024 B covers 2^32. Implementations: rustls issue #3079 open (2026-06-03, maintainer: 'definitely want'); rustls PR #3376 'Add TLS trust anchor IDs' open (2026-10-21, experimental codepoint 0xca34 as BoringSSL, TrustAnchorResolver) = step 1; rustls #3214 open: signature_algorithms_cert not exposed to ResolvesServerCert (blocks per-client ML-DSA vs classical chain choice). OpenSSL PR #33014 (open, 2026-09-27) MTC-07 + TAI-06 feature branch (AI review flagged MTC leaf path skipping auth-level check). Let's Encrypt boulder #9082 align -05->-07 (open), PR #9102 standalone MTC endpoint (open). Go: #82402 UPKI revocation proposal (2026-10-21).
specifics: L5 interface sketch: trait CredentialSelector { fn select(&self, hello: &ClientHelloView{sni, sig_algs, sig_algs_cert, trust_anchors}) -> Arc<CertifiedKey> } with credentials tagged {kind: X509|MtcStandalone|MtcLandmark, trust_anchor_id, requires_negotiation}; ACME module must support ARI + profiles + optional alternates. Reversal: adopt rustls TrustAnchorResolver when #3376 merges.
overclaim_risk: Draft could still change (-05 -> -07 already broke Chrome compatibility with -06).
underclaim_risk: Server-side MTC is mostly certificate selection + ACME plumbing, not new crypto; it is buildable in 2027 on rustls once TAI lands.

verify.note: PR #3376 confirmed (off by default, 0xca34 experimental codepoint, first step to #3079); other statuses spot-checked.

title: Composite ML-DSA: LAMPS draft-19 in RFC Ed Queue; TLS draft WG-adopted 2026-10-20; exact sizes
summary: draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs-19 (2026-10-20, 234 pp, intended Proposed Standard) is in the RFC Editor queue (IANA RFC-Ed-Ack); composite KEM -23 likewise. draft-ietf-tls-composite-mldsa-00 (dated 2026-10-20, posted 10-23, Standards Track) adopted from draft-reddy-tls-composite-mldsa-12: 16 SignatureSchemes, codepoints TBD (e.g. mldsa44_ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256, mldsa44_ed25519_sha512, mldsa87_ecdsa_secp384r1_sha512). Max sizes (App. A, pk/sig bytes): MLDSA44-Ed25519 1344/2484; MLDSA44-ECDSA-P256 1377/2492*; MLDSA65-Ed25519 1984/3373; MLDSA65-ECDSA-P256 2017/3381*; MLDSA65-ECDSA-P384 2049/3413*; MLDSA87-ECDSA-P384 2689/4731*; MLDSA87-Ed448 2649/4741; MLDSA87-RSA4096-PSS 3118*/5139 (*=maximum). Signature = ML-DSA sig || traditional sig over M' = 'CompositeAlgorithmSignatures2025' || Label || len(ctx) || ctx || PH(M). rustls: no composite support; Go: pure ML-DSA chosen (golang #78888), x/crypto/ssh composite proposal #82315 (2026-10-18); OpenSSL PR #32886 (open).
specifics: Token Tier-X per-block (next_pk + sig) with MLDSA44-Ed25519 = 1344+2484 = 3,828 B (matches pqc-capability-token-design). A composite TLS chain adds only ~65-72 B per certificate over pure ML-DSA-44 (measured pure ML-DSA-44 flight 11,680 B -> ~12.0 KB derived).
overclaim_risk: TLS codepoints unassigned; no browser has committed to composite.
underclaim_risk: Composite is the conservative hedge for long-lived signatures (tokens, releases) where size is ~+64 B over pure ML-DSA.

verify.note: Sizes arithmetic-consistent with FIPS 204; RFC Editor queue status not re-verified.

title: Deployable PQ authentication today: Cloudflare-to-origin ML-DSA-44 (Custom Origin Trust Store + Authenticated Origin Pulls)
summary: Cloudflare docs (pqc-to-origin, updated 2026-08-03; overview updated 2026-07-03): origin may present an ML-DSA leaf (private CA uploaded to Custom Origin Trust Store, replacing public CAs), and Cloudflare can present an ML-DSA client cert via zone/per-hostname AOP; keys must be seed-only encoding; TLS 1.3 required; Cloudflare sends an X25519MLKEM768 share first and accepts HRR. title: CNSA 2.0 TLS profile (draft-becker-cnsa2-tls-profile-05, 2026-10-22): pure ML-KEM-1024 + ML-DSA-87 only; measured 21.3 KB server flight in rustls

title: PQ-authentication posture for the golden (decision with dated reversal conditions)
summary: Alternatives enumerated: (A) ECDSA-P256 X.509 everywhere; (B) pure ML-DSA X.509 on public listener; (C) composite ML-DSA X.509; (D) MTC when available; (E) KEM-based auth (AuthKEM/KEMTLS); (F) dual chains selected per ClientHello. Decision: public TCP/QUIC listener = ECDSA-P256 (or Ed25519) WebPKI chain via ACME now (B is blocked: CA/B SC-106 closed 2026-10-21, Chrome CQRS MTC-only; also ML-DSA-65/87 chains exceed initcwnd and all ML-DSA chains exceed QUIC amplification budget). Key agreement = X25519MLKEM768 preferred, HRR-enforced (r3pq.hrr-acceptance-test). Private hops (origin pull from Cloudflare, internal mTLS, upstream/DB mTLS) = ML-DSA-44 X.509 from an operator CA now (rustls 0.23.46 serves/verifies by default; +~90 us server CPU, +9.5 KB, fits initcwnd). Gov profile = pure ML-KEM-1024 + ML-DSA-87 per CNSA2 TLS profile (accept the +1 RTT). (C) composite only for long-lived signatures (tokens/releases), not TLS, until rustls supports it. (E) rejected for TLS: AuthKEM -07 is individual and LAKE/EDHOC is where AuthKEM is moving. Cert layer built as CredentialSelector so (D)/(F) are config, not code.
specifics: Reversal conditions (check monthly): R1 Chrome ships MTC verification enabled by default in Stable for CQRS (target Q3 2027) AND rustls merges trust_anchors (PR #3376) + MTC (#3079) -> add MTC landmark+standalone credentials to public listener. R2 rustls 0.24 released with KeyExchangeSelector -> switch public profile to PreferServerOrder (forces PQ KX for every hybrid-capable client at +1 RTT for X25519-first clients). R3 a CA/B ballot permitting ML-DSA TLS certs passes AND a browser root program accepts them -> reconsider (F) dual chains (needs rustls #3214 signature_algorithms_cert exposure). R4 Let's Encrypt MTC production (2027 target) -> golden ACME client must support ARI + acme-profiles + optional alternates. R5 a practical attack on ML-DSA or implementation break -> composite for private hops. R6 CRQC timeline estimates move inside 2030 -> enable ML-DSA leaf in MTC immediately when available. Pre-registered: P(Chrome Stable verifies public MTCs by default by 2027-12-31) = 0.55; P(CA/B permits ML-DSA in publicly-trusted TLS server certs by 2027-12-31) = 0.2.
overclaim_risk: Assumes WebPKI timelines hold; ECDSA public auth is not PQ-secure (forgery needs a live CRQC, not HNDL, so the risk window is deferred not removed).
underclaim_risk: Waiting for MTC on the public listener is right, but private hops and the gov profile can be PQ-authenticated today with no new code.

(121 of 124 differing strings are absolute registry paths). (2) Remap only the source dir: a5e357c2.. != 990ad966.. (3,777,056 vs 3,777,760 bytes; 242 of 248 differing strings are registry paths). (3) --remap-path-prefix for source, $CARGO_HOME/registry/src and $RUSTUP_HOME: IDENTICAL 397c98ae76a5bf65de099be32205d925c6e8b04abd5a99a41ab262e0159d6d6b (3,769,888 B, builds 1m45s and 1m56s), and with debug=2 also IDENTICAL a47adadd8289.. title: Executed cargo cooldown: 7 days downgrades 6 crates and lands a known advisory (RUSTSEC-2026-0382); 14 days downgrades 26 and lands 6 advisories incl. rustls 0.23.45 classical-KX downgrade
summary: cargo 1.98.0 (stable binary; -Zmin-publish-age enabled with RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1) with [registry] global-min-publish-age = "7 days": `cargo generate-lockfile` on the golden Cargo.toml (hyper/h2/governor/cedar exact pins) yields 220 crates, 6 older than latest: tokio 1.53.3 (1.54.1 is 3.2 days old), rustls-webpki 0.103.15 (0.103.16 is 4.7 days old), cc 1.8.0, smallvec 1.16.3, smol_str 0.3.6, find-msvc-tools 0.1.14. cargo-audit on that lock: 1 vulnerability, RUSTSEC-2026-0382 (CVE-2026-111943, 2026-10-20) rustls-webpki 0.103.15 accepts certificate paths through distrusted emSign intermediates; fixed 0.103.16. With 14 days: the exact pin cedar-policy =4.14.0 (7.4 days) is a hard resolver error ("version 4.14.0 is too new (published 8 days ago, minimum age 14 days)", help suggests 4.13.0 and CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_PUBLISH_AGE=allow); after relaxing cedar and rustls ranges, 26 crates are downgraded (aws-lc-rs 1.18.1, aws-lc-sys 0.45.0, cedar 4.13.0, rustls 0.23.45, rustls-webpki 0.103.15, tokio 1.53.2 ...) and cargo-audit reports 6 advisories: rustls 0.23.45 RUSTSEC-2026-0346 (Debug impls expose TLS secrets), -0347 (buffered data sent to outer server after ECH rejection), -0348 (brotli certificate decompression allocates up to 1 GiB pre-auth), -0349 (unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange) all dated 2026-10-14 and patched in 0.23.46; webpki -0382; tokio 1.53.2 RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (patched >=1.53.3). A blanket cooldown without a security bypass is net-negative for a TLS server in the 2 weeks after a rustls advisory batch.
overclaim_risk: Single resolution date (2026-10-25); the failure depends on advisory timing relative to the cooldown window and would be absent on a quiet week; cargo applies the age check only when resolving new versions, existing lock entries are not re-checked.
underclaim_risk: Shows cargo already surfaces the conflict (messages list "available: vX, published N days ago" and the override env var), so the fix is policy plus a CI rule rather than tooling.
specifics: Extends v.cargo-min-publish-age-rfc3923 and sc.cooldown-policy. Corrects dates: RFC 3923 PR opened 2026-02-23 and MERGED 2026-05-18 (r1 recorded 2026-02-23 as acceptance); cargo PR #17012 (-Zmin-publish-age) merged 2026-06-18 milestone 1.98.0; stabilization PR #17335 merged 2026-08-28 milestone 1.100.0; Rust stable is 1.99.1 (2026-10-13) with 1.100.0-beta.7 (2026-10-17) so stable cargo cannot use it until 1.100 (~2026-11-26 by the 6-week train); beta/stable cargo docs do not yet mention it. Config keys: registry.global-min-publish-age, registries.<name>.min-publish-age, resolver.incompatible-publish-age, env CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_PUBLISH_AGE=allow (preserved in the lockfile).

verify.note: PR #17335 merged 2026-08-28 m1.100.0 and RUSTSEC-2026-0349 (2026-10-14, >=0.23.46) verified; harm is silent loss of PQ confidentiality.
