title: Golden coding rules CR1-CR9 plus clippy.toml and CI gates for cancel correctness
summary: CR1 No tokio::sync::Mutex/RwLock in the golden core or SDK. Use an actor/message pass, or std Mutex not held across an await. Gate: clippy disallowed-types = [tokio::sync::Mutex, tokio::sync::RwLock] in core crates. CR2 clippy.toml await-holding-invalid-types = [tokio::sync::MutexGuard, tokio::sync::OwnedMutexGuard, tokio::sync::RwLockWriteGuard, tokio::sync::SemaphorePermit (where it guards an invariant), aegis_db::RawConn, aegis_wasm::StoreGuard]. Deny lints: clippy::await_holding_invalid_type, await_holding_lock, await_holding_refcell_ref, let_underscore_future, rustc unused_must_use. CR3 clippy.toml disallowed-macros = [tokio::select!, futures::select!, tokio::try_join!] outside modules listed in cancel-audit.toml. Each allowed use carries '// CANCEL-SAFETY: <why every arm is cancel-safe, or that the losing futures are spawned>' (CI grep gate, modelled on SAFETY comments for unsafe). CR4 disallowed-methods in core: tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt::write_all, AsyncReadExt::read_exact/read_to_end/read_to_string, tokio::time::timeout (use aegis_rt::deadline, which is CP-aware). Exempt framing modules carry CANCEL-SAFETY comments. CR5 The commit path runs only through aegis_rt::spawn_must_complete(fut) (tokio::spawn registered with the shutdown drainer); handler futures are CancelOnDisconnect before CP only. Type-level: Tx<Open>::commit(self) -> CommitTicket is not async; the ticket is awaited from a detached task (extends dx.l5-decision-sdk-shape). CR6 Arm a drop guard immediately after any wire send that creates server-side state (Parse/Bind/SAVEPOINT/BEGIN/MULTI), disarmed when the owning value is constructed (the tokio-postgres #1374 pattern). CR7 The pool checkin predicate is the NC3 reusable(c), owned by the golden DB adapter and never the driver default (diesel_async #304 lesson). Gate: unit test plus a cancel-sweep O2. CR8 Every pub async fn in core with more than one await that touches shared state has a '# Cancel safety' rustdoc section (RFD 400). Gate: script over rustdoc JSON. CR9 Pins (2026-10-25): sqlx git rev >= f1e94ec (or not used); diesel_async git rev >= PR #305 merge (or not used); tokio-postgres: carry PR #1374 as a patch until it is released; wasmtime >= 49.0.3 (50.0.0 current), with component-model-async disabled unless required; oneshot >= 0.1.12 if pulled in transitively (cargo-deny ban below).
specifics: Acceptance: (A1) cargo clippy -D warnings on core with the above clippy.toml passes; (A2) a mutant corpus of 12 cancel-unsafe snippets (tokio Mutex across an await, select! on read_exact, let _ = async_fn(), timeout around tx.send, INCR/EXPIRE split, post-hoc debit, missing drop guard, default is_broken, skip-limit-on-timeout, select! &mut fut with await in an arm (futurelock), write_all in a handler, commit inside a cancellable future) must be rejected at 100% by lint or by the cancel-sweep harness, with the split reported; (A3) cancel-sweep PR gate green. Limits: clippy cannot see cancel safety of arbitrary futures, and no lint for futurelock exists (RFD 609 proposals are unimplemented), so CR3 plus the harness carry those cases. async-rust-lsp is editor-only and serves as an optional developer aid, not a gate.
overclaim_risk: Banning select! and timeout in the core creates friction. The allowlist will grow, and its value depends on review of the CANCEL-SAFETY comments.
underclaim_risk: These rules are cheap (clippy config plus about 50 LOC of scripts) and catch 4 of the 15 instance shapes statically.

title: Implementation-phase spike: cost of discard-on-cancel (PG reconnect with TLS 1.3 + SCRAM) and K_total await counts per handler
summary: Not run here (machine-safety rule §0e; no primary measurement exists). Protocol: PG 18 on the same 1 vCPU VPS; pgbench -C (reconnect per txn) vs persistent, with sslmode=require plus scram-sha-256, 60 s each, 3 runs; report connection setup p50/p99 ms and CPU-ms on both sides. Then a cancel storm: N clients send h2 RST at a uniformly random time into a 2-query handler; measure the reconnect rate and p99 of honest traffic, with and without per-client cancel charging (NC4). Decision it informs: if reconnect p50 > 20 ms or a CPU of 1 vCPU saturates below 200 cancels/s, adopt 'discard only if not ReadyForQuery-I' (which needs adapter-level protocol state tracking) instead of unconditional discard, and set the cancel-charge weight so that attacker cancels/s <= 10% of reconnect capacity. Also measure K_total for the 5 reference handlers (expected < 50).

title: Defender CPU per stage on a $5 VPS, marked measured vs assumed
summary: $5/mo fully utilised vCPU = $1.9e-6 per CPU-second. Stage costs on the reference core (i9-14900HX), scaled /0.5 for a $5 shared vCPU (cpu_scale=0.5 is an E assumption): TLS1.3 full handshake 424 us ref (rustls 0.23.37, 2,357 hs/s/core; InfoQ 2026-09; grade C, suite unstated) => 848 us on VPS; resumed 138 us ref (7,249/s/core) => 276 us; hybrid ML-KEM adds ~21% server CPU (Red Sift/OpenSSL, C). Own measurement: GCRA keyed std HashMap 18 ns @1k keys, 88 ns @65k keys, global GCRA 1.2 ns (D). r2 measured: wasmtime component fresh store+instantiate p50 20.3 us (B). Assumed (E): parse 10 us, classify 1 us, 429 write 8 us, challenge issue 150 us, verify 50 us (measured Anubis verify ceiling ~11.5k proofs/s => ~87 us under 64-way contention, C). Consequence: defender dollars per request are ~1e-9 (a rejected request after full TLS costs ~1.7e-9 USD); the binding constraint is capacity: one vCPU saturates at ~1,131 req/s of 429-after-TLS (941/s with hybrid ML-KEM) and ~32 req/s of cost-100 handler work.
specifics: Own microbench: 07-work/gcra_bench.rs (std only, rustc -O, taskset core 2, 2026-10-25, binary deleted); numbers_checked in the raw JSON.
overclaim_risk: TLS number is a laptop core scaled by an assumption; ECDSA vs RSA cert, session-ticket mode and kernel costs not captured. Keyed-store timing used SipHash (pessimistic vs FxHash/DashMap).
underclaim_risk: Reject-path CPU is dominated by TLS, not by any limiter stage (limiter work is <0.1 us vs 424 us): limiter micro-optimisation is worthless; pre-TLS filtering is what moves capacity.

verify.note: InfoQ gives 2,357 hs/s/core on unspecified x86_64 (not i9-14900HX); +21% ML-KEM is OpenSSL 3.5.5; 0.5 scale assumed.

title: Negative: naive key-eviction under key churn costs 3.5 us per check (40x the lookup)

The O(n) scan is an artefact of my eviction rule, but it demonstrates that a K key-churn attacker (r2 swarm actor K) turns eviction into the hot path unless eviction is O(1) amortised (generation sweep / CLOCK / TAT-expiry bucket).

title: Measured PoW asymmetry: native SHA-256 62-89 MH/s vs in-browser ~150 kH/s (430-860x)
summary: pow-buster / 'Proof of Mutex' (Ryzen 9 7950X, 2025-09-06): Anubis SHA-256 single-block, native single thread 62.19 MH/s (SHA-NI) to 85.75-89.16 MH/s (AVX-512), Chromium SIMD128 14.74 MH/s, in-browser Anubis solver ~100-200 kH/s (Firefox ~20% of Chromium), multi-thread native 1.465-1.485 GH/s vs vendor solver ~650 kH/s. Corrects r2 abuse-pow-economics-calc, which used 2.3 MH/s from an e2-micro: a modern native solver does a d4 (16-bit) challenge in ~1 ms and d6 (24-bit) in ~0.27 s on one core, i.e. ~$1e-9 per solve. A human browser at 150 kH/s needs 0.44 s for 16 bits, 1.7 s for 18 bits and 112 s for 24 bits (phones slower; the sim assumes 5x, E). Anubis v1.28.0 (2026-10-08) .. v1.28.2 (2026-10-23) adds opt-in WASM PoW (Argon2id, HashX, SHA-256; difficulty counts leading bits: Fast/Moderate/Strong = 8/16/24 bits SHA-256, 7/15/20 HashX, 2/4/6 Argon2id), disabled by default, no published performance numbers; memory-hard variants are the only change that could alter the asymmetry and are unmeasured here.
specifics: Author-run benchmarks on one CPU; vendor figure 650 kH/s disagrees with the 150 kH/s browser figure by 4x (WASM optimisation/throttling).
overclaim_risk: Do not read this as 'PoW is useless': it is a speed bump plus a way to force a client to run JS/WASM; but no difficulty a phone tolerates changes attacker cost.
underclaim_risk: Argon2id/HashX WASM modes (v1.28) were not measured; they may restore some asymmetry.

verify.note: Proof of Mutex figures verified (single-author blog, 7950X); multi-thread 1.1-1.5 GH/s and EPYC 2.1-3.4 GH/s make farm asymmetry far larger.

title: NEGATIVE: the r2 L5 default pipeline collapses under a 10k-IP solver swarm; no single-parameter change rescues it
summary: Simulation (heapq DES, 120 s, 3-10 seeds; 200 humans, 10 verified agents, 10k-IP solver swarm at 1,000 rps cost-100 + heavy hitter 300 rps): r2 defaults give human failure 99.1% (max 99.4% over seeds 1-10), human server-side p99 3,793 ms vs 46.8 ms unloaded, verified-agent success 59.7%. In 178 single-parameter sweep points (~45 parameters x 3 seeds: s1_rate, anon/sess budgets, L0/Lmin/Lmax, qmax, CoDel, ladder levels, PoW bits, cpu_scale, conn caps, shares) human FP stays 98-100% for all except: exp_frac<1 (26%), fresh_class on (47%), ladder off / max_level 0 (47%), ladder_cost_aware (81%), tls_full_cap 0.2 (87%), anon_burst=30 (16%, because anon burst < cost-100 makes the deep path unreachable without a session). Root causes: (1) PoW-minted cookies land in the same 'session' class as returning humans, so the swarm owns that queue (I3 isolation violated); (2) no concurrency cap on the expensive tier (cost-100 = 30 ms) so 4-8 swarm requests starve everything; (3) per-identity budgets irrelevant because each of 10k identities stays under its own budget. Other scenarios on r2 defaults (10 seeds): naive swarm 22.8% FP (new humans 70.9%), browser swarm 34.2%, aged-cookie swarm 92.6%, cheap flood (cost 5) 75.5%, 1k-IP datacenter swarm 84.8%; heavy single IP only 1.4% (per-IP limit works against one IP).
specifics: Files: 07-work/panel_r2.jsonl (10 seeds x 10 scenarios), sweeps_r2_mixed.jsonl (178 sweep points x 3 seeds). Sim: /home/patrickd/aegis/research/state/raw/round-003/07-work/swarm_sim.py

title: NEGATIVE: full TLS handshakes cap a 1 vCPU box at ~1.1k connections/s; rejects after TLS cannot protect humans
summary: At cpu_scale 0.5 (E) a swarm of 1,000 new-connection rps consumes 85% of the CPU in handshakes alone; the sim's 5 ms accept windows then drop arrivals at random, so human FP has a floor equal to the drop fraction (CAND base 13.8%, fixed to 8.1% by reserving window budget for resumed/keep-alive). Mitigation tested: tls_full_cap = share of the CPU window usable by FULL handshakes: 1.0 -> human FP 7.9%/p99 470 ms; 0.8 -> 7.5%; 0.6 -> 0.9%/170 ms; 0.4 -> 0.9%/85 ms; 0.2 -> 0.8%/59 ms (TUNED base). Cost: new visitors lose handshakes first (new-visitor FP 3%). CPU sensitivity (TUNED): cpu_scale 0.25..2.0 keeps FP 0.8-1.5%. Hybrid X25519MLKEM768 adds ~21% server handshake CPU (Red Sift, OpenSSL) and ~1.1 KB each way: capacity 1,131 -> 941 rps. A CPU-keyed challenge trigger is actively harmful: challenges cannot cheapen handshakes, so the ladder climbed to the 24-bit rung and human FP went 12% -> 23% (CAND).
specifics: Files: sweeps_tuned2_mixed.jsonl (tls_full_cap, cpu_scale), sweeps_cand_mixed.jsonl (trig_cpu).
overclaim_risk: The fix depends on the server being able to tell a resumable client before spending crypto (PSK/ticket identity is visible in ClientHello); not implemented in any stack I verified.
underclaim_risk: A kernel/XDP pre-TLS filter or an upstream CDN/SYN-proxy would remove this floor entirely; not simulated.

verify.note: Depends on 0.5 scale and unspecified benchmark hardware; order of magnitude matches InfoQ.

title: NEGATIVE: the 24-bit PoW rung excludes humans and the load-keyed ladder had no measurable effect once class budgets existed
summary: Human cost at measured browser speed 150 kH/s: 16 bit 0.44 s, 18 bit 1.7 s, 20 bit 7 s, 24 bit 112 s (phones 5x, E). CAND mixed sweep: top-rung bits 16/18 -> human FP 9-10%, 20/22 -> 15%, 24 -> 23% (new visitors 58%). Attacker expensive successes were flat at 6.0-6.2/s across 16-24 bits (native solver 62 MH/s: 24 bits = 0.27 s), so PoW difficulty did not change attacker admission at all. On the TUNED pipeline the ladder (on/off, max_level 0-3, trigger thresholds, bits) changed nothing: the stress signal (anon-queue sojourn >5 ms for 100 ms) never fired because S3 aggregate budgets and the tier cap keep queues short. title: Local loop lower bound: std-only SDK+handlers cold debug build 0.33-0.40 s (159 MB RSS), warm cargo check 0.11 s; axum build not measurable offline

title: Cloudflare Workers bindings = capability grant ('permission and an API in one piece'); runtime isolation incidents remain (workerd URLPattern OOB cross-tenant secret read, Check Point 2026)
summary: Binding model: resources reachable only via env bindings declared in config; secrets never exposed to code. Caveat from docs: isolates may be reused when only bindings change, so construct clients from env per request not in global scope. Separately, search results report a workerd cross-request global-state leak fix (July 2026, details not found) and Check Point's URLPattern out-of-bounds read letting one Worker read another tenant's secrets (self-hosted users told to update to workerd v1.20260619.1) - not verified at primary source here. Implication: API-level capability does not replace isolation; both layers needed.

title: CANDIDATE DECISION: first-party handlers = native Rust against a separate-crate capability-typed SDK (shape B) + compile-fail mutant corpus as CI gate; alternatives listed with reversal conditions
summary: Chosen (provisional): Ctx<'r, E: Effect> built only by the router (Principal non-optional, no Default, private fields), TenantDb/TenantCache lifetimes bound to request and non-Clone, Tx<Open>->Committed gating effects, Html/Url/Secret newtypes, Granted<Cap> proofs; sdk in its own crate; app crate forbid(unsafe_code); no raw-SQL or raw-HTML API. Acceptance criterion: `cargo test` runs a corpus of >=30 compile-fail mutants (trybuild-style or the run_mutants.py harness) and requires >=90% of structural-class mutants rejected, with the semantic classes (ownership, visibility) delegated to Cedar policy + differential oracle tests; error-message guard: no rejected mutant's diagnostic may contain 'make the field public'-type help (test greps stderr). Alternatives: (a) plain axum + lint/clippy rules (A: 1/16; reverse if LLM runs show equal defect rate); (b) WIT component handlers with capability imports (language-independent, adds Wasm TCB, wasi-http repo archived/merged Nov 2025 - reverse if Wasm host chosen for third-party code); (c) Ur/Web or other typed-web language (rejected: bus factor 1, no release since 2020 per map); (d) Encore/Convex-style mandatory annotation + codegen (needs codegen TCB); (e) RLS-only (map: fails when agents create tables). Reversal conditions: LLM agent trials show B raises repair-loop iterations > 2x with no defect drop; or async lifetime ergonomics make B handlers fail to compile in realistic axum/tokio integration (spike).
overclaim_risk: Based on toy SDK + indirect literature; no LLM trial; async/tokio integration (lifetimes in async fn, Send bounds) untested and may break the non-'static handle design.
underclaim_risk: Cost of the decision is low (SDK is ~100 LOC of types) and it is falsifiable cheaply, so even moderate evidence justifies prototyping.
specifics: Spike S1 (impl phase): same 16 mutants against real axum 0.8.9 + tokio handlers, async fn, with B-style extractors (FromRequestParts producing Principal; handle with request lifetime via extension), measure rejected/compiled. Spike S2: paid LLM trial 20 tasks x 2 shapes counting iterations-to-green and mutant rate.

verify.note: Candidate on toy experiment; S1/S2 not run; existing typed-ctx crates not evaluated.

title: WebSocket CSWSH: Origin check is absent by default in both Rust WS crates; 2025-26 CVE stream
summary: Cross-site WebSocket hijacking keeps producing CVEs because the handshake carries ambient cookies and the server must opt in to an Origin check. 2025-26 OSV-verified: Vitest CVE-2025-24964 (2025-02-04, RCE via dev WS API), Mailpit CVE-2026-22689 (2026-01-10), Next.js CVE-2026-27977 (2026-03-17, 'Origin: null' bypassed the dev HMR allowlist), nginx-ui CVE-2026-34403 (2026-04-20, upgrader CheckOrigin always true), Spring for GraphQL CVE-2026-41700 (2026-06-11, GraphQL-over-WS). Neither tungstenite nor fastwebsockets checks Origin: fastwebsockets upgrade.rs doc states it 'does not inspect the Origin, Sec-WebSocket-Protocol or Sec-WebSocket-Extensions headers'. RFC 6455 s4.2.2 makes origin validation optional for servers; draft-ietf-webtrans-http3-16 s3.2 makes it MUST verify for browser sessions (403). Class is fully handled once in a core that owns the handshake.
specifics: Core rule: Origin is a typed value (absent | null | opaque string | parsed origin) compared against a per-route allowlist with null explicitly denied unless listed; cookie-authenticated upgrades with no Origin from a browser UA are denied; SameSite is defence in depth only. Same check reused for WebTransport (MUST in s3.2), SSE with credentials, and GraphQL-over-WS.
overclaim_risk: These are mostly dev tools and small apps, not hardened servers; class prevalence is high but impact is app-specific.
underclaim_risk: Origin:null bypass in a mainstream framework shows even a deliberate allowlist is easy to get wrong; test vectors needed, not just a check.

verify.note: Next.js CVE-2026-27977 is dev-server only, CVSS4 2.3 Low; other CVEs not re-checked.

title: Upgrade/101 desync: Pingora CVE-2026-2833 (critical), Netty CVE-2026-59898, Envoy CVE-2024-23326
summary: Proxy switches to tunnel mode before the backend confirms 101, or the backend upgrades without proper headers, so the proxy keeps parsing HTTP while the backend speaks WebSocket (or the reverse). Pingora <0.8.0 forwarded bytes after an Upgrade request without waiting for 101: CVE-2026-2833 critical, 2026-03-05, GHSA-xq2h-p299-vjwv, fixed 0.8.0. Netty V07/V08 WebSocket handshaker accepted Sec-WebSocket-Version alone (GHSA-4mp9-239f-g9hg / CVE-2026-59898, 2026-07-22/29). Envoy CVE-2024-23326 accepted HTTP 200 as entering upgrade mode (2024-06-04). Origin research: 0ang3el websocket-smuggle (2019). Same advisory batch in Pingora: CVE-2026-2835 TE/HTTP1.0 smuggling (critical), CVE-2026-105299 Connection-nominated header ACL bypass (2026-10-20). RFC 9220 (June 2022) and RFC 8441 avoid Upgrade entirely via Extended CONNECT on h3/h2, so WS-over-h2/h3 removes the class on that leg but not on h1 upstreams.
specifics: Invariant: a connection leaves HTTP-framed mode only after a validated 101 (status exactly 101, Connection and Upgrade tokens match request, Sec-WebSocket-Accept correct); pre-101 bytes after a request with Upgrade are buffered or rejected, never forwarded; h1 pipelining after Upgrade request is rejected. Handled once in the core's connection state machine; testable with a differential fuzz harness (see L5).
overclaim_risk: Pingora is a proxy; for an origin server with no upstream the exposure is the handshake validator (Netty-class) not the forwarding class.
underclaim_risk: A critical smuggling bug survived in the most-used Rust proxy until 2026-03, so 'Rust => no desync' is false.

verify.note: GHSA-xq2h verified: CVE-2026-2833 critical 9.3, 2026-03-05, <=0.7.0 fixed 0.8.0; Cloudflare CDN unaffected.

title: permessage-deflate size check after inflate: 4 independent 2026 CVEs; Rust WS crates implement no deflate
summary: Size limits enforced on the compressed frame or after full inflation are bypassed by compression bombs. OSV-verified 2026: undici CVE-2026-1526 (2026-03-12, PerMessageDeflate.decompress collects all chunks unbounded, CVSS 7.5), websocket-driver CVE-2026-54490 (2026-07-17, check read frame header), Autobahn Python CVE-2026-77528 (2026-09-18, check before inflate). libsoup CVE-2026-15709 appears in Red Hat/AWS feeds but did not resolve in OSV (E lead). PortSwigger (2025-09-17) reports a Java WS ping-of-death: inflated length field causes huge allocation. Rust: fastwebsockets lib.rs says 'permessage-deflate is not supported yet'; tungstenite parses the extension header but implements no compression, so the bomb class is absent by non-implementation. Frame/message defaults: tungstenite max_message 64 MiB, max_frame 16 MiB, max_write_buffer_size usize::MAX (no write backpressure bound by default); fastwebsockets max_message 64<<20. tungstenite RUSTSEC-2023-0065/CVE-2023-43669 (<=0.20.0, fixed 0.20.1, 2023-09-25) was handshake-header re-parse CPU DoS.
specifics: Policy: do not ship permessage-deflate in the golden build (zero-code-when-unused). If ever enabled: inflate with an output cap = min(remaining message budget, per-connection memory budget), abort on exceed, ratio cap, and context-takeover off. Core sets max_message far below 64 MiB (e.g. 1 MiB) and bounds write buffer.
overclaim_risk: Absence of deflate in Rust crates is not a safety proof; 64 MiB defaults times 10k connections is still a memory attack.
underclaim_risk: Four unrelated libraries made the same ordering mistake in one year, so this is a systematic spec-trap, not a one-off.

verify.note: libsoup CVE unresolved so 'four CVEs' is three verified.

title: Rust WebSocket crates: tungstenite/tokio-tungstenite vs fastwebsockets vs tokio-websockets
summary: tungstenite 0.30.0 (2026-07-11, 363M dl, MIT/Apache, 6.3k LOC, 5 unsafe hits, cargo-fuzz dir present, 1 RUSTSEC 2023); tokio-tungstenite 0.30.0 (2026-07-11, 326M dl, MIT, 1.9k LOC, 0 unsafe, no fuzz dir, 0 advisories); fastwebsockets 0.10.0 (2026-01-01, 5.7M dl, Apache-2.0, 3.0k LOC, 1 live unsafe in mask.rs align_to_mut, fuzz dir present, 0 advisories, no Origin check, no deflate); tokio-websockets 0.13.3 (2026-06-25, 18M dl, MIT; not source-audited here); hyper-tungstenite 0.30.0. title: gRPC/Connect: path canonicalization authz bypass (grpc-go CVE-2026-33186 critical), DATA fragmentation OOM, stalled-body leak
summary: Top 3 classes with ids. (1) Authorization on non-canonical routing identity: grpc-go CVE-2026-33186 (GHSA-p77j-4mvh-x3m3, critical, 2026-03-17): server routed ':path' without leading slash but authz interceptors (incl. official grpc/authz) matched the raw string, so deny rules were skipped; also CVE-2026-84303 (2026-08-19) xDS RBAC mixed-case header match bypass. (2) HTTP/2 framing resource exhaustion: grpc-go CVE-2026-84304 (2026-08-19, 1-byte DATA frames, heap OOM, fixed 1.83.1), h2 crate RUSTSEC-2026-0258/GHSA-q83h-524g-xf6h (2026-08-17, unbounded empty DATA frames, fixed 0.4.16), Pingora CVE-2026-105297 (2026-10-20, unlimited streams + 16 MiB header list defaults, 1 connection OOM-killed a 2 GiB process), Rapid Reset CVE-2023-44487 (grpc-go GHSA-m425-mq94-257g). (3) Stream lifecycle/accept-loop: tonic CVE-2024-47609 (0.12.0-0.12.2, accept loop exits, 2024-10-01), connect-rust GHSA-jx5x-3mcr-qp8r / RUSTSEC-2026-0304 (2026-09-21: finished streaming call keeps reading stalled body, 4 MiB buffer + task + stream held), @grpc/grpc-js CVE-2026-48068 (2026-07-14 unhandled stream error crash), grpc-go CVE-2026-84445 (xDS no :authority, 2026-09-14).
specifics: Core must expose one canonical route identity (RFC 3986 normalized, leading slash enforced, method+service+rpc split) and ALL policy engines consume only that value; raw :path is never visible to authz. Message-size, per-stream deadline, header-list and stream-count limits are core budgets (h2 level), message-count and decode-size are front-end hooks.
overclaim_risk: grpc-go is Go; Rust analogue of the :path bug is not demonstrated, though hyper/tonic routing differentials are plausible.
underclaim_risk: Class (1) is a spec-differential class that no budget or parser fuzz finds; it needs an explicit invariant.

verify.note: CVE-2026-33186 exists (GHSA-p77j, GO-2026-4762); other CVEs not re-checked.

title: tonic 0.14.6 and connectrpc 0.9.1: advisories, unsafe, fuzz, defaults (tonic overrides hyper's 200-stream cap with unlimited)
summary: tonic 0.14.6 (2026-05-07, 441M dl, MIT, 1 GHSA CVE-2024-47609, ~15 unsafe-word hits in src outside generated code (codec/buffer.rs 4, metadata 11), no fuzz dir, no OSS-Fuzz). connectrpc 0.9.1 (github connectrpc/connect-rust, crate created 2025-10-14, 2026-09-21, 8.8M dl, Apache-2.0, 0 unsafe, no fuzz dir, 1 advisory in its first year). Defaults read from source 2026-10-25: tonic DEFAULT_MAX_RECV_MESSAGE_SIZE 4 MiB, send unlimited; tonic Server stores max_concurrent_streams: Option<u32> = None and calls hyper builder.max_concurrent_streams(None) (transport/server/mod.rs:840) whereas hyper 1.x h2 server defaults to Some(200) and 16 KiB header list; tonic only applies header-list limit when set, so header list stays at hyper's 16 KiB but stream concurrency becomes unlimited (source-read, not runtime-verified: spike). Same shape as Pingora CVE-2026-105297, which was exactly 'defaults unbounded'. Alternatives enumerated: tonic, connect-rust, grpc-rs (C core), hand-rolled gRPC framing over hyper (5-byte length-prefixed message, ~300 LOC), grpc-web via tonic-web.
specifics: Pin tonic with explicit max_concurrent_streams, http2_max_header_list_size, max_decoding_message_size, per-RPC timeout; or terminate h2 in the core and feed tonic's service via tower so limits are the core's, not tonic's. CI check: assert effective SETTINGS via an h2 client test.
overclaim_risk: Source-read of defaults; tonic may set the cap elsewhere (e.g. via a layer) - unconfirmed at runtime.
underclaim_risk: tonic's 441M downloads and one advisory is real maturity; the finding is about defaults not code quality.

verify.note: tonic None pass-through confirmed in source; effective SETTINGS unverified (hyper default 200 vs None).

title: GraphQL: validation-rule quadratic cost, directive/alias/batch amplification, CSRF via GET or loose Content-Type, CSWSH
summary: Classes with ids. (1) Cost amplification through validation or execution that depth/complexity limits do not cover: graphql-php CVE-2026-40476 / GHSA-68jq-c3rv-pcrr (2026-04-17, OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged quadratic, existing QueryDepth/QueryComplexity rules do not mitigate, fixed 15.31.5); async-graphql CVE-2024-47614 / GHSA-5gc2-7c65-8fq8 (2024-10-02, directive overload, high, fixed 7.0.10, mitigation limit_directives); async-graphql CVE-2022-31173 + juniper RUSTSEC-2022-0038 (2022-07, nested fragments overflow). (2) Request-level bypass: Apollo Server CVE-2026-23897 (2026-02-04, charset body DoS, high 7.5). (3) Cross-origin: Spring for GraphQL CVE-2026-41700 (2026-06-11) CSWSH over graphql-ws. Spec: GraphQL-over-HTTP draft: GET MUST NOT execute mutations (405), POST MUST support application/json, missing Content-Type SHOULD be 4xx (415), warns urlencoded/multipart are simple requests with no preflight. IBM cost spec (Draft, c 2021): @cost(weight: String!), @listSize(assumedSize, slicingArguments, sizedFields, requireOneSlicingArgument=true), default weight 0 scalars/enums and 1.0 composites, abstract types use max member, negative field cost rounds to 0; Apollo router implements an Int-weight variant (demand control). Introspection and field suggestions are information leakage controls, not DoS controls.
specifics: GraphQL needs a body-semantic admission stage (parse, validate, static cost via IBM cost model) that cannot be done by byte/frame budgets, so it is per-front-end logic, but its output is one number charged to the core's per-principal cost budget.
overclaim_risk: IBM spec is a 2021 draft, not a standard; Apollo/graphql-js adoption of @listSize semantics is partial.
underclaim_risk: Parser/validator quadratics are invisible to depth and complexity caps; that is the part cost limits underclaim.

verify.note: Not re-verified; IBM cost spec draft; several CVEs non-Rust.

title: async-graphql 7.2.1 source audit: every cost limit defaults to None; any Content-Type parsed as JSON; no GET-mutation guard; body read_to_end uncapped
summary: Read from HEAD (pushed 2026-04-21): Schema defaults complexity None, depth None, max_directives None, max_aliases None, recursive_depth 32 (schema.rs:395-410). http/mod.rs receive_batch_body: with no Content-Type it assumes application/graphql-response+json, and every non-multipart type falls through to serde_json parse - so text/plain (a CORS simple request) is accepted, contrary to GraphQL-over-HTTP 'SHOULD reject'. integrations/axum extract.rs line 100 serves GET by parsing the query string; grep over src/ and integrations/axum finds no mutation-over-GET rejection (spec: MUST NOT). receive_batch_json does body.read_to_end into a Vec with no cap (axum DefaultBodyLimit applicability unverified). 0 unsafe, forbid(unsafe_code) in 10 files, parser has a cargo-fuzz dir, 2 GHSAs. This is a library-default finding, not a CVE.
specifics: Wrap async-graphql behind the core: core enforces Content-Type allowlist (application/json, application/graphql-response+json), 415 otherwise; method policy (GET only for queries, reject mutation text, require custom header or JSON content-type for preflight); body cap before the library sees bytes; set limit_depth/limit_complexity/limit_aliases/limit_directives explicitly.
overclaim_risk: Static read only; not executed; the axum DefaultBodyLimit or a tower layer could bound body size and some checks may live in the core engine outside my grep.
underclaim_risk: Defaults-open libraries are normal; the point is that the core, not the library, must hold these policies.

verify.note: Grep-absence evidence; DefaultBodyLimit unverified.

title: WebTransport: capsule/stream lifecycle memory DoS, withheld flow-control credit, datagram cap bypass in the QUIC layer
summary: webtransport-go (quic-go) 2026: CVE-2026-21434 oversized WT_CLOSE_SESSION error message (2026-02-12), CVE-2026-21435 withheld flow-control credit blocks CloseWithError forever, CVE-2026-21438 closed streams never removed from session map, CVE-2026-57497 (2026-07-23, GHSA-g35j-m5xg-vh3q) unknown capsules fully buffered; Socket.IO CVE-2026-59724 (2026-07-08) crafted session id crashes Engine.IO WebTransport. Rust substrate quinn: 13 GHSAs, 11 in 2026 (first 2026-03-09), including GHSA-2hv7-gw8g-gpq5 (2026-08-17, zero-length DATAGRAM frames bypass datagram_receive_buffer_size), GHSA-4w2j-m93h-cj5j (2026-06-22, out-of-order stream reassembly memory, bypassed again by GHSA-qfwj-vfxf-92j2), GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c (2026-09-30, MAX_STREAM_DATA opens streams over limit); quiche 9 GHSAs incl CVE-2026-12523 (H3/QPACK, 2026-07-14). Spec: draft-ietf-webtrans-http3-16 (2026-07-06, in WGLC, expires 2027-01-07): no numeric session cap; servers SHOULD rate-limit sessions; MUST limit buffered streams/datagrams; SETTINGS_WT_INITIAL_MAX_{STREAMS_UNI,STREAMS_BIDI,DATA}; Origin MUST be verified for browser sessions. Rust candidates: wtransport 0.7.2 (2026-08-11, 1.06M dl, 11 unsafe hits mostly varint/bytes, no fuzz dir, 0 advisories, rides quinn) and h3-webtransport 0.1.2 + h3 0.0.8 (both 2025-05-06, stale 17 months; h3 has a fuzz dir, 1 unsafe). 0 advisories on wtransport reflects low scrutiny plus quinn inheriting the findings.
specifics: WebTransport is the front end that most strains one core: it is multi-stream + datagram + capsule over a QUIC connection shared across sessions, so budgets must be hierarchical (connection > session > stream/datagram) and datagram queue must be a drop-oldest bounded ring with byte accounting that counts zero-length frames as nonzero cost.
overclaim_risk: Go-library CVEs do not transfer to Rust; quinn findings affect plain h3 equally.
underclaim_risk: Standard is unfinished (draft-16), so freezing a WebTransport interface in the golden is premature; conservative to leave it out of v1.

verify.note: Quinn advisory count explorer-only; draft in WGLC.

title: Webhooks: missing signature checks, timing-unsafe compare, replay windows, and SSRF with DNS-rebinding TOCTOU on delivery
summary: Inbound (receiver): missing verification: n8n CVE-2026-56357 (GitHub trigger, 2026-06-22) and CVE-2026-56360 (Zendesk, 2026-07-08), OneUptime CVE-2026-33143 (2026-03-20); timing-unsafe compare: pay-rails CVE-2026-70658 (2026-09-14, Ruby == on HMAC, fixed 11.6.2). Replay: GitHub's validation doc has no timestamp or nonce at all (X-Hub-Signature-256 only); Stripe signs t.payload, default tolerance 300 s, 'tolerance 0 disables recency check', retries get fresh timestamp+signature for up to 3 days so event-id dedup is the real replay control; Standard Webhooks signs msg_id.timestamp.payload (HMAC-SHA256 v1 / ed25519 v1a), recommends tolerance and id dedup (e.g. 5 min in Redis). Outbound (callback registration, an egress concern the ingress core must not forget): validate-at-registration then re-resolve-at-delivery TOCTOU: PraisonAI CVE-2026-57114 (2026-10-23), Firefly III CVE-2026-71250 (2026-08-05), Plane CVE-2026-104973 (2026-10-05, a fix-of-fix of CVE-2026-30242), Gogs CVE-2026-47267 (redirects to 169.254.169.254), Postiz CVE-2026-34590 (only create endpoint validated), CVE-2026-72761 (NAT64/6to4/Teredo pass an is_global check). Rust: standardwebhooks crate 1.0.1 (2024-03-04, 92k dl, forbid(unsafe), 349 LOC, manual constant-time compare, 300 s tolerance, requires UTF-8 payload, verify() has no id dedup) vs svix 2.9.0 (2026-10-23).
specifics: Webhooks break 'normalize first': signature is over RAW bytes, so the core must hand the verifier the untouched body (Stripe: 'any manipulation causes failure'; GitHub: proxies must not modify). Verification is a per-route, per-provider module with core-supplied primitives: raw-body capture with size cap, constant-time compare (subtle), replay store (id dedup TTL >= tolerance and >= provider retry horizon), egress guard. The 349-LOC crate is small enough to vendor and prove.
overclaim_risk: Most webhook CVEs are in apps, not servers; a server can only supply primitives, not make apps call them.
underclaim_risk: SSRF-at-delivery sits outside ingress but is the highest-count webhook CVE class in 2026 and a server that offers a 'register callback' API inherits it.

verify.note: Mostly app CVEs; Stripe/GitHub/Standard Webhooks docs stable.

title: SSE: parser-side CVEs are client-side; server-side risk is a budget class (connection count, retry storms) with no CVE stream
summary: 2026 SSE CVEs found are client parsers: MCP PHP SDK CVE-2026-53965 (2026-08-25, unbounded buffer until delimiter), httpx2 CVE-2026-84378 (2026-09-02, quadratic line buffering), Spring CVE-2026-47890 (stream corruption). No server-side connection-exhaustion CVE surfaced, consistent with it being a configuration-budget class rather than a parser bug. WHATWG SSE: no numeric per-origin connection cap, default reconnect 'a few seconds', server controls reconnect via retry: field (ms) and Last-Event-ID: a server that emits small retry values or resumes expensive replays creates its own reconnect storm; HTTP/1.1 browsers limit ~6 connections/origin, h2 multiplexes so 1 connection holds many streams. Relevant to MCP streamable HTTP, which uses SSE.
specifics: Core budgets: max concurrent streams per principal and per IP, idle/keepalive timer with comment pings, max replay window for Last-Event-ID, jittered server-enforced minimum retry:, write-side backpressure with disconnect on slow reader. These are the same budget primitives as WebSocket; no front-end-specific parser.
overclaim_risk: Absence of server CVEs is absence of evidence from search aggregators.
underclaim_risk: Reconnect storms are a design property under agent swarms; no CVE does not mean low risk.

verify.note: Absence claim; recommended numbers are explorer's own.

title: TCP/UDP stream proxy: PROXY-protocol spoofing CVEs (3 in 2026) and QUIC/UDP amplification accounting bugs
summary: PROXY protocol: Puma CVE-2026-47737 (2026-07-14, repeated PROXY v1 headers on keep-alive overwrite client address), Netty codec CVE-2026-59919 (2026-07-29, CRLF injection via AF_UNIX address), ProxySQL CVE-2026-48772 (2026-06-19, v1 UNKNOWN frame parsed, spoofed address defeats ACL; default trusted networks '*'). Spec (haproxy proxy-protocol.txt): receiver MUST NOT guess whether header is present, MUST NOT process connection before a complete valid header, only trusted proxies allowed, v1 max 107 bytes, malformed => abort, suggested header timeout >=3 s; senders on multiplexed connections must not use it. Rust: ppp 2.3.0 (2025-02-14, 3.6M dl), proxy-protocol-codec 0.3.1 (2026-03-27, 74k dl). UDP amplification: Netty QUIC CVE-2026-44894 (2026-06-12, default token handler marks every address validated), OpenSSL QUIC CVE-2026-35191 (2026-09-29, coalesced packets overcount 3x credit when address validation disabled). Envoy threat model: tcp_proxy and udp_proxy are 'robust_to_untrusted_downstream' only (upstream assumed trusted), contrib extensions not covered, unsafe defaults are out of scope, and DoS counts only at >=100x the configured limit.
specifics: L4 proxy sits below the HTTP normalization core: it has no request, no origin, no content-type. It can only enforce connection-level budgets, TLS/SNI policy, PROXY-header trust (explicit CIDR allowlist, once per connection, strict v1/v2 parser, UNKNOWN => real addr), and UDP anti-amplification (3x until validated; stateless retry). It should be a separate feature crate with its own TCB line, not part of the HTTP core.
overclaim_risk: Servers in this slot may not need TCP/UDP proxying in v1; threat evidence is for the module if built.
underclaim_risk: Envoy's own posture says L4 modules are hardened one-way only; a 'same core' claim for L4 would overclaim.

verify.note: Non-Rust CVEs; Envoy threat model paraphrased.

title: Fuzzing status: OSS-Fuzz covers only hyperium/http and httparse among these Rust ingress crates
summary: google/oss-fuzz projects/ (2026-10-25): hyperium (builds the http crate fuzz_http, address sanitizer, libfuzzer), httparse; no entries for tungstenite, tokio-tungstenite, fastwebsockets, tonic, h2, hyper, quinn, wtransport, async-graphql, connect-rust, standardwebhooks. 'h3' in OSS-Fuzz is uber/h3 (geospatial), NOT hyperium/h3. In-repo cargo-fuzz dirs: tungstenite, fastwebsockets, h3, async-graphql parser; none in tonic, connect-rust, wtransport, tokio-tungstenite. Non-Rust differential oracles exist in OSS-Fuzz: graphql-java, grpc-go, grpc-py, grpc-swift, libwebsockets, grpc-gateway. title: Which failure classes the normalization core handles once vs per front end
summary: Core once (byte/frame/time/identity primitives): connection and stream-count caps; per-principal memory/CPU budgets; header-list/frame/message byte caps (including post-inflate); slow-reader/idle timers; Origin typed check; canonical route identity; Upgrade state machine (101 gate); PROXY-header trust; UDP amplification 3x; Content-Type allowlist and method safety policy. Per front end (body-semantic): GraphQL static cost (IBM model), alias/directive/batch counts; gRPC message framing, per-message decode size and deadline propagation (grpc-timeout header, max 8 digits); webhook raw-body signature + replay store + provider schema; WebTransport capsule and datagram queue semantics; SSE replay window; WebSocket subprotocol and per-message authz (CSWSH covers handshake only; per-message authz is app-level). Evidence: of roughly 45 distinct CVE/GHSA ids in the sibling nodes, about two thirds are core-class (resource, desync, origin, identity) and one third body-semantic.
specifics: Counting is by the author from the ids in sibling nodes; classification is judgment.
overclaim_risk: Classification is my own, n=~40 distinct ids across the 12 sibling nodes; not a statistical result.
underclaim_risk: Per-front-end logic is smaller than feared because it outputs a scalar charged to a core budget.

verify.note: Self-classified tally.

title: R-ING-1 amendment: the one-core verdict survives for the HTTP family only if split into an L4 connection core and an L7 exchange core; stream proxy is outside it
summary: Verdict test per front end: WebSocket, SSE, gRPC/Connect, GraphQL and webhooks all arrive as HTTP exchanges (h1 Upgrade or h2/h3 Extended CONNECT or POST), so one normalized exchange model works for them (consistent with w02.ingress-design-verdict, which rested on indirect evidence; this adds failure-class evidence). Three things break the naive 'normalized Request' core: (a) long-lived multi-message exchanges (WS, gRPC streaming, SSE, WebTransport) need budgets per message and per lifetime, so the core object must be an Exchange with a frame/message stream, not a Request; (b) TCP/UDP proxying has no HTTP semantics and Envoy classifies it as downstream-hardened only, so it must be a separate module beneath the L7 core; (c) webhook signatures need raw bytes, so normalization must be non-destructive (retain raw body with cap) and be skippable. Strongest strain: WebTransport (hierarchical connection/session/stream/datagram budgets over a draft-stage spec). Recommended: keep one core; defer WebTransport and UDP proxying out of the golden v1; gate every other front end as a cargo feature.
specifics: Reversal condition: if a front end needs to bypass or reorder the core's budget accounting (e.g. gRPC deadline propagation needing end-to-end semantics) the core API must grow a hook, and if >2 hooks per front end appear, per-protocol stacks win.
overclaim_risk: Judgment from failure-class evidence, not from building it; gate score 0.41 means this overlaps w02 and is an extension.
underclaim_risk: I found no evidence that per-protocol stacks lower risk; each stack re-implements the same budgets (Pingora's 2026 batch shows even the shared core had defaults bugs).

verify.note: Recommendation built on unverified matrix; directionally consistent.

title: L5: per-front-end budget table with pins, config keys, defaults and CI assertions
summary: BUDGET TABLE (golden v1 proposal; all numbers are proposals to be tuned by BENCH_PLAN, not measurements). Core (L4 conn): max_conns_global, max_conns_per_ip=256, header_read_timeout=10 s, idle=60 s, PROXY header trust = explicit CIDR list, empty by default. H2/H3: max_concurrent_streams<=100 (hyper default 200), max_header_list_size=16 KiB (hyper default; Pingora learned 16 MiB is wrong), max_local_error_reset_streams=1024, empty-DATA-frame cap per RFC (h2>=0.4.16). WebSocket (tungstenite 0.30.x or fastwebsockets 0.10.x, no deflate): max_message=1 MiB, max_frame=64 KiB, max_write_buffer<=4x max_message, Origin allowlist required (deny null), ping interval 30 s, close on 2 missed pongs, per-conn message rate token bucket. SSE: max_streams_per_principal=8, keepalive comment 15 s, replay window 1000 events, retry>=3000 ms with jitter. gRPC/Connect (tonic 0.14.6 or connectrpc 0.9.x): max_decoding_message_size=1 MiB (tonic default 4 MiB), explicit max_concurrent_streams, grpc-timeout upper bound 30 s default, canonical-path authz only. GraphQL (async-graphql 7.2.1 behind core): body<=64 KiB, depth<=12, complexity per IBM cost <=1000, aliases<=15, directives<=10, batch<=1, introspection off in prod, POST application/json only. Webhook receiver (standardwebhooks 1.0.1 vendored): raw body<=1 MiB, tolerance 300 s, id dedup TTL>=max(tolerance, provider retry horizon), constant-time compare via subtle, secrets rotation list>=2. WebTransport: out of golden v1; if built: sessions<=4/conn, datagram queue<=64 KiB drop-oldest, zero-length frames cost>=1, Origin MUST. UDP/TCP stream: separate crate, off by default.
specifics: CI gate: a test boots the server with default config and asserts effective limits via an h2 client (SETTINGS frame), WS oversize close code 1009, GraphQL over-limit 4xx, webhook replay rejection. Fail build if any limit is None/unbounded in the effective config dump.
overclaim_risk: Numbers are untested proposals; bad values would cause false rejections of legitimate agent traffic.
underclaim_risk: Defaults-as-bugs record (Pingora CVE-2026-105297, tonic stream cap, async-graphql None limits) justifies a fail-closed config.

title: L5: ingress conformance and fuzz harness spec (differential oracles and acceptance criteria)
summary: Harness per class with oracle: (1) CSWSH matrix: Origin absent/null/foreign/case-variant/trailing-dot/port-variant x cookie present/absent x route allowlist; acceptance: only listed origins upgrade. (2) Upgrade desync: send 'GET + Upgrade' followed immediately by a second pipelined request and by garbage, with backend replying 200/400/101/101-with-wrong-Accept; acceptance: no byte forwarded pre-101, differential vs hyper and Pingora 0.9. (3) Deflate: not negotiated; Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate must be ignored or declined (test returns no extension); if enabled later, 1 KiB bomb expanding to 1 GiB must close 1009 within 10 ms and RSS delta <1 MiB. (4) gRPC: :path without leading slash, double slash, percent-encoded, and case variants must either 404 or canonicalize before authz; 1-byte DATA frame flood of 10^6 frames per stream must hold RSS under budget (regression for CVE-2026-84304 and RUSTSEC-2026-0258). (5) GraphQL: text/plain POST => 415; GET mutation => 405; 10k aliases => reject; OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged 10k repeats => reject in <50 ms. (6) Webhook: replay within tolerance rejected via id store; tolerance 0 rejected at config load; non-constant-time compare detected by lint (clippy disallowed-methods on ==). (7) PROXY: two v1 headers on keep-alive, UNKNOWN with fields, CRLF in AF_UNIX path, header from untrusted peer. Tooling: cargo-fuzz targets per codec + the tungstenite/fastwebsockets fuzz dirs as seeds; one Docker-free Rust test crate; run under heavy.sh. Acceptance: all classes green; every CVE id cited here has a named regression test.
overclaim_risk: Test list derived from CVEs; unknown-unknown classes need continued fuzzing.

title: Zero-downtime listener handoff: five mechanisms, one invariant
summary: Mechanisms: (a) fd inheritance via exec (nginx NGINX env, tableflip, shellflip), (b) SCM_RIGHTS over a UDS (HAProxy -x, Envoy hot restart, Pingora --upgrade, Proxygen Socket Takeover), (c) systemd socket unit / fd store holding the socket outside the process, (d) bind-with-SO_REUSEPORT in a second process (loses queued conns, rejected by Cloudflare/HAProxy), (e) kernel socket migration (tcp_migrate_req + BPF select) or BPF-steered REUSEPORT groups (nginx quic_bpf). The only mechanism class with zero queue loss by construction is one where the same kernel socket object (same accept queue) stays open throughout: (a)(b)(c).
overclaim_risk: Not every mechanism was benchmarked by us; loss rates are vendor/blog-reported.
underclaim_risk: Kernel socket migration (5.14+) narrows the gap for SO_REUSEPORT designs; do not dismiss it.

verify.note: Synthesis; HAProxy fd-transfer 0/1/11 verified; mechanism (e) lacks primary URL.

title: Same-socket handoff beats SO_REUSEPORT-second-process for accept-queue integrity; REUSEPORT needs explicit claim/close discipline
summary: A second process binding with SO_REUSEPORT creates a separate kernel socket with its own accept queue; closing the old one resets queued connections (HAProxy measured 2-3 resets per million connections per reload; 155 per million after 180 reloads at 55k conn/s, 10 reloads/s, kernel 4.9). Passing the existing fd keeps the queue (HAProxy ab test: restart 11/2000 failed, plain reload 1, fd transfer 0). With REUSEPORT groups passed by fd, every received fd MUST be claimed or closed or it black-holes its share (Proxygen paper; Pingora close_unclaimed). Envoy: decreasing worker concurrency across a hot restart can drop accept-queue connections.
overclaim_risk: Loss numbers are from 2017 kernel 4.9 and a vendor blog (HAProxy Tech), small samples.
underclaim_risk: Modern kernels with tcp_migrate_req may reduce this; no independent measurement found.

verify.note: 2017 kernel 4.9 lab numbers verified; tiny ab sample; tcp_migrate_req mitigates if enabled.

title: HAProxy seamless reload (fd transfer over CLI socket), 1.8 (2017)
summary: New process connects to old process's stats/CLI unix socket (requires bind option expose-fd listeners; reload with -x <sock> -sf <pid>); old sends listener fds with SCM_RIGHTS; max 253 listeners in the 2017 design. Source: src/cli.c _getsocks sends MAX_SEND_FD fds per sendmsg, expose-fd only accepts 'listeners' (ACCESS_FD_LISTENERS). Extends gap.haproxy.

verify.note: 253-listener limit is historical 2017 design.

title: nginx binary upgrade (USR2/WINCH/QUIT) and reload (HUP)
summary: USR2: master renames pidfile to .oldbin, execs new binary with env NGINX="fd;fd;..." (ngx_exec_new_binary in src/core/nginx.c builds it from cycle->listening; ngx_add_inherited_sockets getenv-parses it). Old master keeps listen sockets so it can spawn workers on rollback (HUP to old, QUIT to new). WINCH drains old workers; QUIT old commits. Mixed old/new workers both accept during overlap. Reload (HUP) keeps same master and listening sockets, closes only idle keepalive.

verify.note: Canonical documented behaviour; line numbers drift.

title: Envoy hot restart: UDS datagram RPC, new process initializes first, then requests listeners
summary: Child fully initializes (config, initial discovery, health checks) before asking the parent for listen sockets (pass_listen_socket by worker index for reuse_port sockets); parent then drained (--drain-time-s) and shut down (--parent-shutdown-time-s, should exceed drain). Counters/gauges transferred; connections are NOT. Source: source/server/hot_restarting_{base,parent,child}.cc; AF_UNIX SOCK_DGRAM at <socket_path>_<role>_<base_id+id>, fchmod(socket_mode); one SCM_RIGHTS fd per message. Extends gap.envoy.

verify.note: Docs consistent; 'no shared memory' negative not re-fetched.

title: Pingora graceful upgrade: --upgrade + upgrade socket + SIGQUIT; source-level hardening evidence
summary: New instance started with --upgrade requests listeners over a configured UDS; SIGQUIT to old triggers transfer then graceful shutdown. pingora-core/src/server/transfer_fd/mod.rs (737 lines): MAX_FDS=32 per recvmsg, MAX_RETRY=5 at 1s, nonblocking send polls 20x500ms; recvmsg uses MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC with an in-code rationale (subprocess exec'd by app would otherwise keep the port bound after server exit); close_unclaimed() closes inherited SO_REUSEPORT fds absent from the new config because 'an unclaimed SO_REUSEPORT socket ... can black-hole connections'; tests assert FD_CLOEXEC and no fd leak. Extends gap.pingora and w02.pingora-tokio-panic context.
overclaim_risk: Docs describe no guarantee for in-flight connections beyond grace period; do not read 'no connection refused' as 'no connection dropped'.

verify.note: close_unclaimed corroborated by Proxygen paper.

title: Facebook Zero Downtime Release (SIGCOMM 2020): Socket Takeover, Downstream Connection Reuse, Partial Post Replay
summary: Naseer, Niccolini, Pant, Frindell, Dasineni, Benson; doi 10.1145/3387514.3405885, pp 529-541. Socket Takeover passes all listening FDs (TCP and UDP VIPs) via SCM_RIGHTS; for QUIC/UDP the new process user-space-routes packets of pre-existing flows to the old process by connection ID during drain. Edge L7 drain 20 min; app servers 10-15 s; release time 25 min (app tier) and 90 min (L7LB); +15-20% effective L7LB CPU capacity; takeover costs <1% idle CPU (parallel process); binary updates ~47% of releases; hard restart of 10% of Origin proxies made the app cluster spend 20% of CPU rebuilding state; PPR uses HTTP 379 to replay partial POSTs to another server.
overclaim_risk: Hyperscaler scale and a Katran L4 tier it relies on; not directly transferable to a single VPS.
underclaim_risk: The failure-mode section (orphan sockets, fd leaks, kernel GSO bug surviving restarts) is the most transferable content.

verify.note: Peer-reviewed but hyperscaler self-reported 2020; figures not re-verified.

title: systemd file descriptor store + socket units for the single-node household upgrade
summary: FileDescriptorStoreMax= (default 0=off); service pushes fds with sd_pid_notify_with_fds FDSTORE=1 (+FDNAME, FDPOLL=0 to avoid auto-removal on POLLHUP/ERR); returned at next start through LISTEN_FDS/LISTEN_FDNAMES/LISTEN_PID/LISTEN_PIDFDID; FDSTOREREMOVE=1 required when the service closes its copy; store kept across a restart job but cleared on full stop unless FileDescriptorStorePreserve=yes|on-success; NotifyAccess= restricts who may modify (default main PID only; =all for child processes); systemd-analyze fdstore lists. kexec/LUO preserves memfd only (sockets dropped). systemd.socket: Accept=no passes sockets to one service; Backlog= default 4294967295 silently capped by net.core.somaxconn (usually 4096); FlushPending=no keeps pending conns for restarted service; ReusePort= option exists. A restart via fdstore keeps listener queue but kills accepted connections of the old process: it gives zero-refusal, not zero-drop.
overclaim_risk: Cannot by itself preserve accepted connections.
underclaim_risk: Combined with an in-process child-spawn handover (shellflip-style) it covers both queue and accepted connections on one node.

verify.note: somaxconn default kernel-dependent (4096 on 5.4+).

title: Caddy config reload: graph-swap via admin API, drain-or-grace_period semantics
summary: caddy reload = POST /load; failed config keeps old config running; identical config skipped unless --force; reload call blocks until requests on old config finish, long-lived WebSocket/SSE/downloads stall it unless the global grace_period option cancels them. Not a binary upgrade (same process), so no fd handoff and no binary swap. STEK: modules/caddytls/sessiontickets.go RotationInterval default 12h, MaxKeys default 4, 32-byte keys; distributed_stek (storage-coordinated) for clusters. Extends gap.caddy.
overclaim_risk: Reload semantics taken from community answers plus source; official doc page not fetched.

verify.note: Forum thread primary; master source may change.

title: Kernel SO_REUSEPORT socket migration (tcp_migrate_req) and its 2026 bug
summary: Iwashima 11-patch series (v8 2021-06, LKML) adds net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req and BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE: on close()/shutdown() of a listener, queued established and SYN_RECV children migrate to a sibling listener in the same reuseport group; without a BPF program kernel picks a random live listener; mismatched socket options (e.g. TCP_SAVE_SYN) can crash apps. CVE-2026-46015 (published 2026-05-27, modified 2026-10-19, CVSS3.1 7.8 per INCIBE page): sk_data_ready() not called after migration in inet_csk_listen_stop, so epoll/accept waiters on the target listener can sleep forever; affected ranges 5.14..<5.15.209, 5.16..<6.1.175, 6.2..<6.6.140, 6.7..<6.12.86, 6.13..<6.18.27, 6.19..<7.0.4. Implication: a kernel-migration-based design must pin kernels >= those fixes and add an accept-liveness watchdog.
overclaim_risk: CVE data from a single aggregator page (not cross-checked against NVD/kernel.org); sysctl default and 5.14 mainline version from search snippet.

verify.note: INCIBE verified (2026-05-27, CVSS 7.8, fix list matches, modified 2026-10-19); tcp_migrate_req opt-in default off; CVSS likely inflated for a missed wakeup.

title: Orphan fd failure modes: black-holed REUSEPORT sockets and leaked sockets surviving process death
summary: Proxygen paper section 5.1: (i) if the new process ignores a received SO_REUSEPORT fd without closing or listening, the kernel keeps routing its share of packets/connections there and they idle until timeout; (ii) a passed fd is equivalent to dup(), so leaked fds keep the socket (and its buffers) alive after the process terminates; a UDP GSO kernel bug accumulated buffers and a process restart did not clear it because the socket object persisted. Remediations in paper: explicit ready acknowledgement before old process drains, dynamic disable switch for takeover, version-compat of the takeover protocol, Katran LRU connection-table cache. Independent corroboration: Pingora close_unclaimed + MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC comments (2026 tree).

verify.note: Two independent sources agree.

title: HTTP/2 graceful drain = two GOAWAYs (RFC 9113 s6.8); what drops vs what is retried
summary: Server SHOULD send initial GOAWAY with last_stream_id=2^31-1 and NO_ERROR, wait >= 1 RTT for in-flight stream creation, then send a second GOAWAY with the real last stream id; endpoints MUST NOT increase last_stream_id; streams above it were not processed and are safely retriable; a client unable to retry (e.g. intermediary serving non-H2 clients) loses in-flight requests. Fetched from rfc-editor.org 2026-10-25. Implication: drain deadline D must exceed longest tolerated request; requests/streams crossing D are lost unless the app supports Proxygen-style partial replay.

verify.note: RFC text; double GOAWAY is a SHOULD-level practice.

title: QUIC across restarts: CID routing is the only way; nginx quic_bpf, Proxygen user-space forwarding, QUIC-LB draft
summary: UDP has no accept queue: during a handover the 4-tuple hash can send packets of an old connection to the new process, which has no state. Proxygen forwards by connection ID in user space to the old process. nginx quic_bpf (Linux 5.7+; since 1.31.7 per docs fetched 2026-10-25) uses eBPF CID routing to keep established QUIC connections across reload and live upgrade; cannot be toggled on reload; quic_host_key default regenerated per reload so old Retry/stateless-reset tokens are rejected. IETF draft-ietf-quic-load-balancers-22 (2026-10-23, expires 2027-04-26): server ID in CID (3-bit config rotation, AES-ECB single-pass or 4-round Feistel), sec 6.4 non-normative process demux. Decision: AEGIS H3 can ship with 'connection loss on upgrade, clients reconnect via 0-RTT/new CID' unless CID-routing is implemented.
overclaim_risk: nginx 1.31.7 version number taken from the doc page; not verified in release notes.

verify.note: nginx docs: 1.31.7 preserves QUIC conns across reload/live upgrade (quic_bpf itself 1.25.0, Linux 5.7+); cannot toggle on reload; QUIC-LB draft-22 2026-10-23.

title: STEK continuity across reload/upgrade/scale-out: lifetimes in the wild and in code
summary: Springall/Durumeric/Halderman IMC 2016 (Alexa top-1M, 9-week scan): 354,697 domains issued tickets; 38% of sites decryptable >24h after a server compromise and 10% >30 days; STEK reuse: 41% daily-unique, 22% >=7 days, 10% (28,210) >=30 days; 12 Alexa-top-100 sites reused >=30 days. Implementation facts: nginx auto-rotated keys live in the ssl_session_cache shared zone (3 slots, RAND_bytes(80), expire=now+session timeout; since 1.23.2) else random-per-start unless ssl_session_ticket_key files (first encrypts, rest decrypt-only); Caddy 12h rotation, 4 keys max (so worst-case key life ~48h); Cloudflare (2015) hourly random keys from in-memory daemon, kept 18h, never on disk; rustls TicketRotator: ticketer valid for >=1 and <=2 lifetimes. Inference (unverified): nginx binary upgrade creates a fresh shm zone so tickets from the old master stop resuming; our design should pass the ring explicitly.
overclaim_risk: 2016 data; TLS1.3 tickets are PSK-based so forward secrecy is lost differently; do not quote percentages as current.
underclaim_risk: Cross-vhost ticket scoping is already a separate map node (crs-ce-tls-ticket-cross-vhost).

verify.note: nginx docs do not state 3 slots/rotation/USR2 behaviour; 2015-16 data predates TLS 1.3.

title: Cloudflare 2025-11-18: globally pushed auto-generated config exceeded proxy limit, Rust unwrap panic
summary: 11:20-14:30 UTC main impact (~3h10), full resolution 17:06 (5h46 total). A ClickHouse permissions change doubled the Bot Management feature file (limit 200 features, ~60 used); FL2 proxy panicked on Result::unwrap(); file regenerated every 5 min and pushed network-wide giving flapping good/bad states; fix: stop propagation, manually insert known-good file, force core proxy restart. Remediations: treat internally generated config like user input, add global kill switches. Lesson for AEGIS: reload path must (1) validate+parse in a staging context before swap, (2) keep last-known-good on any error (Caddy semantic), (3) never panic on config ingest, (4) canary the push.

verify.note: All times/limits/unwrap verified; root cause was ClickHouse permission change doubling output, not operator push.

title: Drain-forever failure: old workers linger with long-lived connections (HAProxy, nginx, Caddy, Envoy)
summary: HAProxy soft-stop old workers live until last connection closes; mitigations hard-stop-after (since 1.7.4), reload-storm leaks of fds and memory documented on Discourse/GitLab (community grade); nginx 2017-09 thread: limit_conn drops/memory growth with frequent reloads, old workers up to 30 min; Red Hat bz1320233 OpenShift router reload per endpoint resync dropping connections (fix: <=1 reload per sync); Caddy reload blocks on WebSocket/SSE until grace_period; Envoy needs --drain-time-s < --parent-shutdown-time-s. Implication: every drain needs a hard deadline, a metric for old-generation connection count, and rate-limited reloads (coalesce).
overclaim_risk: Mostly forum/vendor-blog evidence; no dated formal postmortem of a reload-induced outage at a named company found except Cloudflare 2025 config push (different mechanism).

title: Reload as attack surface: env-var fd injection, unauthenticated handoff socket, fd leaks, privilege at re-exec
summary: (1) nginx NGINX env var is trusted: any party able to set the env of the exec'd binary can make nginx adopt arbitrary inherited fd numbers as listeners (src/core/nginx.c ngx_add_inherited_sockets; no type/addr verification before ngx_set_inherited_sockets). (2) Envoy hot-restart IPC is an unauthenticated AF_UNIX datagram socket protected only by filesystem mode; RELEASE_ASSERT aborts on unexpected cmsg; GitHub issue envoyproxy/envoy#45872 (2026-06-29, OPEN, reporter-assigned CVSS 6.1 AV:L) wire-length+8 overflow -> resize(0) -> heap overflow; main already carries a guard dropping datagrams with length > UINT64_MAX-8. (3) HAProxy expose-fd listeners grants fd-extraction to anyone with access to that CLI socket level. (4) leaked listener fds into children keep ports bound after exit (Pingora MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC comment). (5) a new binary is code execution with the old process's privileges: path must be pinned and hash/signature-verified. Mitigations for AEGIS: handover socket created by supervisor with SO_PEERCRED uid+pid check, abstract-free path under 0700 dir, validate each received fd (SO_TYPE, SO_ACCEPTCONN, getsockname == configured bind), strict length caps, no panics (return error), ASLR-independent; fuzz the handover parser.
overclaim_risk: Envoy #45872 is an unconfirmed reporter claim (AV:L, needs local socket write); nginx env injection requires pre-existing control of the exec environment (not a remote vector).

title: Horizontal scale-out: what state must be shared and the option per state
summary: STEK: (a) per-node random keys (resumption only on same node; zero coordination), (b) shared ring from storage (Caddy distributed_stek; Cloudflare in-memory daemon + replication; nginx ssl_session_ticket_key files), (c) derive epoch keys from a shared master secret by HKDF(master, epoch) [design option, no cited production example]. Rate limit: local-only (Envoy local limit multiplies by replica count), per-site consistent-hash counters (Cloudflare Twemproxy), gossip aggregation (Raghavan 2007), Redis atomic Lua (centralized). Idempotency keys: need a linearizable create-if-absent keyed by (client,key) with 409/422 semantics (IETF draft -08 says nothing on multi-node): single-owner by consistent hashing of key, or DB unique constraint. Sessions: stateless sealed tokens vs shared store. Audit log: one sequencer per log (Tessera assigns contiguous durable indices per batch, order within batch unspecified, checkpoint needs witness cosignatures) so multi-node means one log per node or a single sequencing service. Extends abuse-rate-limit-algos-crates, sdg-idempotency-draft, ops.audit-log-spec, crs-ce-stek-lifecycle.

title: L5: AEGIS in-place upgrade protocol (single node, systemd) with invariants UP-1..UP-7
summary: Actors: S=systemd (Type=notify, FileDescriptorStoreMax=64, NotifyAccess=all, FileDescriptorStorePreserve=yes), A=serving process, B=new binary. Steps: (0) A holds flock(/run/aegis/upgrade.lock) -> one upgrade at a time. (1) `aegisctl upgrade <path>`: control socket (0700 dir, SO_PEERCRED uid==service uid) ; A verifies B's sha256+signature against pinned release key; runs `B --check-config` (parse+validate, no bind). (2) A spawns B on a dedicated pre-seccomp thread with listener fds (CLOEXEC cleared only in pre_exec), handover pipe (carries: STEK ring with ids+ages, generation counter, rate-limit snapshot optional), completion pipe; LISTEN_PID rewritten. (3) B validates every inherited fd (SO_TYPE, SO_ACCEPTCONN, getsockname == config bind), claims or closes the rest, starts accept loops, writes ACCEPTING; (4) A on ACCEPTING sends sd_notify MAINPID=<B>, pushes FDSTORE=1 for B's fds (or B does), stops its own accept loops (does NOT close listener fds until B ACK_OWNS), sends H2 GOAWAY(2^31-1) -> >=1 RTT -> GOAWAY(last), starts drain with deadline D (default 30 s, hard max configurable); (5) at drain end or empty, A closes sockets, zeroizes STEK ring memory, exits 0. (6) Failure before ACCEPTING: A kills B, unchanged. After ACCEPTING but B crashes: A still holds listener fds and resumes accept loops (rollback window W=10 s). Invariants: UP-1 (queue safety) every listening kernel socket is open in >=1 live process at all times, and no accept queue is ever closed while non-empty without a process polling it. UP-2 (no orphan) after ACK_OWNS no process holds a SO_REUSEPORT listener fd that no accept loop services. UP-3 (graceful stream semantics) every H2 connection of A receives GOAWAY NO_ERROR with last_stream_id >= highest stream it began processing; streams above are un-processed. UP-4 (bounded drain) A exits <= D + epsilon after ACCEPTING; connections open past D are closed and counted (aegis_upgrade_forced_close_total); thus 'no accepted connection dropped before D'. UP-5 (STEK) tickets are encrypted only with a key younger than L_enc and accepted only while key age < L_enc+L_dec (defaults 12h/12h total <=24h); the ring crosses processes only via the handover pipe, never disk; if handover pipe is missing/corrupt B generates a fresh ring (all old tickets fail -> full handshake, never accept-unknown). Key ids unique (128-bit random). A zeroizes on exit. UP-6 (fd hygiene) all non-listener fds CLOEXEC; no fd leaks into helper subprocesses; fd count of A+B <= base + K. UP-7 (config safety) a failing B (config invalid, panic, hang >T_init) never reduces A's service; handover parser returns errors, never panics, caps all lengths. QUIC: out of scope in golden v1 (H3 connections reset on upgrade; clients reconnect) unless CID-routed.
specifics: Crate pins to evaluate: nix 0.31.x (recvmsg, MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC), sd-notify 0.5.0 (notify_with_fds, FdStore), shellflip 2.1.3 only as reference (BSD) - prefer ~300 LOC in-tree; rustls 0.23.46 TicketRotator for the ring semantics or custom ProducesTickets. Model in TLA+ (states: A serving, B starting, B accepting, A draining, A exited; actions incl. crash of either) to check UP-1/UP-2/UP-4.
overclaim_risk: Design synthesized from sources; no implementation run or measured yet. UP-1 in an OS sense depends on kernel behaviour not proven.
underclaim_risk: Strong existence proofs exist for each step individually (HAProxy, Envoy, Pingora, Proxygen).

title: L5: upgrade test harness and CI gate (acceptance criteria for UP-1..UP-7)
summary: Harness (implementation-phase spike; heavy: run only via tools/heavy.sh): loadgen at fixed 2k new conn/s over H1.1, H2 (long streams 5-20 s) and TLS resumption clients; perform 200 consecutive upgrades at 5/s alternating A/B binaries. Pass: 0 connect failures/refused/RST for connections initiated at any time; every in-flight H2 request either completes or sees GOAWAY with last_stream_id below its stream id (client retries successfully); forced-close counter 0 when D > longest stream. Fault injection (deterministic, one per run): SIGKILL B at each protocol step; B hangs before ACCEPTING (A must kill after T_init); invalid config; truncated/oversized handover message; wrong-uid connect to control socket; extra unexpected fd in env; second concurrent upgrade (must be refused). Assert via /proc: fd inventory (no fd without owner, listener fds CLOEXEC in children), `ss -ltn` Recv-Q on listeners never stranded, RSS bounded. STEK check: ring ids/ages logged; test with injected clock that a ticket older than L_enc+L_dec fails to resume and a ticket from before upgrade resumes after (and not after expiry). Fuzz: cargo-fuzz target on handover deserializer (no panics, bounded alloc). Negative controls: run same harness with a naive 'bind second process with SO_REUSEPORT then close' variant and require harness to FAIL it (expect ~2-3 resets/million per HAProxy; may need >=1M conns to observe) to prove oracle power. Gate: harness green on CI nightly; golden release requires 3 consecutive nights.
overclaim_risk: The negative-control loss rate may be unobservable on a small VPS (HAProxy saw errors only when CPU differed from NIC IRQ CPU).

title: CAPMAS (arXiv 2609.06500) macaroon delegation vs RFC 8693 token exchange, and a 89-source agent authorization review (arXiv 2609.15906): both Sept 2026, both self-reported
summary: CAPMAS (Veski, Guerraoui, Froelicher; 2026-09-06): contrastive-learning scoping maps natural-language queries to bounded privilege sets plus Macaroon tokens for offline attenuation; claims about 30x faster delegation ops, 2x less delegation latency and 3x lower bandwidth than OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693); over 90 percent perfect privilege-bundle retrieval within 17 ms over 3,100+ endpoints; 99.5 percent fewer unnecessary privileges. Caveat for us: its scoping step is an ML classifier deciding privileges, which re-introduces a probabilistic component in front of the authorization decision. arXiv 2609.15906 (2026-09-14, Surapani et al., 70 pages): narrative review of 89 sources; five-level principal hierarchy (user, operator, orchestrator, sub-agent, tool endpoint), seven structural requirements; names runtime enforcement and aggregation bounds as the main open gaps. overclaim_risk: Latency/bandwidth ratios are against a baseline of their choice and unspecified hardware; do not cite as evidence that macaroons beat Biscuit.

title: Refined invariant CRS (Cross-Request State) with clauses C1-C8 and definitions
summary: DEFINITIONS. Cross-request state = any state that outlives the request that created it and can affect a later request's processing or response. It exists at four levels: connection (TLS session, H2/H3 stream tables, HPACK/QPACK), process (caches, pools, counters, maps), fleet (STEK, shared cache, idempotency/session store), and client-held server-issued (tickets, NEW_TOKEN, cookies, idempotency keys). Authenticated = this server verified a cryptographic binding at the time of use, under a current, non-default key and the current policy epoch, to a scope tuple sigma = (issuer cert-chain hash, origin/authority, principal/tenant or PUBLIC, auth context {client-cert trust store id, auth method, privilege level}, config epoch). Transport-authenticated attributes (socket peer, verified client cert) authenticate only what they prove. CLAUSES. C1 Provenance: server-issued state is AEAD-sealed under a CSPRNG key that is rotated (STEK at most 24 h with a 2-key window; ticket lifetime at most 24 h, below the 7 d spec max). Startup refuses an all-zero or default key. C2 Scope: state S may influence request R only if sigma(S) == sigma(R), with sigma(R) computed per request (not per connection) and equality on every component. PUBLIC is allowed only for responses the origin marked public, with no Authorization or Set-Cookie. C3 Key completeness: every input that can change the response bytes or the authorization outcome is in the lookup key, or is stripped or normalized at ingress by the SAME parser the router and origin use. C4 Freshness: state that authorizes a side effect is single-use, or the effect is idempotent. Early data is accepted only on routes marked replay_safe, with at-most-once per ticket per instance, Early-Data: 1 forwarded, and 425 otherwise. C5 Epoch revocation: any auth or config change (login, logout, privilege change, cert/CA rotation, reload) bumps the epoch. Old-epoch state is rejected; session IDs are regenerated and pooled upstream connections drained. C6 Failure atomicity: failed validation never inserts or retains state, and a failed refresh never evicts last-good state. C7 Authority ceiling: state influenced by unauthenticated input may affect only resource budgets and address validation. Its size is capped per transport-authenticated key, refreshes triggered by unverified fields are rate-limited and negatively cached, and maps over attacker keys use secret-keyed hashing. C8 Shared-context partitioning: compression contexts, upstream connections and response queues are never shared between principals. Sensitive headers are never-indexed, and the upstream connection is closed on any framing error.
overclaim_risk: The numeric parameters (24 h, the epoch granularity) are engineering choices, not evidence-derived optima.
underclaim_risk: Treating C2 as optional for single-tenant deployments. Coalescing and vhosts make 'single tenant' rarer than it looks.
