title: Derived PoW economics: attacker cost per session vs human cost
summary: Derived (not measured by us): d=4 hex => 2^16=65,536 expected hashes; at ~2.3M hash/s native single core that is ~28 ms of CPU, ~1e-7 USD at cloud vCPU prices; d=6 => 2^24 ~ 16.7M hashes ~ 7 s native. Challenge cookie reuse (valid up to ~a week per Ormandy) amortises the cost over thousands of requests => per-request attacker cost ~0. Human side: GNOME saw ~1 min (desktop) and ~2 min (phone) waits during a link-spike. Conclusion: PoW difficulty that a phone tolerates (<~2 s) is irrelevant to a native-solver attacker; PoW is only a load-keyed speed bump and must be paired with per-session cost budgets and cheap-reject paths.
overclaim_risk: Hash rate taken from Ormandy's e2-micro; JS-in-browser rate unmeasured here; attacker actually pays for residential proxy egress (not CPU) which dominates.
underclaim_risk: Ignoring that PoW also forces attackers to run JS/WASM, raising per-request engineering cost and memory; unquantified.

verify.note: Derived; d6 ~8 s; human tail from single report.

correction: Superseded r3 by measurement: native SHA-256 62-89 MH/s single thread (not 2.3 MH/s), 1.1-3.4 GH/s multi-thread, in-browser ~150 kH/s; asymmetry 430-860x single-thread. See r3e07-pow-asymmetry-measured.

title: L5: admission-control pipeline order and default parameters for a 1 vCPU / 1-2 GB box
summary: Order is by ascending cost-to-reject; every stage must reject in O(1) memory-bounded work before the next, costlier stage. S0 listener: max 2,048 open conns; per-/32 (v4) or per-/64 (v6) conn cap 32; header-read deadline 10 s and min body rate 1 KiB/s; TLS handshakes behind a semaphore of 8. S1 pre-auth anonymous GCRA (governor 0.10.4 keyed by /32 or /64, bounded key store 65,536 entries with LRU eviction; on overflow degrade to a global anonymous bucket): 5 req/s sustained, burst 20, cost-weighted; plus a /24-/48 aggregate bucket 50 req/s burst 200. S2 identity classes: (a) Web Bot Auth-verified key id (verify only after S1 passes), (b) session-cookie humans who passed a challenge, (c) Privacy Pass redeemed (type 2 blind RSA) if an issuer is configured, (d) anonymous. S3 cost class from route table: static/cached=1, dynamic read=5, DB write/search=20, pathological (blame/log/export) =100 units; per-identity GCRA over units: anonymous 60 units/min burst 120; session 600/min burst 1,200; verified agent 1,200/min default (operator-raised by contract). S4 load-keyed challenge ladder (only active when S5 queue sojourn > 5 ms for 100 ms or concurrency at limit): weight-based like Anubis thresholds (metarefresh -> PoW d4 -> d6) applied to class (d) only, with an accessible alternative path (see invariant). S5 concurrency admission: Gradient2/Vegas-style adaptive limit start 16, min 4, max 64 (1 vCPU async; start low because CPU-bound), Percentage partition: verified 0.30, session 0.50, anonymous 0.20 floor with work-conserving borrow; queue per class max 32 entries; CoDel target 5 ms / interval 100 ms scaled to 2x handler p50, adaptive LIFO only inside the anonymous queue. S6 handler under hard CPU deadline (Wasm fuel / 250 ms wall) and DB statement_timeout 2 s; actual cost debited post hoc to the S3 bucket (negative balance allowed, GCRA TAT advances). Shed responses: per-identity -> 429 + Retry-After computed from TAT; global shed -> 503 + Retry-After 1-5 s jittered; never HTTP 200 for rejects (Anubis returns 200 for CHALLENGE/DENY, which breaks monitoring and caches). Parameter values are engineering proposals (grade E) to be calibrated by the swarm test, not measurements.
overclaim_risk: Defaults are not benchmarked; 1 vCPU numbers (2,048 conns, concurrency 16) are reasoning, not measurement.
underclaim_risk: Not specifying numbers would leave implementers to copy Anubis/nginx defaults tuned for other cost profiles.

verify.note: verifier sampled other nodes; explorer grade kept

correction: r3 simulator: r2 default parameters fail C1-C4 under a 10k-IP solver swarm (human failure 99.1%, verified success 59.7%); replaced by r3e07-L5-tuned-default-table (D) with fresh-session class, aggregate expensive-tier budgets and handshake reservation.

title: RLS plan-cache / role-change CVE family (2016-2026)
summary: Recurring bug class: cached or inlined plans keep applying policies of a prior role after user-id changes. CVE-2016-2193 (pub 2016-04-11), CVE-2023-2455 (2023-06-09, inlining; 14.8/15.3), CVE-2024-10976 (2024-11-14; subquery/WITH/security-invoker view/SQL function; 17.1/16.5/15.9/14.14/13.17/12.21; CVSS ~4.2-5.4 per source), CVE-2026-14666 (published 2026-08-13; cached RLS policies survive role membership/attribute/db-ownership changes; fixed 18.6/17.11/16.15/15.19/14.24; CVSS 4.2 AV:N/AC:H/PR:L; stale policies persist until invalidation or connection end). All need role switching inside one backend session with plan reuse - exactly what SET ROLE + pooled connections do. CVE-2023-39418 (MERGE skips UPDATE/SELECT policies, 15.4). All verified in cveawg.mitre.org.
specifics: L5: never change role on a connection that will run prepared/cached statements for another principal; one backend session = one principal for its lifetime OR use SET LOCAL ROLE only inside a txn on a connection whose plan cache is invalidated (DISCARD PLANS/ DEALLOCATE ALL) - and still treat as defense-in-depth not primary gate. Pin Postgres >= 18.6/17.11/16.15 (and subscribe to security list).
overclaim_risk: Over: CVSS 4.2 understates impact for a multi-tenant gate (confidentiality of other tenants' rows).
underclaim_risk: Under: exploitation needs app-specific plan reuse pattern; no public exploitation found.

verify.note: All 5 CVEs match; recycle pooled conns on role DDL.

revision_title: PG RLS plan-cache CVE family re-verified
revision_summary: All 5 CVEs, dates, fixed versions MATCH (cveawg). CNA CVSS 4.2 for 2024-10976 and 2026-14666 (5.4 only NVD secondary). CVE-2026-14666 trigger is role membership/attribute/ownership change during a live session -> long-lived pooled backends widen the stale window; gateway must recycle connections on role DDL.
correction: r3: CVE-2026-14666 fix 1974acf23 (no regression test) and an executed q1012 reproducer on 17.11/19rc1 (SET LOCAL ROLE + statement cache safe on patched minors; session-level set_config leaks). Advisory: stale policies persist until invalidation or session end, so recycle pooled connections after the minor upgrade.

title: LLM package hallucination rates and slopsquatting incidents (no Rust data exists)
summary: Spracklen et al. USENIX Security 2025: 16 LLMs, 576,000 Python/JS samples, >=5.2% commercial / 21.7% open-source hallucinated packages, 205,474 unique names; 58% of hallucinated names recur within 10 reruns, 43% on all 10. 2026 independent preprint (arXiv 2605.17062, Churilov): 199,845 paired prompts, 5 frontier models (Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V3.2) 4.62%-6.10%; 127 names all five invent (109 PyPI, 18 npm), 53 still registrable. Incidents: react-codeshift (npm, Jan 2026, spread to 237 repos via cloned agent skills; defensively registered), huggingface-cli (>30k downloads in 3 months), unused-imports (233 dl/week Feb 2026); HalluSquatting (Jul 2026). NO crates.io-specific measurement found in either study (gap).
overclaim_risk: The 2026 replication is a single-author preprint; incident details (react-codeshift, huggingface-cli) are via CSA secondary notes. Rates are for PyPI/npm, not crates.io; crates.io flat namespace + smaller catalogue may differ.
underclaim_risk: Rates compressed but non-zero (~5%) and repeatability (43%) is what makes it exploitable; agents with `cargo add` automation widen exposure.
specifics: L5: (a) agent sandbox has NO network write to crates.io and `cargo add` is wrapped by a script that implements sc.crates-malicious-record rules; (b) CI diff gate (sc.vet-ci-gate); (c) measure OUR agent hallucination rate: seed 500 server-coding prompts, count non-existent crate names (cargo search/crates.io API 404) = acceptance metric tracked per model release (E).

verify.note: 2605.17062 models are small/mid tier (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V3.2, GPT-5.4-mini); PyPI/npm only; single author.

correction: r3: Rust data exists (arXiv 2606.08444, Internetware 2026): headline 22.23% counts std items; re-extraction gives 6.1% of use-roots (0.7-3.0% of samples), 272 unregistered names. See sc3.slopsquat-rust-study-2606.

title: Ingress: one protocol-normalization core with feature-gated front ends beats per-protocol stacks; evidence is indirect
summary: Direct evidence: (1) the measured fixed cost of the h1+h2+TLS+PQ core is 4.21 MB/39 deps/3.3k non-crypto unsafe lines, so each additional per-protocol stack that re-links TLS/HTTP parsing multiplies that, while a shared core adds only the codec crate (+23 crates for QUIC/h3). (2) Envoy HCM filter chain, Pingora ProxyHttp phases and hyper Service all converge on one normalized http::Request model over multiple codecs (existing in-tree design, not measured). (3) Practitioner/industry reporting (PortSwigger-derived summaries Aug-Sep 2025; trackr.live 2026 opinion) locates the smuggling bug class at the seam where an h2/h3 edge translates to h1 for a backend, which a single typed normalized model with no re-serialization to text removes by construction (D-grade, secondary). (4) hyperium/h3 has no release since h3 0.0.8 on 2025-05-06 although commits continue (2026-09-20), so front-end crates evolve at different cadence; pluggability limits blast radius. Recommended structure: normalized core = http crate types + one admission/limits layer; front ends: h1, h2, h3 (QUIC), WS/SSE/WebTransport as upgrade/stream modes on the same request; gRPC/Connect/GraphQL/MCP/webhooks are request-handler layers over normalized HTTP not stacks; TCP/UDP proxy is a separate L4 path sharing only admission control and metrics. Not measured: cost of normalization copy vs zero-copy streaming; no existing project runs the whole matrix.
overclaim_risk: Seam-bug claim rests on secondary and opinion sources; no measurement here compares per-protocol stacks
underclaim_risk: Design may have extra benefits (single fuzz target, single limits budget) not captured

verify.note: Seam sources weak (trackr.live looks SEO/AI-generated); primary sources should be PortSwigger research and CVEs; normalization copy cost unmeasured.

correction: r3: copy cost measured (zero-copy Bytes 0 userspace copies, owned codec +0.58-0.72 ms per 10 MB at 1 core); core object must be an Exchange with a message stream; L4/PROXY handling separate below L7; WebTransport and permessage-deflate deferred from golden v1 (r3e09.ring1-verdict-amendment, w02.norm-copy-cost-measured).

title: Invariant: Attenuation monotonicity
summary: Denotation [[t]] is a subset of Requests × Time. For every token t and every block or caveat b, [[append(t, b)]] ⊆ [[t]]. For policy updates p -> p' accepted without human approval: [[p']] ⊆ [[p]] (SMT-checked as `implies(p', p)`). For delegation chains: [[t_k]] ⊆ [[t_{k-1}]] ⊆ ... ⊆ [[t_0]] ⊆ ceiling(issuer).
specifics: Lean: define `denote : Token → Request → Prop` with denote (append t b) r := denote t r ∧ caveat b r, so monotonicity is a one-line ∧-elimination proof. The burden moves to proving that the Rust checker refines `denote` (DRT plus Verus). Biscuit-style Datalog blocks need an extra side condition: facts from block i are not visible to authority checks unless explicitly trusted (scope), else a later block could add facts that satisfy an earlier check. Prove `scope_isolation`. Use cedar-policy-symcc checkImplies (SymCC soundness is proved in Lean) to gate policy diffs in CI.
overclaim_risk: Monotonicity of the set does not prevent confused deputy if the deputy merges authority from several tokens.
underclaim_risk: It is trivially provable once caveats are conjunctive. Do not design caveats that can widen, such as disjunctive blocks.

verify.note: verifier sampled other nodes; explorer grade kept

correction: r3 counterexample: Tenuo 0.3.3 (cel feature) leaf-only evaluation + syntactic subsumption checker accepts widening children (r3e05.tenuo-cel-attenuation-bypass, A). Golden form: evaluate the conjunction of every caveat in the chain; monotonicity is then List.all_append (r3e05.l5-token-wire-format-lean).

title: rustls 0.23.46 defaults prefer X25519MLKEM768: rustls-based DB drivers offer PQ-hybrid with no driver changes
summary: rustls 0.23.46 (2026-10-14) default features [aws_lc_rs, logging, prefer-post-quantum, std, tls12]; manual says X25519MLKEM768 is highest-priority by default with aws-lc-rs. Drivers with rustls paths: mysql_async, sqlx, tiberius, mongodb, redis, fred, scylla, opensearch, aws-sdk-*, object_store, rust-s3, rskafka, async-nats, reqwest, tonic. Caller-supplied rustls::ClientConfig hooks seen (GitHub code search, partial due to rate limit) in redis-rs, scylla, async-nats, rskafka, aws-smithy-http-client. Not inherited: rdkafka (librdkafka OpenSSL), foundationdb (libfdb_c).
specifics: Whether the session is actually PQ depends on the DB server TLS stack (OpenSSL 3.5+/Go 1.24+/JDK) — not verified per server here (seed). Cargo feature unification means one top-level rustls feature choice governs all drivers.

title: Dependency update cooldown (no native Cargo support)
summary: Neither Cargo nor crates.io has a native minimum-release-age as of 2026-10-24 (searched CHANGELOG/unstable.md). Dependabot supports cooldown {default-days, semver-major/minor/patch-days}, security updates bypass it (shipped Jul 2025); Renovate has minimumReleaseAge. Evidence for: arrayref malicious versions lived 86-107 min; tokio 1.54.0 was yanked ~2 days after release (RUSTSEC-2026-0384/CVE-2026-115567; 1.54.1 on 2026-10-21 = what my lock resolved). Evidence against blanket cooldown: advisories arrive ~45-55/month and security fixes must bypass.
overclaim_risk: Cooldown only protects against fast-detected compromises; a long-dwell compromise (xz: ~2 years) is unaffected.
underclaim_risk: Costs almost nothing for a solo dev with --locked.
specifics: dependabot.yml: package-ecosystem: cargo, cooldown: {default-days: 7, semver-patch-days: 3}, security PRs bypass automatically; human merge only; CI `cargo vet`. Pass: no Cargo.lock change lands < 72h after the crate version publish date (script queries crates.io API created_at) unless labeled security-advisory.

verify.note: HEADLINE REFUTED: Cargo RFC 3923 min-publish-age accepted, implemented (cargo PR #17012, -Zmin-publish-age), stabilized (PR #17335, tracking #17009 closed 2026-08-28), targeting Rust 1.100 (~mid-Nov 2026). Third-party cooldown proxies exist.

correction: r3 executed: native cargo cooldown exists (stable in 1.100.0); a blanket 14-day window on the golden lock resolved rustls 0.23.45 and 6 advisories and broke exact pins. Policy: 7 days + audited security-advisory bypass (sc3.l5-cooldown-security-bypass).

title: rustls 0.23.46 (2026-10-14): 4 advisories incl. silent PQ downgrade via key-share prediction poisoning
summary: RUSTSEC-2026-0349 / GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28 (low 3.7): unauthenticated ServerHello selecting X25519 poisons per-server-name key-share record; later ClientHellos send only X25519 share even though X25519MLKEM768 first in supported_groups; if server accepts without HelloRetryRequest, handshake completes classical-only => HNDL exposure; mitigation: server HRR for preferred group, resumption store off. Also 0346 session Debug leaks TLS secrets (medium), 0347 ECH rejection leaks buffered app data to outer server, 0348 brotli cert decompress 1GiB pre-auth. Also 0.23.45 (09-14) GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc accepted handshake msgs across encryption levels. Related draft-ietf-tls-key-share-prediction.
specifics: L5: server config must send HRR when client key_share lacks preferred hybrid group (policy: require X25519MLKEM768, never accept X25519-only for PQ-required listeners); test: downgrade-injection harness; rustls >=0.23.46 pin; disable brotli cert compression; no Debug on session types in logs (lint).
overclaim_risk: Low severity per CVSS; client-side only in rustls (our server is server-side) - our exposure is for outbound clients/upstream mTLS.
underclaim_risk: CVSS 3.7 hides that it silently strips the whole PQ property.
correction: r3 server-side verdicts executed (r3pq.hrr-acceptance-test): the default 0.23.46 server follows client group order, so an X25519-first client negotiates classical; pq-required kx_groups=[X25519MLKEM768] yields HRR 0x11EC or alert 40.

title: L5: adapter isolation rule: in-process feature-gated for pure-Rust drivers; out-of-process for C-binding and third-party adapters
summary: Rule: an adapter runs in-process (Cargo feature, zero code when unused) only if its driver is pure Rust, <=~15 unsafe sites at HEAD, has no C/C++ client library, and is first-party in the golden. Otherwise it runs out-of-process (separate binary, seccomp+Landlock, IPC carrying the WIT-encoded Op; or a Wasm component when the driver compiles to wasm32-wasip2 with sockets).
specifics:
Measured inputs (HEAD clones 2026-10-24, regex unsafe{|fn|impl, non-test): IN-PROCESS eligible: tokio-postgres 1/23.1k, mysql_async 4/14.9k, redis 6/49.3k, scylla 3/93.9k, async-nats 9/40.2k, mongodb 14/91.7k, tiberius 6/40k, neo4rs 6/31.9k (but stale), rskafka 0, object_store 2/38.7k, rust-s3 0 (forbid), qdrant-client 0, opensearch 0, meilisearch-sdk 0. OUT-OF-PROCESS required: libsql (831 + ~1.43M C/C++), foundationdb (120 + libfdb_c C++), rdkafka (335 + librdkafka C), questdb-rs (1508 + 39.9k C). TCB cost: in-process adds the driver's full LOC to the core TCB (e.g. mongodb 91.7k, scylla 93.9k) and its TLS stack; out-of-process adds an IPC codec (~1-2k LOC est.) + per-op IPC latency (UNMEASURED: implementation spike). 
Which invariants survive a malicious/buggy adapter (third-party contract): only those enforced NATIVELY with credentials the core mints per tenant and hands to the adapter: PG/CRDB/YSQL/SQL Server RLS role or session; DynamoDB/S3 per-tenant STS session policy; Redis per-tenant ACL user (key pattern t:<tenant>:*, -@scripting -@dangerous); Kafka per-tenant principal with PREFIXED ACL; NATS per-tenant account/user JWT; FDB tenant JWT (experimental). For PEP-only families (MySQL, TiDB, Mongo, Cassandra/Scylla, Neo4j Community, Qdrant, Meili, Influx, libSQL) the adapter is inside the trust boundary: third-party adapters for these families cannot get core-guaranteed tenant isolation, which should be stated in the extension contract.
PQ: rustls 0.23.46 default features include prefer-post-quantum + aws_lc_rs, so all rustls-based drivers offer X25519MLKEM768 first by default; C-stack adapters (librdkafka, libfdb_c) do not inherit this, which is another reason to put them out-of-process with a separately audited TLS config.
overclaim_risk: unsafe-site regex counts are a proxy; the ~15-site threshold is a judgment call; IPC overhead unmeasured.
underclaim_risk: Out-of-process adapters also give crash isolation (a C-driver segfault cannot take down ingress).

verify.note: verifier sampled other nodes; explorer grade kept

correction: r3: out-of-process hop measured 4.8 us (UDS) / 2.1 us (futex ring) per call on one pinned laptop core vs 0.02-0.05 us in process; placement by unsafe/C-binding count first, hop budget second (w02.L5-adapter-oop-threshold-table, C).
